9961 — Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ (may Allah be pleased with him) said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited me during the Farewell Pilgrimage while I was suffering from an illness that had brought me close to death.
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, you see the severity of my illness. I possess wealth, and only one daughter will inherit from me. May I give two-thirds of my wealth in charity?”
He replied:
“No.”
I asked:
“Then half?”
He said:
“No. One-third, and even one-third is much. It is better to leave your heirs wealthy than to leave them poor and dependent upon people. You will not spend anything seeking the Face of Allah except that you will be rewarded for it—even the morsel of food that you place into your wife’s mouth.”
I then asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, will I remain behind after my companions?”
He replied:
“You will not remain behind and perform any deed seeking the Face of Allah except that it will increase you in rank and honor. Perhaps you will live on so that through you some people will benefit and others will be harmed. O Allah, complete the migration of my Companions and do not cause them to turn back on their heels. But pitiable is Saʿd ibn Khawlah.”
Saʿd explained:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ expressed sorrow because Saʿd ibn Khawlah had died in Makkah.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3936) and Muslim (1628, no. 5).
The Prophet’s ﷺ statement,
“Perhaps you will live on so that through you some people will benefit…”
meant that Saʿd would not die from this illness, but would live for many years thereafter. He later led the Muslim conquest of Iraq and other lands. Through him, the Muslims greatly benefited, while the disbelievers were defeated, most notably at the Battle of al-Qādisiyyah during the caliphate of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.

“Yes. But perhaps Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will raise your rank, and through you He will harm some people and benefit others.”

٩٩٦٤ — عن جابر بن سمرة قال: شكا أهل الكوفة سعدًا إلى عمر، فعزله واستعمل عليهم عمارًا، فشكوا حتى ذكروا أنه لا يحسن يصلي، فأرسل إليه، فقال: يا أبا إسحاق، إن هؤلاء يزعمون أنك لا تحسن تصلي؟
قال أبو إسحاق: أما أنا والله، فإني كنت أصلي بهم صلاة رسول الله ﷺ ما أخرم عنها، أصلي صلاة العشاء، فأركد في الأوليين، وأخف في الأخريين.
قال: ذاك الظن بك يا أبا إسحاق.
فأرسل معه رجلًا أو رجالًا إلى الكوفة، فسأل عنه أهل الكوفة، ولم يدع مسجدًا إلا سأل عنه، ويثنون عليه معروفًا، حتى دخل مسجدًا لبني عبس، فقام رجل منهم يقال له: أسامة بن قتادة، يكنى أبا سَعْدة، فقال: أما إذ نشدتنا، فإن سعدًا كان لا يسير بالسرية، ولا يقسم بالسوية، ولا يعدل في القضية.
قال سعد: أما والله، لأدعون بثلاث: اللهم إن كان عبدك هذا كاذبًا، قام رياءً وسمعةً، فأطل عمره، وأطل فقره، وعرِّضه للفتن.
وكان بعدُ إذا سئل يقول: شيخ كبير مفتون، أصابتني دعوة سعد.
قال عبد الملك: فأنا رأيته بعد، قد سقط حاجباه على عينيه من الكبر، وإنه ليتعرض للجواري في الطرق يغمزهن.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٥٥)، ومسلم (٤٥٣).

9964 — Jābir ibn Samurah (may Allah be pleased with him) said:
The people of Kūfah complained about Saʿd to ʿUmar. As a result, ʿUmar removed him from office and appointed ʿAmmār as governor over them.
They continued making complaints until they even claimed that Saʿd did not know how to lead the prayer properly.
ʿUmar summoned him and said:
“O Abū Isḥāq, these people claim that you do not perform the prayer correctly.”
Abū Isḥāq (Saʿd) replied:
“By Allah, I used to lead them exactly as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed, without falling short in any way. I would prolong the first two rakʿahs of the ʿIshāʾ prayer and shorten the last two.”
ʿUmar said:
“That is exactly what I expected of you, O Abū Isḥāq.”
He then sent one man—or several men—with Saʿd to Kūfah to investigate.
They visited every mosque in the city, asking the people about him, and everywhere they went the people praised him.
Finally they entered a mosque belonging to Banū ʿAbs.
A man named Usāmah ibn Qatādah, whose kunyah was Abū Saʿdah, stood up and said:
“Since you have placed us under oath, I will speak. Saʿd did not personally accompany military expeditions, he did not distribute wealth equally, and he was not just in his judgments.”
Saʿd then said:
“By Allah, I shall supplicate with three prayers:
O Allah, if this servant of Yours is lying and has spoken only for showing off and seeking fame, then prolong his life, prolong his poverty, and expose him to trials.”
Afterward, whenever that man was asked about his condition, he would say:
“I am an old man afflicted by trials. The supplication of Saʿd has overtaken me.”
ʿAbd al-Malik said:
I later saw him myself. His eyebrows had drooped over his eyes from extreme old age, yet he still exposed himself to temptation by pursuing young women in the streets and winking at them.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (755) and Muslim (453).

٩٩٦٥ — عن عامر بن سعد أن سعدًا ركب إلى قصره بالعقيق، فوجد عبدًا يقطع شجرًا أو يخبطه، فسلبه، فلما رجع سعد جاءه أهل العبد، فكلموه أن يرد على غلامهم أو عليهم ما أخذ من غلامهم، فقال: معاذ الله أن أرد شيئًا نفَّلنيه رسول الله ﷺ، وأبى أن يرد عليهم.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٣٦٤).

9965 — ʿĀmir ibn Saʿd narrated that Saʿd rode to his residence at al-ʿAqīq, where he found a slave cutting trees—or striking them to knock off their leaves.
Saʿd confiscated what the slave had with him.
When Saʿd returned, the slave’s family came to him and asked him to return to their servant—or to them—what he had taken.
Saʿd replied:
“Allah forbid that I should return something which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ granted to me as lawful spoils.”
He refused to return it to them.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1364).

٩٩٦٦ — عن جابر قال: كنا جلوسًا عند النبي ﷺ، فأقبل سعد بن أبي وقاص، فقال النبي ﷺ: ((هذا خالي، فليرني امرؤ خاله)).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٣٧٥٢)، والحاكم (٣/٤٩٨).
قال الترمذي: “وكان سعد بن أبي وقاص من بني زهرة، وكانت أم النبي ﷺ من بني زهرة، فلذلك قال النبي ﷺ: ((هذا خالي)).”

9966 — Jābir (may Allah be pleased with him) said:
We were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ approached.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“This is my maternal uncle. Let each person show me his maternal uncle!”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3752) and al-Ḥākim (3/498).
Al-Tirmidhī said:
“Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ belonged to Banū Zuhrah, and the Prophet’s ﷺ mother also belonged to Banū Zuhrah. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘This is my maternal uncle.’”

arabic_source:
٩٩٦٨ — عن أنس أنه قال: قدم علينا عبد الرحمن بن عوف، وآخى رسول الله ﷺ بينه وبين سعد بن الربيع، وكان كثير المال، فقال سعد: قد علمت الأنصار أني من أكثرها مالًا، سأقسم مالي بيني وبينك شطرين، ولي امرأتان، فانظر أعجبهما إليك فأطلقها، حتى إذا حلت تزوجتها.
فقال عبد الرحمن: بارك الله لك في أهلك ومالك.
فلم يرجع يومئذ حتى أفضل شيئًا من سمن وأقط. فلم يلبث إلا يسيرًا حتى جاء رسول الله ﷺ وعليه وضر من صفرة، فقال له رسول الله ﷺ: ((مهيم؟))
قال: تزوجت امرأة من الأنصار.
فقال: ((ما سقت إليها؟)) قال: وزن نواة من ذهب - أو نواة من ذهب.
فقال: ((أولم ولو بشاة)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٧٨١)، ومسلم (١٤٢٧/٨١).

english_source:
9968 — Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) said:
When ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf arrived in Madinah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established a bond of brotherhood between him and Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ.
Saʿd was a man of great wealth and said:
“The Anṣār know that I am among the wealthiest of them. I will divide my wealth equally between you and me. I also have two wives; look to see which one pleases you most, and I will divorce her so that, after her waiting period is complete, you may marry her.”
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān replied:
“May Allah bless your family and your wealth.”
That very day, he went to the marketplace and returned having earned some clarified butter and dried yogurt.
Not long afterward, he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with traces of yellow perfume upon him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“What is the matter?”
He replied:
“I have married a woman from the Anṣār.”
The Prophet ﷺ asked:
“What did you give her as her bridal gift (mahr)?”
He replied:
“The weight of a date-stone of gold.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Hold a wedding feast, even if only with one sheep.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3781) and Muslim (1427, no. 81).

٩٩٦٩ — عن المغيرة بن شعبة قال في قصة: فانتهينا إلى القوم وقد قاموا في الصلاة، يصلي بهم عبد الرحمن بن عوف، وقد ركع بهم ركعة، فلما أحس بالنبي ﷺ ذهب يتأخر، فأومأ إليه، فلما سلم قام النبي ﷺ وقمت، فركعنا الركعة التي سبقتنا.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٧٤/٨١).

english_source:
9969 — Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah (may Allah be pleased with him) said:
We came to the people while they had already begun the prayer. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf was leading them, and they had already completed one rakʿah.
When he realized that the Prophet ﷺ had arrived, he tried to step back, but the Prophet ﷺ motioned for him to remain where he was.
After ʿAbd al-Raḥmān concluded the prayer with salām, the Prophet ﷺ and I stood and performed the rakʿah that we had missed.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (274, no. 81).

9970 — ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came while he was leading the people in prayer.
He attempted to step back, but the Prophet ﷺ signaled to him:
“Remain where you are.”
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ completed the prayer behind ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Ṭayālisī (223), al-Bazzār (1014), Abū Yaʿlā (853), and al-Shāshī in his Musnad (246).

9971 — Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her) said:
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf came to her and said:
“O my mother, I fear that the abundance of my wealth may destroy me. I am the wealthiest man among Quraysh.”
She replied:
“My son, spend generously, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
‘Among my Companions are those who will not see me after I depart from them.’”
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān then left and met ʿUmar, informing him of what Umm Salamah had said.
ʿUmar came to her and asked:
“By Allah, am I one of them?”
She replied:
“No, and I will not declare anyone else free from that after you.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (26489), al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (2496), and Abū Yaʿlā (7003).

٩٩٧٢ — عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف، عن عائشة أن رسول الله ﷺ كان يقول: ((إن أمركنَّ مما يهمني بعدي، ولن يصبر عليكن إلا الصابرون)).
قال: ثم تقول عائشة: فسقى الله أباك من سلسبيل الجنة، تريد عبد الرحمن بن عوف، وقد كان وصل أزواج النبي ﷺ بمال، يقال: بيعت بأربعين ألفًا.
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٣٧٤٩)، وأحمد (٢٤٤٨٥)، وصححه ابن حبان (٦٩٩٥)، والحاكم (٣/٣١٢).
وقوله: ((إن أمركنَّ مما يهمني بعدي)) يعني أمر أزواجه، فقد دخل على إحدى عشرة امرأة، ماتت منهن عنده ﷺ خديجة بنت خويلد، وزينب بنت خزيمة أم المساكين، ومات هو عن سائرهن.
وكان عبد الرحمن بن عوف ممن اهتم بأمور أمهات المؤمنين بعد النبي ﷺ، فأوصى بحديقة لأمهات المؤمنين، بيعت بأربعين ألفًا أو أربع مائة ألف كما عند الترمذي (٣٧٥٠).

9972 — Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf narrated from ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say to his wives:
“Your welfare is one of the matters that concerns me after my death, and none will treat you with patience and care except those who are truly patient.”
Thereafter, ʿĀʾishah would say:
“May Allah give your father to drink from the Salsabīl spring of Paradise,”
referring to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, because he had provided financial support to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. It is said that the property he gave them was sold for forty thousand.
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3749), Aḥmad (24485), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (6995) and al-Ḥākim (3/312).
The Prophet’s ﷺ statement,
“Your welfare is one of the matters that concerns me after my death,”
refers to the affairs of his wives.
The Prophet ﷺ married eleven women. During his lifetime, Khadījah bint Khuwaylid and Zaynab bint Khuzaymah (Umm al-Masākīn) passed away, while he passed away leaving the remainder of his wives alive.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf was among those who took special care of the Mothers of the Believers after the Prophet ﷺ. He bequeathed an orchard to them, which was later sold for forty thousand—or four hundred thousand, according to another narration recorded by al-Tirmidhī (3750).

٩٩٧٣ — عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال: كاتبتُ أميَّة بن خلف كتابًا أن يحفظني في صاغيتي بمكة، وأحفظه في صاغيته بالمدينة. فلما كتبتُ: عبد الرحمن، قال: لا أعرف الرحمن، كاتبني باسمك الذي كان في الجاهلية. فكاتبته: عبد عمرو.
قال: وكان في يوم بدر خرجتُ إلى جبل لأحرزه حين نام الناس، فأبصره بلال، فخرج عني، فوقف على مجلس من الأنصار، فقال: أمية بن خلف، لا نجوتُ إن نجا أمية.
فخرج معه فريق من الأنصار في أثري، فلما خشيت أن يلحقونا خلفت لهم ابنه ليشغلهم، فقتلوه، ثم أبوا حتى يتبعونا. وكان رجلًا ثقيلًا، فلما أدركونا قلت له: ابرك. فبرك، فألقيت نفسي عليه لأمنعه، فتخللوه بالسيوف من تحتي حتى قتلوه، وأصاب أحدهم رجلي بسيفه.
وكان عبد الرحمن بن عوف يرينا ذلك الأثر في ظهر قدمه.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٣٠١).

9973 — ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf (may Allah be pleased with him) said:
I entered into a written agreement with Umayyah ibn Khalaf: he would protect my property in Makkah, and I would protect his property in Madinah.
When I wrote my name as ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, he said:
“I do not recognize ‘al-Raḥmān.’ Write to me using the name you had during the pre-Islamic period.”
So I wrote ʿAbd ʿAmr.
On the Day of Badr, when the people had gone to sleep, I went with Umayyah toward a mountain to keep him safe.
Bilāl saw him and cried out:
“Umayyah ibn Khalaf! May I not survive if Umayyah survives!”
He then called a group of the Anṣār, and they pursued us.
When I feared they would catch us, I left Umayyah’s son behind for them in hopes of delaying them, but they killed him and continued after us.
Umayyah was a heavy man.
When they caught up to us, I said to him:
“Kneel down.”
He knelt, and I threw myself over him in an attempt to shield him.
However, they thrust their swords beneath me until they killed him.
One of their swords struck my foot, leaving a scar.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf used to show us that scar on the top of his foot.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2301).

٩٩٧٣ — عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال: كاتبتُ أميَّة بن خلف كتابًا أن يحفظني في صاغيتي بمكة، وأحفظه في صاغيته بالمدينة. فلما كتبتُ: عبد الرحمن، قال: لا أعرف الرحمن، كاتبني باسمك الذي كان في الجاهلية. فكاتبته: عبد عمرو.
قال: وكان في يوم بدر خرجتُ إلى جبل لأحرزه حين نام الناس، فأبصره بلال، فخرج عني، فوقف على مجلس من الأنصار، فقال: أمية بن خلف، لا نجوتُ إن نجا أمية.
فخرج معه فريق من الأنصار في أثري، فلما خشيت أن يلحقونا خلفت لهم ابنه ليشغلهم، فقتلوه، ثم أبوا حتى يتبعونا. وكان رجلًا ثقيلًا، فلما أدركونا قلت له: ابرك. فبرك، فألقيت نفسي عليه لأمنعه، فتخللوه بالسيوف من تحتي حتى قتلوه، وأصاب أحدهم رجلي بسيفه.
وكان عبد الرحمن بن عوف يرينا ذلك الأثر في ظهر قدمه.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٣٠١).

٩٩٧٤ — عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((إن لكل أمة أمينًا، وإن أميننا أيتها الأمة أبو عبيدة بن الجراح)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٧٤٤)، ومسلم (٢٤١٩/٥٣).
وفي لفظ: “إن أهل اليمن قدموا على رسول الله ﷺ فقالوا: ابعث معنا رجلًا يعلمنا السنة والإسلام. قال: فأخذ بيد أبي عبيدة، فقال: ((هذا أمين هذه الأمة)).” رواه مسلم (٢٤١٩/٥٤).

9974 — Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Every nation has a trustworthy guardian, and the trustworthy guardian of this nation is Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3744) and Muslim (2419, no. 53).
Another narration states:
The people of Yemen came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
“Send with us a man who will teach us the Sunnah and Islam.”
The Prophet ﷺ took Abū ʿUbaydah by the hand and said:
“This is the trustworthy guardian of this nation.”
Recorded by Muslim (2419, no. 54).

٩٩٧٥ — عن حذيفة قال: جاء أهل نجران إلى النبي ﷺ فقالوا: ابعث لنا رجلًا أمينًا. فقال: ((لأبعثن إليكم رجلًا أمينًا حق أمين)). فاستشرف له الناس، فبعث أبا عبيدة بن الجراح.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٣٨١)، ومسلم (٢٤٢٠/٥٥).
وفي لفظ من وجه آخر عند البخاري (٤٣٨٠): “جاء العاقب والسيد صاحبا نجران إلى رسول الله ﷺ يريدان أن يلاعناه، فقال أحدهما لصاحبه: لا تفعل؛ فوالله إن كان نبيًا فلاعناه لا نفلح نحن ولا عقبنا من بعدنا. فقالا: إنا نعطيك ما سألتنا، وابعث معنا رجلًا أمينًا، ولا تبعث معنا إلا أمينًا. فقال: ((لأبعثن معكم رجلًا أمينًا حق أمين)). فاستشرف له أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: ((قم يا أبا عبيدة بن الجراح)). فلما قام قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((هذا أمين هذه الأمة)).

9975 — Ḥudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated:
The people of Najrān came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“Send us a trustworthy man.”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“I will certainly send you a man who is truly trustworthy.”
The people eagerly looked on to see whom he would choose.
He then sent Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4381) and Muslim (2420, no. 55).
Additional Wording
Another narration recorded by al-Bukhārī states:
The al-ʿĀqib and al-Sayyid, the two leaders of Najrān, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ intending to invoke mutual imprecation (mubāhalah).
One of them said to the other:
“Do not do it. By Allah, if he is truly a prophet and we invoke mutual imprecation against him, neither we nor our descendants after us will ever prosper.”
They then said:
“We will give you what you have asked of us. Send with us a trustworthy man, and send only one who is trustworthy.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“I will certainly send with you a man who is truly trustworthy.”
The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ eagerly hoped to be chosen.
Then he said:
“Stand up, O Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ.”
When he stood, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ declared:
“This is the trustworthy guardian of this nation.”

٩٩٧٨ — عن عبد الله بن شقيق قال: قلت لعائشة: أي أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ كان أحب إلى رسول الله؟ قالت: أبو بكر. قلت: ثم من؟ قالت: عمر. قلت: ثم من؟ قالت: ثم أبو عبيدة بن الجراح. قلت: ثم من؟ قال: فسكتت.
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٣٦٥٧)، وابن ماجه (١٠٢)، وأبو يعلى (٤٧٣٢).
ومن أخبار أبي عبيدة بن الجراح أن أبا بكر الصديق قال وقت وفاة رسول الله ﷺ بسقيفة بني ساعدة: “قد رضيت لكم أحد هذين الرجلين: عمر وأبا عبيدة”. وكان أبو بكر ولَّى أبا عبيدة بيت المال - يعني أموال المسلمين -.
ومن أخباره أن أبا بكر الصديق سيَّره على الشام أميرًا، فكان فتح أكثر الشام على يده، وتوفي في طاعون عمواس بالشام سنة ثماني عشرة، وله ثمان وخمسون سنة.

9978 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Shaqīq said:
I asked ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her):
“Which of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was most beloved to him?”
She replied:
“Abū Bakr.”
I asked:
“Then who?”
She said:
“ʿUmar.”
I asked:
“Then who?”
She replied:
“Then Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ.”
I asked:
“Then who?”
He said:
She remained silent.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3657), Ibn Mājah (102), and Abū Yaʿlā (4732).
Among the notable reports concerning Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ is that, at the gathering of Saqīfah Banī Sāʿidah following the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq said:
“I am pleased for you to choose either of these two men: ʿUmar or Abū ʿUbaydah.”
Abū Bakr also appointed Abū ʿUbaydah to oversee the Bayt al-Māl (the treasury of the Muslims).
Among his achievements was that Abū Bakr appointed him commander of the Muslim forces in Greater Syria (al-Shām). Through his leadership, most of Syria was conquered.
He passed away during the Plague of ʿAmwās in Syria in the year 18 AH, at the age of fifty-eight.

٩٩٧٩ — عن سعيد بن زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل يقول في مسجد الكوفة: والله لقد رأيتني وإن عمر لموثقي على الإسلام قبل أن يسلم عمر، ولو أن أحدًا ارفضَّ للذي صنعتم بعثمان لكان.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٨٦٢).
وفي لفظ: “لو رأيتني موثقي عمر على الإسلام أنا وأخته وما أسلم، ولو أن أحدًا انقضَّ لما صنعتم بعثمان لكان محقوقًا أن ينقض.” رواه البخاري (٣٨٦٧).

9979 — Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl (may Allah be pleased with him) said in the mosque of Kūfah:
“By Allah, I remember when ʿUmar had me bound because of my Islam before he himself embraced Islam. If Mount Uḥud had collapsed because of what you did to ʿUthmān, it would have been justified.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3862).
Another wording states:
“You should have seen me when ʿUmar had me and his sister bound because of Islam before he himself embraced Islam. If Mount Uḥud had collapsed because of what you did to ʿUthmān, it would indeed have been justified in collapsing.”
Recorded by al-Bukhārī (3867).

9980 — ʿUmar ibn Muḥammad narrated that his father narrated from Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl (may Allah be pleased with him):
A woman named Arwā disputed with him over a portion of his property.
Saʿīd said:
“Leave her and her claim, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
‘Whoever wrongfully takes even a handspan of land will be burdened with it from the depths of seven earths on the Day of Resurrection.’”
Then Saʿīd supplicated:
“O Allah, if she is lying, then take away her eyesight and make her grave within her own house.”
The narrator said:
Later I saw her blind, feeling her way along the walls, saying:
“The supplication of Saʿīd ibn Zayd has struck me.”
Then, while she was walking within her property, she passed by a well in the courtyard, fell into it, and it became her grave.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1610, no. 138).
Among the reports concerning Saʿīd ibn Zayd is that he was one of the earliest people to embrace Islam. He accepted Islam before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered Dār al-Arqam.
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb embraced Islam in Saʿīd’s house, because Saʿīd was married to ʿUmar’s sister, Fāṭimah.
Arwā mentioned in the narration was Arwā bint Uways.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said:
“Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Saʿd, Saʿīd, Ṭalḥah, al-Zubayr, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf all occupied the same position with the Prophet ﷺ: they stood before him in battle and behind him in prayer.”
This was mentioned by Ibn Ḥajar in al-Iṣābah.
Al-Wāqidī said:
Saʿīd died at al-ʿAqīq and was then carried to Madinah for burial. This occurred in 50 AH, though it has also been said 51 AH or 52 AH. He lived to be over seventy years of age.

٩٩٨١ — عن أبي حميد الساعدي أنهم قالوا: يا رسول الله، كيف نصلي عليك؟ فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((قولوا: اللهم صلِّ على محمد وأزواجه وذريته، كما صليت على آل إبراهيم، وبارك على محمد وأزواجه وذريته، كما باركت على آل إبراهيم، إنك حميد مجيد)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٣٦٩)، ومسلم (٤٠٧-٦٩).
قلت: وقد ورد عند الشيخين وغيرهما، كما سبق في الصلاة في موضعه: ((وعلى آل محمد)) مكان ((أزواجه وذريته))، فدل على أن الآل يشملهم.

9981 — Abū Ḥumayd al-Sāʿidī narrated that the Companions asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, how should we invoke Allah’s blessings upon you?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“Say: O Allah, bestow Your blessings upon Muḥammad, his wives, and his descendants, just as You bestowed Your blessings upon the family of Ibrāhīm. And bless Muḥammad, his wives, and his descendants, just as You blessed the family of Ibrāhīm. Indeed, You are the Praiseworthy, the Glorious.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3369) and Muslim (407, no. 69).
The author said:
The wording recorded by al-Bukhārī, Muslim, and others—as previously mentioned in the chapter on prayer—is:
“And upon the family of Muḥammad,”
in place of:
“His wives and descendants.”
This demonstrates that the term “family” includes his wives and descendants.

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٣٦٩)، ومسلم (٤٠٧-٦٩).
قلت: وقد ورد عند الشيخين وغيرهما، كما سبق في الصلاة في موضعه: ((وعلى آل محمد)) مكان ((أزواجه وذريته))، فدل على أن الآل يشملهم.
9981 — Abū Ḥumayd al-Sāʿidī narrated that the Companions asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, how should we invoke Allah’s blessings upon you?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“Say: O Allah, bestow Your blessings upon Muḥammad, his wives, and his descendants, just as You bestowed Your blessings upon the family of Ibrāhīm. And bless Muḥammad, his wives, and his descendants, just as You blessed the family of Ibrāhīm. Indeed, You are the Praiseworthy, the Glorious.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3369) and Muslim (407, no. 69).
The author said:
The wording recorded by al-Bukhārī, Muslim, and others—as previously mentioned in the chapter on prayer—is:
“And upon the family of Muḥammad,”
in place of:
“His wives and descendants.”
This demonstrates that the term “family” includes his wives and descendants.

٩٩٨٢ — عن زيد بن أرقم قال: قام رسول الله ﷺ يومًا فينا خطيبًا بماء يُدعى خُمًّا بين مكة والمدينة، فحمد الله وأثنى عليه، ووعظ وذكَّر، ثم قال: ((أما بعد، ألا أيها الناس، فإنما أنا بشر يوشك أن يأتي رسول ربي فأجيب، وأنا تارك فيكم ثقلين: أولهما كتاب الله، فيه الهدى والنور، فخذوا بكتاب الله واستمسكوا به)).
فحث على كتاب الله ورغَّب فيه، ثم قال: ((وأهل بيتي، أذكركم الله في أهل بيتي، أذكركم الله في أهل بيتي، أذكركم الله في أهل بيتي)).
فقال له حصين: ومن أهل بيته يا زيد؟ أليس نساؤه من أهل بيته؟ قال: نساؤه من أهل بيته، ولكن أهل بيته من حُرم الصدقة بعده. قال: ومن هم؟ قال: هم آل علي، وآل عقيل، وآل جعفر، وآل عباس. قال: كل هؤلاء حُرم الصدقة؟ قال: نعم.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤٠٨).
وليس في هذا الحديث الأمر بالتمسك بهدي أهل بيت النبي ﷺ، وإنما فيه وجوب مراعاتهم ومحبتهم واجتناب ما يسوءهم إذا كانوا متمسكين بالكتاب والسنة، وهذا الذي فهمه الصحابة، فقال أبو بكر الصديق: والذي نفسي بيده، لقرابة رسول الله ﷺ أحب إليَّ أن أصل من قرابتي. رواه البخاري (٣٧١٢).
وأما الأخذ بأقوالهم والاعتصام بأعمالهم مع كتاب الله، فلم يثبت فيه شيء.

9982 — Zayd ibn Arqam narrated:
One day, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us to deliver a sermon at a watering place called Khumm, situated between Makkah and Madinah.
He praised and extolled Allah, admonished us, and reminded us. He then said:
“To proceed: O people, I am only a human being. The messenger of my Lord may soon come to me, and I will answer his call. I am leaving among you two weighty things. The first of them is the Book of Allah, in which there is guidance and light. So hold firmly to the Book of Allah and adhere to it.”
He strongly encouraged them to adhere to the Book of Allah and urged them toward it.
Then he said:
“And the members of my household. I remind you of Allah regarding the members of my household. I remind you of Allah regarding the members of my household. I remind you of Allah regarding the members of my household.”
Ḥuṣayn asked Zayd:
“Who are the members of his household, O Zayd? Are his wives not among the members of his household?”
He replied:
“His wives are among the members of his household. However, the members of his household referred to here are those for whom charity remained forbidden after him.”
Ḥuṣayn asked:
“Who are they?”
He replied:
“They are the family of ʿAlī, the family of ʿAqīl, the family of Jaʿfar, and the family of al-ʿAbbās.”
He asked:
“Was charity forbidden to all of them?”
Zayd replied:
“Yes.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2408).
This hadith does not contain a command to adhere to the guidance of the Prophet’s household. Rather, it establishes the obligation of caring for them, loving them, and avoiding whatever would cause them harm, provided that they adhere to the Qur’an and Sunnah.
This is how the Companions understood it.
Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq said:
“By the One in whose hand is my soul, maintaining ties with the relatives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is more beloved to me than maintaining ties with my own relatives.”
Recorded by al-Bukhārī (3712).
As for the claim that their statements and actions must be adhered to alongside the Book of Allah, nothing authentic has been established concerning that.

٩٩٨٣ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((والذي نفسي بيده، لا يبغضنا أهل البيت رجل إلا أدخله الله النار)).
حسن: رواه ابن حبان (٦٩٧٨).

9983 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“By the One in whose hand is my soul, no man hates us, the People of the Household, except that Allah will admit him into the Fire.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Ḥibbān (6978).

٩٩٨٤ — عن علي بن ربيعة الأسدي الوالبي قال: لقيت زيد بن أرقم، وهو يريد الدخول على المختار، فقلت له: بلغني عنك حديث. قال: ما هو؟ قلت: أسمعت النبي ﷺ يقول: ((إني تارك فيكم الثقلين: كتاب الله عز وجل، وعترتي))؟ قال: نعم.
صحيح: رواه يعقوب الفسوي في المعرفة والتاريخ (١/٥٣٧)، والطبراني في الكبير (٥/٢١٠).
قوله: “عترتي” أي أهل بيتي.

9984 — ʿAlī ibn Rabīʿah al-Asadī al-Wālibī narrated:
I met Zayd ibn Arqam while he was intending to enter upon al-Mukhtār.
I said to him:
“A hadith has reached me from you.”
He asked:
“What is it?”
I said:
“Did you hear the Prophet ﷺ say: ‘I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and my close family’?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
Authentic: Narrated by Yaʿqūb al-Fasawī in al-Maʿrifah wa-al-Tārīkh (1/537) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (5/210).
His statement “my close family” means: the members of my household.

صحيح: رواه يعقوب الفسوي في المعرفة والتاريخ (١/٥٣٧)، والطبراني في الكبير (٥/٢١٠).
قوله: “عترتي” أي أهل بيتي.

english_source:
9985 — Yazīd ibn Ḥayyān narrated from Zayd ibn Arqam:
We entered upon him and said:
“You have witnessed much good. You accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and prayed behind him.”
He then related the hadith with wording similar to that of Abū Ḥayyān, except that he said that the Prophet ﷺ stated:
“Indeed, I am leaving among you two weighty things. One of them is the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is the rope of Allah. Whoever follows it will remain upon guidance, and whoever abandons it will be upon misguidance.”
The narration also states:
We asked:
“Who are the members of his household? Are they his wives?”
Zayd replied:
“No, by Allah. A woman may remain with a man for a long period of time, and then he may divorce her, whereupon she returns to her father and her people. The members of his household are his blood relatives and paternal kin, for whom charity was forbidden after him.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2407).
His statement:
“It is the rope of Allah,”
means that it is the means that leads to His pleasure and mercy.
It has also been said that it refers to His light by which He guides, and it has been said that it refers to His covenant.

٩٩٨٦ — عن عبد الله بن عمر أن النبي ﷺ قال: ((أُريت في المنام أني أنزع بدلو بكرة على قليب، فجاء أبو بكر فنزع ذَنوبًا أو ذَنوبين نزعًا ضعيفًا، والله يغفر له، ثم جاء عمر بن الخطاب فاستحالت غربًا، فلم أر عبقريًّا يفري فريَّه، حتى روي الناس وضربوا بعطن)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٦٨٢)، ومسلم (٢٣٩٣).
وفي لفظ للبخاري: “رأيت الناس مجتمعين في صعيد… وفي بعض نزعه ضعف”. رواه البخاري (٣٦٣٣).

english_source:
9986 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said:
“I was shown in a dream that I was drawing water from a well with a bucket attached to a pulley. Abū Bakr came and drew one or two buckets, and there was some weakness in his drawing—may Allah forgive him. Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb came, and the bucket transformed into a large one. I have never seen a remarkably strong man perform as he did, until the people had drunk their fill and brought their camels to their resting places.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3682) and Muslim (2393).
Another wording recorded by al-Bukhārī states:
“I saw the people gathered upon an open plain…”
It also states:
“There was some weakness in his drawing.”
Recorded by al-Bukhārī (3633).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٦٦٤)، ومسلم (٢٣٩٢-١٧).

9987 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
“While I was sleeping, I saw myself beside a well with a bucket upon it. I drew from it for as long as Allah willed. Then the son of Abū Quḥāfah took it and drew one or two buckets, and there was some weakness in his drawing—may Allah forgive his weakness. Then it transformed into a large bucket, and Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb took it. I have never seen any remarkably strong man draw water as ʿUmar did, until the people brought their camels to their resting places.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3664) and Muslim (2392, no. 17).

٩٩٨٩ — عن ابن عباس قال: وُضع عمر بن الخطاب على سريره، فتكنفه الناس يدعون ويثنون ويصلون عليه قبل أن يُرفع، وأنا فيهم. قال: فلم يرعني إلا برجل قد أخذ بمنكبي من ورائي، فالتفت إليه فإذا هو علي، فترحم على عمر وقال: ما خلَّفت أحدًا أحب إليَّ أن ألقى الله بمثل عمله منك، وأيم الله، إن كنت لأظن أن يجعلك الله مع صاحبيك، وذاك أني كنت كثيرًا أسمع رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((جئت أنا وأبو بكر وعمر، ودخلت أنا وأبو بكر وعمر، وخرجت أنا وأبو بكر وعمر)). فإن كنت لأرجو، أو لأظن، أن يجعلك الله معهما.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٦٨٥)، ومسلم (٢٣٨٩).
وفي لفظ للبخاري (٣٦٧٧): “إذا رجل من خلفي وضع مرفقه على منكبي يقول: رحمك الله”.

english_source:
9989 — Ibn ʿAbbās narrated:
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was placed upon his bier, and the people gathered around him, supplicating for him, praising him, and invoking blessings upon him before he was carried away. I was among them.
Suddenly, a man placed his hand upon my shoulder from behind. I turned and saw that it was ʿAlī.
He prayed for mercy upon ʿUmar and said:
“You have left behind no one whose deeds I would more dearly wish to meet Allah with than yours. By Allah, I have always believed that Allah would join you with your two companions, for I frequently heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: ‘I came with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; I entered with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; and I went out with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.’ Therefore, I used to hope—or believe—that Allah would join you with them.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3685) and Muslim (2389).
Another wording recorded by al-Bukhārī states:
“Suddenly, a man behind me placed his forearm upon my shoulder and said: ‘May Allah have mercy upon you.’”
Recorded by al-Bukhārī (3677).

٩٩٩٠ — عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((بينما رجل يسوق بقرة له قد حمل عليها، التفتت إليه البقرة فقالت: إني لم أُخلق لهذا، ولكني إنما خُلقت للحرث)). فقال الناس: سبحان الله! تعجبًا وفزعًا، أبقرة تتكلم؟ فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((فإني أؤمن به، وأبو بكر وعمر)).
قال أبو هريرة: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((بينا راع في غنمه، عدا عليه الذئب فأخذ منها شاة، فطلبه الراعي حتى استنقذها منه، فالتفت إليه الذئب فقال له: من لها يوم السبع، يوم ليس لها راع غيري؟)). فقال الناس: سبحان الله! فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((فإني أؤمن بذلك، أنا وأبو بكر وعمر)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٦٦٣)، ومسلم (٢٣٨٨-١٣).

9990 — Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“While a man was driving a cow upon which he had placed a load, the cow turned toward him and said: ‘I was not created for this. I was created only for plowing.’”
The people exclaimed:
“Glory be to Allah!”
They were amazed and alarmed, saying:
“A cow speaks?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“I believe it, and so do Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.”
Abū Hurayrah also narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“While a shepherd was tending his sheep, a wolf attacked and seized one of them. The shepherd pursued it until he rescued the sheep from it. The wolf then turned toward him and said: ‘Who will care for it on the Day of the Beast, when it will have no shepherd other than me?’”
The people exclaimed:
“Glory be to Allah!”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“I believe that, and so do Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3663) and Muslim (2388, no. 13).

9991 — Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah narrated:
I asked my father, ʿAlī:
“Who is the best of people after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?”
He replied:
“Abū Bakr.”
I asked:
“Then who?”
He replied:
“Then ʿUmar.”
I feared that he would next say ʿUthmān, so I asked:

٩٩٩٥ — عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: إني لجالس مع رسول الله ﷺ ليس معنا أحد من البشر، إذ أقبل أبو بكر وعمر رضي الله عنهما يمشيان، كل واحد منهما آخذ بيد صاحبه، فقال ﷺ: ((هذان سيدا كهول أهل الجنة من الأولين والآخرين إلا النبيين والمرسلين، لا تخبرهما يا علي)). فما أخبرتهما، ولو كانا حيين ما حدثت به.
حسن: رواه الدولابي في الكنى (٢/٩٩).

٩٩٩٦ — عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: أمرنا رسول الله ﷺ يومًا أن نتصدق، فوافق ذلك مالًا عندي، فقلت: اليوم أسبق أبا بكر إن سبقته يومًا. فجئت بنصف مالي، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((ما أبقيت لأهلك؟)). فقلت: مثله. قال: وأتى أبو بكر بكل ما عنده، فقال له رسول الله ﷺ: ((ما أبقيت لأهلك؟)). قال: أبقيت لهم الله ورسوله. قلت: لا أسابقك إلى شيء أبدًا.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (١٦٧٨)، والترمذي (٣٦٧٥)، وقال الترمذي: “حسن صحيح”.

9996 — ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb narrated:
One day, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to give charity. At that time, I happened to possess some wealth, so I said to myself:
“Today I will surpass Abū Bakr, if I am ever able to surpass him.”
I brought half of my wealth.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“What have you left for your family?”
I replied:
“An equal amount.”
Then Abū Bakr came with everything he possessed.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him:
“What have you left for your family?”
He replied:
“I have left Allah and His Messenger for them.”
I then said:
“I will never compete with you in anything again.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1678) and al-Tirmidhī (3675). Al-Tirmidhī said: “good authentic hadith.”

9998 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“The inhabitants of ʿIlliyyīn will be seen by those below them just as a brilliant star is seen upon the horizon of the sky. Abū Bakr and ʿUmar are indeed among them—and what excellent men they are.”
Good through supporting narrations: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (3987), al-Tirmidhī (3658), Ibn Mājah (96), and Aḥmad (11882, 11467).
The first part of the hadith is authentically established with the following wording:
“The people of Paradise will see the inhabitants of the lofty chambers above them just as you see a brilliant star disappearing on the eastern or western horizon, because of the difference in rank between them.”
They asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, are those the dwellings of the prophets, which no one else can attain?”
He replied:
“No. By the One in whose hand is my soul, they are men who believed in Allah and affirmed the messengers.”
Recorded by al-Bukhārī (3256) and Muslim (2831).

10001 — Anas narrated that the Prophet ﷺ ascended Mount Uḥud accompanied by Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān.
The mountain shook beneath them, so the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Be firm, Uḥud, for upon you are only a prophet, a truthful one, and two martyrs.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3675).
Another wording recorded by al-Bukhārī states:
“It shook beneath them, so he struck it with his foot and said: ‘Be firm, Uḥud…’”
Recorded by al-Bukhārī (3686).

١٠٠٠٢ — عن أبي موسى أنه توضأ في بيته ثم خرج، فقال: لألزمن رسول الله ﷺ، ولأكونن معه يومي هذا. قال: فجاء المسجد فسأل عن النبي ﷺ، فقالوا: خرج ووجَّه هاهنا. فخرجت على إثره أسأل عنه حتى دخل بئر أريس، فجلست عند الباب، وبابها من جريد، حتى قضى رسول الله ﷺ حاجته فتوضأ.
فقمت إليه، فإذا هو جالس على بئر أريس، وتوسط قُفَّها، وكشف عن ساقيه ودلاهما في البئر. فسلمت عليه، ثم انصرفت فجلست عند الباب، فقلت: لأكونن بواب رسول الله ﷺ اليوم.
فجاء أبو بكر فدفع الباب، فقلت: من هذا؟ فقال: أبو بكر. فقلت: على رسلك. ثم ذهبت فقلت: يا رسول الله، هذا أبو بكر يستأذن. فقال: ((ائذن له وبشره بالجنة)). فأقبلت حتى قلت لأبي بكر: ادخل، ورسول الله ﷺ يبشرك بالجنة.
فدخل أبو بكر فجلس عن يمين رسول الله ﷺ معه في القُفِّ، ودلى رجليه في البئر كما صنع النبي ﷺ، وكشف عن ساقيه.
ثم رجعت فجلست، وقد تركت أخي يتوضأ ويلحقني، فقلت: إن يرد الله بفلان خيرًا - يريد أخاه - يأت به. فإذا إنسان يحرك الباب، فقلت: من هذا؟ فقال: عمر بن الخطاب. فقلت: على رسلك. ثم جئت رسول الله ﷺ فسلمت عليه، فقلت: هذا عمر بن الخطاب يستأذن. فقال: ((ائذن له وبشره بالجنة)).

10002 — Abū Mūsā narrated:
I performed ablution in my house and then went out, saying to myself:
“I will remain close to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and spend this entire day with him.”
I went to the mosque and asked where the Prophet ﷺ was. The people said:
“He went out and headed in that direction.”
I followed his path, asking about him, until he entered the garden containing the Well of Arīs.
I sat at its gate, which was made of palm branches, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ relieved himself and performed ablution.
I then went to him and found him sitting upon the stone ledge surrounding the Well of Arīs. He sat in the middle of it, uncovered his lower legs, and let them hang into the well.
I greeted him and then returned to sit at the gate, saying:
“Today I will serve as the gatekeeper of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
Abū Bakr came and pushed the gate.
I asked:
“Who is it?”
He replied:
“Abū Bakr.”
I said:
“Wait there.”
I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, Abū Bakr is requesting permission to enter.”
He said:
“Admit him and give him the glad tidings of Paradise.”
I returned and said to Abū Bakr:
“Enter, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gives you the glad tidings of Paradise.”
Abū Bakr entered and sat to the Prophet’s right upon the stone ledge. He uncovered his lower legs and let them hang into the well, just as the Prophet ﷺ had done.
I then returned to my place. I had left my brother performing ablution, intending to join me, so I thought:
“Should Allah intend good for him, He will bring him here.”
Then someone moved the gate.
I asked:
“Who is it?”
He replied:
“ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.”
I said:
“Wait there.”
I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, greeted him, and said:
“ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb is requesting permission to enter.”
He said:
“Admit him and give him the glad tidings of Paradise.”
I returned and said:
“Enter, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gives you the glad tidings of Paradise.”
He entered and sat to the Prophet’s left upon the stone ledge, and he let his legs hang into the well.
I returned to the gate and again thought:
“Should Allah intend good for my brother, He will bring him here.”
Then someone came and moved the gate.
I asked:
“Who is it?”
He replied:
“ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān.”
I said:
“Wait there.”
I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him.
He said:
“Admit him and give him the glad tidings of Paradise, along with a trial that will afflict him.”
I returned and said:
“Enter, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gives you the glad tidings of Paradise, along with a trial that will afflict you.”
He entered and found that the stone ledge was full, so he sat facing them on the opposite side.
Sharīk said that Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib stated:
“I interpreted this as referring to their graves.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3647) and Muslim (2403, no. 29).

“Open the gate for him and give him the glad tidings of Paradise.”

“Open the gate for him and give him the glad tidings of Paradise, along with a trial that will befall him.”
It was ʿUthmān.
I informed him of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said.

“Allah is the One whose help is sought.”

١٠٠٠٤ — عن أبي موسى أن النبي ﷺ دخل حائطًا وأمرني بحفظ باب الحائط، فجاء رجل يستأذن، فقال: ((ائذن له وبشره بالجنة)). فإذا أبو بكر، ثم جاء آخر يستأذن، فقال: ((ائذن له وبشره بالجنة)). فإذا عمر، ثم جاء آخر يستأذن، فسكت هنيهة، ثم قال: ((ائذن له وبشره بالجنة على بلوى ستصيبه)). فإذا عثمان بن عفان.
قال حماد: وحدثنا عاصم الأحول وعلي بن الحكم سمعا أبا عثمان يحدث عن أبي موسى بنحوه، وزاد فيه عاصم: ((أن النبي ﷺ كان قاعدًا في مكان فيه ماء، قد انكشف عن ركبتيه أو ركبته، فلما دخل عثمان غطاها)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٦٩٥).
وفي لفظ للبخاري (٦٢١٦): “أنه كان مع النبي ﷺ في حائط من حيطان المدينة، وفي يد النبي ﷺ عود يضرب به بين الماء والطين، فجاء رجل يستفتح…” وفي آخره: “ثم استفتح رجل آخر، وكان متكئًا، فجلس، فقال: ((افتح وبشره بالجنة على بلوى تصيبه أو تكون)).”

10004 — Abū Mūsā narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ entered a garden and instructed me to guard its gate.
A man came requesting permission to enter.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Let him enter and give him the glad tidings of Paradise.”
It was Abū Bakr.
Then another man came requesting permission.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Let him enter and give him the glad tidings of Paradise.”
It was ʿUmar.
Then another man came requesting permission.
The Prophet ﷺ remained silent for a short while before saying:
“Let him enter and give him the glad tidings of Paradise together with a trial that will befall him.”
It was ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān.
Ḥammād said:
ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal and ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated to us that they heard Abū ʿUthmān narrating from Abū Mūsā a similar report.
ʿĀṣim added:
“The Prophet ﷺ was sitting in a place containing water, and his knees—or one of his knees—were uncovered. When ʿUthmān entered, he covered them.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3695).
Another wording recorded by al-Bukhārī states:
The Prophet ﷺ was in one of the gardens of Madinah holding a small stick with which he was striking the water and mud when a man came requesting permission to enter.
At the end of the narration it states:
“Then another man requested permission to enter. The Prophet ﷺ had been reclining, but he sat upright and said: ‘Open the gate for him and give him the glad tidings of Paradise together with a trial that will befall him.’”
Recorded by al-Bukhārī (6216).

١٠٠٠٥ — عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: خرج النبي ﷺ يومًا إلى حائط من حوائط المدينة لحاجته، وخرجت في إثره، فلما دخل الحائط جلست على بابه، وقلت: لأكونن اليوم بواب النبي ﷺ ولم يأمرني، فذهب النبي ﷺ وقضى حاجته، وجلس على قُفِّ البئر، فكشف عن ساقيه ودلاهما في البئر، فجاء أبو بكر يستأذن عليه ليدخل، فقلت: كما أنت حتى أستأذن لك، فوقف، فجئت إلى النبي ﷺ فقلت: يا نبي الله، أبو بكر يستأذن عليك، قال: ((ائذن له وبشره بالجنة)).
فدخل، فجاء عن يمين النبي ﷺ، فكشف عن ساقيه ودلاهما في البئر، فجاء عمر، فقلت: كما أنت حتى أستأذن لك، فقال النبي ﷺ: ((ائذن له وبشره بالجنة)). فجاء عن يسار النبي ﷺ، فكشف عن ساقيه فدلاهما في البئر، فامتلأ القُفُّ فلم يكن فيه مجلس.
ثم جاء عثمان، فقلت: كما أنت حتى أستأذن لك، فقال النبي ﷺ: ((ائذن له وبشره بالجنة معها بلاء يصيبه)). فدخل فلم يجد معهم مجلسًا، فتحول حتى جاء مقابلهم على شفة البئر، فكشف عن ساقيه ثم دلاهما في البئر.
فجعلت أتمنى أخي وأدعو الله أن يأتي.
قال ابن المسيب: فتأولت ذلك قبورهم، اجتمعت هاهنا، وانفرد عثمان.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٧٠٩٧).

10005 — Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī narrated:
One day the Prophet ﷺ went out to one of the gardens of Madinah to relieve himself, and I followed him.
When he entered the garden, I sat at its gate and said to myself:
“Today I will serve as the gatekeeper of the Prophet ﷺ,”
even though he had not instructed me to do so.
The Prophet ﷺ relieved himself and then sat upon the stone ledge surrounding the well. He uncovered his lower legs and let them hang into the well.
Abū Bakr then came seeking permission to enter.
I said:
“Please wait until I ask permission for you.”
He waited.
I went to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Prophet of Allah, Abū Bakr is asking permission to enter.”
He replied:
“Let him enter and give him the glad tidings of Paradise.”
Abū Bakr entered and sat on the Prophet’s right. He uncovered his lower legs and let them hang into the well.
Then ʿUmar came.
I said:
“Please wait until I ask permission for you.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Let him enter and give him the glad tidings of Paradise.”
He entered, sat on the Prophet’s left, uncovered his lower legs, and let them hang into the well until the stone ledge became completely occupied.
Then ʿUthmān came.
I said:
“Please wait until I ask permission for you.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Let him enter and give him the glad tidings of Paradise together with a trial that will befall him.”
He entered but found no place to sit with them, so he moved to the opposite edge of the well, uncovered his lower legs, and let them hang into the well.
Meanwhile, I continued hoping that my brother would arrive and kept praying to Allah that he would come.
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said:
“I interpreted this as symbolizing their graves: Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and the Prophet ﷺ would be buried together, while ʿUthmān would be buried separately.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7097).
The author’s statement regarding Abū Mūsā’s words:
“I will serve today as the Prophet’s gatekeeper, although he had not instructed me.”
may be understood to mean that Abū Mūsā initially volunteered to guard the entrance without being instructed by the Prophet ﷺ. Later, the Prophet ﷺ formally directed him to guard the gate.

١٠٠٠٦ — عن عائشة قالت: كان رسول الله ﷺ مضطجعًا في بيتي، كاشفًا عن فخذيه أو ساقيه، فاستأذن أبو بكر، فأذن له وهو على تلك الحال، فتحدث، ثم استأذن عمر، فأذن له وهو كذلك، فتحدث، ثم استأذن عثمان، فجلس رسول الله ﷺ وسوَّى ثيابه - قال محمد: ولا أقول ذلك في يوم واحد - فدخل فتحدث. فلما خرج قالت عائشة: دخل أبو بكر فلم تهتش له ولم تباله، ثم دخل عمر فلم تهتش له ولم تباله، ثم دخل عثمان فجلست وسويت ثيابك؟ فقال: ((ألا أستحي من رجل تستحي منه الملائكة؟)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤٠١).

10006 — ʿĀʾishah narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was reclining in my house with his thighs—or his lower legs—uncovered.
Abū Bakr sought permission to enter, and the Prophet ﷺ admitted him while remaining in that state. They spoke together.
Then ʿUmar sought permission to enter, and the Prophet ﷺ admitted him while remaining in the same state. They spoke together.
Then ʿUthmān sought permission to enter. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat upright and adjusted his clothing.
Muḥammad said:
“I do not say that all of this occurred on the same day.”
ʿUthmān entered and spoke with him.
After he left, ʿĀʾishah said:
“Abū Bakr entered, yet you did not become particularly animated or concerned by his entrance. Then ʿUmar entered, and you did not become particularly animated or concerned by his entrance. But when ʿUthmān entered, you sat upright and adjusted your clothing.”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“Should I not feel modest before a man before whom the angels feel modest?”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2401).

١٠٠٠٧ — عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ وعثمان حدثاه أن أبا بكر استأذن على رسول الله ﷺ وهو مضطجع على فراشه، لابس مرط عائشة، فأذن لأبي بكر وهو كذلك، فقضى إليه حاجته ثم انصرف، ثم استأذن عمر، فأذن له وهو على تلك الحال، فقضى إليه حاجته ثم انصرف.
قال عثمان: ثم استأذنت عليه، فجلس وقال لعائشة: ((اجمعي عليك ثيابك)). فقضيت إليه حاجتي ثم انصرفت.
فقالت عائشة: يا رسول الله، ما لي لم أرك فزعت لأبي بكر وعمر رضي الله عنهما كما فزعت لعثمان؟ قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((إن عثمان رجل حيي، وإني خشيت إن أذنت له على تلك الحال أن لا يبلغ إليَّ في حاجته)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤٠٢).

10007 — ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and ʿUthmān narrated:
Abū Bakr sought permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was reclining upon his bed and wearing ʿĀʾishah’s woolen garment.
The Prophet ﷺ permitted Abū Bakr to enter while remaining in that state. Abū Bakr presented his need and then departed.
Then ʿUmar sought permission to enter. The Prophet ﷺ admitted him while remaining in the same state. ʿUmar presented his need and then departed.
ʿUthmān said:
Then I sought permission to enter. The Prophet ﷺ sat upright and said to ʿĀʾishah:
“Gather your garments around yourself.”
I presented my need to him and then departed.
ʿĀʾishah asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, why did I not see you become concerned about Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, as you became concerned about ʿUthmān?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“ʿUthmān is an exceedingly modest man, and I feared that if I admitted him while I was in that state, he would not fully express his need to me.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2402).

١٠٠٠٨ — عن محمد بن سيرين أن رجلًا بالكوفة شهد أن عثمان رضي الله عنه قُتل شهيدًا، فأخذته الزبانية فرفعوه إلى علي رضي الله عنه، وقالوا: لولا أن تنهانا - أو نهيتنا - أن لا نقتل أحدًا لقتلناه، هذا زعم أنه شهد أن عثمان رضي الله عنه قُتل شهيدًا.
فقال الرجل لعلي رضي الله عنه: وأنت تشهد. أتذكر أني أتيت رسول الله ﷺ فسألته فأعطاني، وأتيت أبا بكر فسألته فأعطاني، وأتيت عمر فسألته فأعطاني، وأتيت عثمان رضي الله عنه فسألته فأعطاني؟
قال: فأتيت رسول الله ﷺ فقلت: يا رسول الله، ادع الله أن يبارك لي. فقال النبي ﷺ: ((كيف لا يبارك لك، وأعطاك نبي وصديق وشهيدان، وأعطاك نبي وصديق وشهيدان، وأعطاك نبي وصديق وشهيدان؟)).
صحيح: رواه أبو يعلى (١٦٠١).

10008 — Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn narrated:
A man in Kūfah testified that ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, had been killed as a martyr.
Some harsh guards seized him and brought him before ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him. They said:
“Were it not that you have forbidden us—or had forbidden us—from killing anyone, we would have killed him. He claims to testify that ʿUthmān was killed as a martyr.”
The man said to ʿAlī:
“You also bear witness to this. Do you remember that I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him, and he gave to me; then I came to Abū Bakr and asked him, and he gave to me; then I came to ʿUmar and asked him, and he gave to me; and then I came to ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, and asked him, and he gave to me?”
He continued:
I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah to bless me.”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“How could you not be blessed when a prophet, a truthful one, and two martyrs have given to you? A prophet, a truthful one, and two martyrs have given to you. A prophet, a truthful one, and two martyrs have given to you.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Yaʿlā (1601).

١٠٠٠٩ — عن الأسود بن هلال، عن رجل من قومه قال: كان يقول في خلافة عمر بن الخطاب: لا يموت عثمان حتى يُستخلف. قلنا: من أين تعلم ذلك؟ قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((رأيت الليلة في المنام كأن ثلاثة من أصحابي وُزنوا، فوُزن أبو بكر فوزن، ثم وُزن عمر فوزن، ثم وُزن عثمان فنقص صاحبنا، وهو صالح)).
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٦٦٠٤).

10009 — Al-Aswad ibn Hilāl narrated from a man of his people who used to say during the caliphate of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb:
“ʿUthmān will not die until he becomes caliph.”
We asked him:
“How do you know that?”
He replied:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Last night, I saw in a dream that three of my Companions were weighed. Abū Bakr was weighed and proved weighty. Then ʿUmar was weighed and proved weighty. Then ʿUthmān was weighed, and our companion fell short, though he is righteous.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (16604).

I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“Last night, I saw in a dream that three of my Companions were weighed. Abū Bakr was weighed and proved weighty. Then ʿUmar was weighed and proved weighty. Then ʿUthmān was weighed, and our companion fell short, though he is righteous.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (16604).

١٠٠١٠ — عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: كنت مع رسول الله ﷺ، فجاء أبو بكر فاستأذن، فقال: ((ائذن له وبشره بالجنة)). ثم جاء عمر فاستأذن، فقال: ((ائذن له وبشره بالجنة)). ثم جاء عثمان فاستأذن، فقال: ((ائذن له وبشره بالجنة)). قال: قلت: فأين أنا؟ قال: ((أنت مع أبيك)).
صحيح: رواه أحمد (٦٥٤٨)، والطبراني في الكبير (١٣/٦١٥-٦١٦).

10010 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr narrated:
I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when Abū Bakr came and sought permission to enter.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Admit him and give him the glad tidings of Paradise.”
Then ʿUmar came and sought permission to enter.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Admit him and give him the glad tidings of Paradise.”
Then ʿUthmān came and sought permission to enter.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Admit him and give him the glad tidings of Paradise.”
I asked:
“Then where will I be?”
He replied:
“You will be with your father.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (6548) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (13/615–616).

١٠٠١١ — عن بريدة بن الحصيب أن رسول الله ﷺ كان جالسًا على حراء، ومعه أبو بكر وعمر وعثمان، فتحرك الجبل، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((اثبت حراء، فإنه ليس عليك إلا نبي، أو صديق، أو شهيد)).
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٢٩٣٩)، وابن أبي عاصم في السنة (١٤٤٣)، وقوله: “حراء” غير صحيح، والصواب: “أُحد” كما في الأحاديث الصحيحة.

10011 — Buraydah ibn al-Ḥuṣayb narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting upon Mount Ḥirāʾ with Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān when the mountain moved.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Be firm, Ḥirāʾ, for upon you there is only a prophet, a truthful one, or a martyr.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (22939) and Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim in al-Sunnah (1443).
The wording “Ḥirāʾ” is incorrect. The correct wording is “Uḥud,” as established in the authentic narrations.

١٠٠١٣ — عن أبي بكرة أن النبي ﷺ قال ذات يوم: ((من رأى منكم رؤيا؟)). فقال رجل: أنا، رأيت كأن ميزانًا نزل من السماء، فوزنت أنت وأبو بكر، فرجحت أنت بأبي بكر، ووُزن أبو بكر وعمر، فرجح أبو بكر، ووُزن عمر وعثمان، فرجح عمر، ثم رُفع الميزان، فرأينا الكراهية في وجه رسول الله ﷺ.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٦٣٤)، والترمذي (٢٢٨٧)، والنسائي في الكبرى (٨٠٨٠)، والحاكم (٣/٧٠-٧١).

10013 — Abū Bakrah narrated:
One day, the Prophet ﷺ asked:
“Who among you has seen a dream?”
A man replied:
“I have. I saw as though a scale descended from heaven. You and Abū Bakr were weighed, and you outweighed Abū Bakr. Then Abū Bakr and ʿUmar were weighed, and Abū Bakr outweighed ʿUmar. Then ʿUmar and ʿUthmān were weighed, and ʿUmar outweighed ʿUthmān. Then the scale was raised.”
We then saw displeasure upon the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4634), al-Tirmidhī (2287), al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (8080), and al-Ḥākim (3/70–71).

١٠٠١٤ — عن سمرة بن جندب أن رجلًا قال: يا رسول الله، إني رأيت كأن دلوًا دُلِّي من السماء، فجاء أبو بكر، فأخذ بعراقيها فشرب شربًا ضعيفًا، ثم جاء عمر فأخذ بعراقيها فشرب حتى تضلَّع، ثم جاء عثمان فأخذ بعراقيها فشرب حتى تضلَّع، ثم جاء علي فأخذ بعراقيها فانتُشِطت، وانتضح عليه منها شيء.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٦٣٧)، وأحمد (٢٠٢٤٢).
قوله: “دُلِّي” أي أُرسل. وقوله: “بعراقيها” أي بأعوادها التي يُربط بها الحبل. وقوله: “فانتُشِطت” أي جُذبت إلى السماء ورُفعت إليه بسرعة. وقوله: “انتضح” الانتضاح: رشاش الماء على الثوب ونحوه.

10014 — Samurah ibn Jundub narrated that a man said:
“O Messenger of Allah, I saw in a dream that a bucket was lowered from the sky. Abū Bakr came, took hold of its crosspieces, and drank a small amount. Then ʿUmar came, took hold of its crosspieces, and drank until he was fully satisfied. Then ʿUthmān came, took hold of its crosspieces, and drank until he was fully satisfied. Then ʿAlī came and took hold of its crosspieces, but the bucket was suddenly pulled upward, and some of its water splashed upon him.”

The word “فانتُشِطت” means that it was suddenly pulled toward the sky and swiftly raised.
The word “انتضح” refers to drops or splashes of water falling upon a garment or something similar.

١٠٠١٤ — عن سمرة بن جندب أن رجلًا قال: يا رسول الله، إني رأيت كأن دلوًا دُلِّي من السماء، فجاء أبو بكر، فأخذ بعراقيها فشرب شربًا ضعيفًا، ثم جاء عمر فأخذ بعراقيها فشرب حتى تضلَّع، ثم جاء عثمان فأخذ بعراقيها فشرب حتى تضلَّع، ثم جاء علي فأخذ بعراقيها فانتُشِطت، وانتضح عليه منها شيء.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٦٣٧)، وأحمد (٢٠٢٤٢).
قوله: “دُلِّي” أي أُرسل. وقوله: “بعراقيها” أي بأعوادها التي يُربط بها الحبل. وقوله: “فانتُشِطت” أي جُذبت إلى السماء ورُفعت إليه بسرعة. وقوله: “انتضح” الانتضاح: رشاش الماء على الثوب ونحوه.

١٠٠١٥ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ كان على حراء، هو وأبو بكر وعمر وعثمان وعلي وطلحة والزبير، فتحركت الصخرة، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((اهدأ، فما عليك إلا نبي، أو صديق، أو شهيد)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤١٧-٥٠).
وأما ذكر “حراء” في هذا الحديث فالصحيح أنه “أُحد” كما ثبت في الأحاديث الأخرى.

10015 — Abū Hurayrah narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was upon Mount Ḥirāʾ together with Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Ṭalḥah, and al-Zubayr. The rock moved beneath them, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Be still, for upon you there is only a prophet, a truthful one, or a martyr.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2417, no. 50).
As for the mention of Ḥirāʾ in this narration, the correct name is Uḥud, as established in the other authentic narrations.

١٠٠١٦ — عن سعيد بن زيد قال: أنا أشهد على رسول الله ﷺ بما سمعت أذناي ووعاه قلبي من رسول الله ﷺ، فإني لم أكن لأروي عنه كذبًا يسألني عنه إذا لقيته، أنه قال: ((أبو بكر في الجنة، وعمر في الجنة، وعلي في الجنة، وعثمان في الجنة، وطلحة في الجنة، والزبير في الجنة، وعبد الرحمن في الجنة، وسعد بن مالك في الجنة، وتاسع المؤمنين في الجنة)).
لو شئت أن أسميه لسميته. قال: فضج أهل المسجد يناشدونه: يا صاحب رسول الله، من التاسع؟ قال: ناشدتموني بالله، والله عظيم، أنا تاسع المؤمنين، ورسول الله ﷺ العاشر.
ثم أتبع ذلك يمينًا، قال: والله لمشهد شهده رجل يغبر فيه وجهه مع رسول الله ﷺ أفضل من عمل أحدكم، ولو عُمِّر عمر نوح عليه السلام.
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٦٢٩) - واللفظ له -، وأبو داود (٤٦٥٠)، وابن ماجه (١٣٣).

10016 — Saʿīd ibn Zayd said:
I bear witness concerning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to that which my ears heard and my heart retained from him. I would never narrate a lie concerning him for which he might question me when I meet him.
He said:
“Abū Bakr is in Paradise, ʿUmar is in Paradise, ʿAlī is in Paradise, ʿUthmān is in Paradise, Ṭalḥah is in Paradise, al-Zubayr is in Paradise, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān is in Paradise, Saʿd ibn Mālik is in Paradise, and the ninth believer is in Paradise.”
Saʿīd added:
“Were I to wish to name him, I could do so.”
The people in the mosque raised their voices and implored him:
“O Companion of the Messenger of Allah, who is the ninth?”
He replied:
“You have adjured me by Allah—and Allah is Most Great—I am the ninth believer, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the tenth.”
He then followed this with an oath, saying:
“By Allah, a single battle attended by a man, in which his face became covered with dust alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, is better than the lifetime deeds of any one of you, even were he granted the lifespan of Nūḥ, peace be upon him.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (1629), whose wording is cited here, Abū Dāwūd (4650), and Ibn Mājah (133).

10017 — Ibn ʿUmar narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Ten men from Quraysh are in Paradise: Abū Bakr is in Paradise, ʿUmar is in Paradise, ʿUthmān is in Paradise, ʿAlī is in Paradise, Ṭalḥah is in Paradise, al-Zubayr is in Paradise, Saʿd and Saʿīd are in Paradise, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf is in Paradise, and Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ is in Paradise.”
Good: Narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (13823), al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ (2222), and al-Muʿjam al-Ṣaghīr (62).

١٠٠٢٠ — عن عمرو بن العاص أن النبي ﷺ بعثه على جيش ذات السلاسل، فأتيته فقلت: أي الناس أحب إليك؟ قال: ((عائشة)). فقلت: من الرجال؟ فقال: ((أبوها)). قلت: ثم من؟ قال: ((ثم عمر بن الخطاب)). فعد رجالًا.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٦٦٢)، ومسلم (٢٣٨٤-٨).

10020 — ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ appointed me commander of the army sent on the expedition of Dhāt al-Salāsil.
I came to him and asked:
“Who among the people is most beloved to you?”
He replied:
“ʿĀʾishah.”
I asked:
“Among the men?”
He replied:
“Her father.”
I asked:
“Then who?”
He replied:
“Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.”
He then named a number of other men.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3662) and Muslim (2384, no. 8).

١٠٠٢١ — عن بريدة بن الحصيب قال: كان أحب النساء إلى رسول الله ﷺ فاطمة، ومن الرجال علي.
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٣٨٦٨)، والطبراني في الأوسط (٧٢٥٨)، والحاكم (٣/١٥٥).
والحديث محمول على أهل بيته وأقاربه من حيث النسب، كما ذكر الترمذي عن شيخه إبراهيم بن سعيد الجوهري.
فعلى هذا لا تعارض بين هذا الحديث وبين الحديث الذي ورد فيه أن أحب الناس إلى رسول الله ﷺ: ((عائشة)). ومن الرجال: ((أبوها)).

english_source:
10021 — Buraydah ibn al-Ḥuṣayb narrated:
The most beloved of women to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was Fāṭimah, and the most beloved of men was ʿAlī.
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3868), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ (7258), and al-Ḥākim (3/155).
This hadith is understood as referring specifically to the members of the Prophet’s household and his blood relatives, as al-Tirmidhī related from his teacher Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿīd al-Jawharī.
Accordingly, there is no contradiction between this hadith and the narration stating that the most beloved person to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was ʿĀʾishah, and among the men, her father.

١٠٠٢٢ — عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ قالت: خرج النبي ﷺ غداة وعليه مرط مرحَّل من شعر أسود، فجاء الحسن بن علي فأدخله، ثم جاء الحسين فدخل معه، ثم جاءت فاطمة فأدخلها، ثم جاء علي فأدخله، ثم قال:
﴿إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُذْهِبَ عَنْكُمُ الرِّجْسَ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمْ تَطْهِيرًا﴾ [الأحزاب: ٣٣].

١٠٠٢٣ — عن أم سلمة أن النبي ﷺ كان في بيتها، فأتته فاطمة ببرمة فيها خزيرة، فدخلت بها عليه، فقال لها: ((ادعي زوجك وابنيك)).
قالت: فجاء علي والحسين والحسن، فدخلوا عليه، فجلسوا يأكلون من تلك الخزيرة، وهو على منامة له على دكان، تحته كساء خيبري.
قالت: وأنا أصلي في الحجرة، فأنزل الله عز وجل هذه الآية:
﴿إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُذْهِبَ عَنْكُمُ الرِّجْسَ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمْ تَطْهِيرًا﴾.
قالت: فأخذ فضل الكساء فغشاهم به، ثم أخرج يده فألوى بها إلى السماء، ثم قال:
((اللهم هؤلاء أهل بيتي وخاصتي، فأذهب عنهم الرجس، وطهرهم تطهيرًا. اللهم هؤلاء أهل بيتي وخاصتي، فأذهب عنهم الرجس، وطهرهم تطهيرًا)).
قالت: فأدخلت رأسي البيت، فقلت: وأنا معكم يا رسول الله؟ قال: ((إنك إلى خير، إنك إلى خير)).
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٦٥٠٨).
والمقصود من أهل البيت هنا من حيث النسب، وأما تطهير أهل البيت من الرجس فهو شامل للنسب والصهر جميعًا.

10023 — Umm Salamah narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ was in her house when Fāṭimah brought him a cooking pot containing a dish of meat and flour. She entered with it, and he said to her:
“Call your husband and your two sons.”
She said:
ʿAlī, al-Ḥusayn, and al-Ḥasan came and entered upon him. They sat and ate from that dish while the Prophet ﷺ was upon a sleeping mat placed on a raised platform, beneath which was a Khaybarī cloak.
She continued:
I was praying in the room when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse:
“Allah only intends to remove impurity from you, O People of the Household, and to purify you completely.”
The Prophet ﷺ took the remaining part of the cloak and covered them with it. He then extended his hand and raised it toward the sky, saying:
“O Allah, these are the members of my household and my closest ones. Remove impurity from them and purify them completely. O Allah, these are the members of my household and my closest ones. Remove impurity from them and purify them completely.”
She said:
I placed my head inside the room and asked:
“Am I with you, O Messenger of Allah?”
He replied:
“You are upon goodness. You are upon goodness.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (26508).
The expression “the People of the Household” here refers to those related to the Prophet ﷺ by blood. As for the purification of the household from impurity, it includes both blood relatives and those related through marriage.

١٠٠٢٤ — عن عمر بن أبي سلمة ربيب النبي ﷺ قال: نزلت هذه الآية على النبي ﷺ:
﴿إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُذْهِبَ عَنْكُمُ الرِّجْسَ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمْ تَطْهِيرًا﴾
في بيت أم سلمة، فدعا النبي ﷺ فاطمة وحسنًا وحسينًا، فجللهم بكساء، وعلي خلف ظهره فجلله بكساء، ثم قال:
((اللهم هؤلاء أهل بيتي، فأذهب عنهم الرجس وطهرهم تطهيرًا)).
قالت أم سلمة: وأنا معهم يا رسول الله؟ قال: ((أنت على مكانك، وأنت إلى خير)).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٣٢٠٥، ٣٧٨٧)، والطبري في تفسيره (١٩/١٠٦)، والطبراني في الكبير (٨٢٩٥).
10024 — ʿUmar ibn Abī Salamah, the stepson of the Prophet ﷺ, narrated:
This verse was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ in the house of Umm Salamah:
“Allah only intends to remove impurity from you, O People of the Household, and to purify you completely.”
The Prophet ﷺ called Fāṭimah, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn and covered them with a cloak. ʿAlī was behind him, so he covered him with the cloak as well. Then he said:
“O Allah, these are the members of my household. Remove impurity from them and purify them completely.”
Umm Salamah asked:
“Am I with them, O Messenger of Allah?”
He replied:
“You shall remain in your place, and you are upon goodness.”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3205, 3787), al-Ṭabarī in his Tafsīr (19/106), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (8295).

10025 — Shaddād Abū ʿAmmār narrated:
I entered upon Wāthilah ibn al-Asqaʿ while a group of people were with him. They mentioned ʿAlī. After they had left, he said to me:
“Shall I tell you what I witnessed from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?”
I replied:
“Yes.”
He said:
I went to Fāṭimah, may Allah be pleased with her, to ask about ʿAlī. She said:
“He has gone to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
I sat and waited for him until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived accompanied by ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn, holding each of the two boys by the hand.
When he entered, he drew ʿAlī and Fāṭimah close and seated them before him. He seated al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, one upon each thigh. He then wrapped his garment—or he said, a cloak—around them and recited:
“Allah only intends to remove impurity from you, O People of the Household, and to purify you completely.”
He then said:
“O Allah, these are the members of my household, and the members of my household are the most entitled.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (16988), authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (6976), and recorded by al-Ḥākim (2/416, 3/147).
Ibn Ḥibbān and al-Bayhaqī added at the end of the hadith:
Wāthilah, who was standing at one side of the house, said:
“Am I also among your family, O Messenger of Allah?”
He replied:
“You are among my family.”
Wāthilah said:
“This is among the things for which I have the greatest hope.”
That is, he was among the Prophet’s family in the sense of belonging to the people of Islam, not through blood relationship.

حسن: رواه الطبراني في الأوسط (٥٥١٠).

١٠٠٣١ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: كان رسول الله ﷺ يصلي، فإذا سجد وثب الحسن والحسين على ظهره، فإذا منعوهما أشار إليهم أن دعوهما، فلما قضى الصلاة وضعهما في حجره فقال: ((من أحبني فليحب هذين)).
حسن: رواه النسائي في الكبرى (٨١١٤)، وصححه ابن خزيمة (٨٨٧) - والسياق له -، وابن حبان (٦٩٧٠).

10031 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was praying, and whenever he prostrated, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn would leap upon his back. When the people attempted to prevent them, he gestured to them to leave the two boys alone.
When he completed the prayer, he placed them in his lap and said:
“Whoever loves me should love these two.”
Good: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (8114), authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (887), whose wording is cited here, and recorded by Ibn Ḥibbān (6970).

١٠٠٣٢ — عن بريدة بن الحصيب قال: كان رسول الله ﷺ يخطبنا، إذ جاء الحسن والحسين عليهما قميصان أحمران، يمشيان ويعثران، فنزل رسول الله ﷺ من المنبر فحملهما ووضعهما بين يديه، ثم قال:
((صدق الله: ﴿إِنَّمَا أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَأَوْلَادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ﴾، نظرت إلى هذين الصبيين يمشيان ويعثران، فلم أصبر حتى قطعت حديثي ورفعتهما)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (١١٠٩)، والترمذي (٣٧٧٤) وحسنه، والنسائي (١٤١٣، ١٥٨٥).

10032 — Buraydah ibn al-Ḥuṣayb narrated:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was delivering a sermon to us when al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn came wearing two red shirts, walking and stumbling.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ descended from the pulpit, carried them, and placed them before him. He then said:
“Allah has spoken the truth:
‘Your wealth and your children are only a trial.’
I looked at these two boys walking and stumbling, and I could not remain patient until I interrupted my speech and lifted them up.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1109), al-Tirmidhī (3774), who graded it good, and al-Nasāʾī (1413, 1585).

arabic_source:
١٠٠٣٣ — عن خالد بن معدان قال: وفد المقدام بن معديكرب، وعمرو بن الأسود، ورجل من بني أسد من أهل قنسرين إلى معاوية بن أبي سفيان، فقال معاوية للمقدام: أعلمت أن الحسن بن علي توفي؟ فرجَّع المقدام، فقال له رجل: أتراها مصيبة؟ قال له: ولم لا أراها مصيبة، وقد وضعه رسول الله ﷺ في حجره فقال: ((هذا مني، وحسين من علي)).
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤١٣١)، وأحمد (١٧١٨٩)، والطبراني في الكبير (٢٠/٢٦٩).
وقوله في الحديث: ((هذا مني)) يعني الحسن بن علي، وذلك من باب إظهار المحبة؛ لأن الحسن كان أكبر من الحسين، ولأنه قال فيه: ((إن الله سيصلح على يديه بين فئتين عظيمتين)). فقوله: ((هذا مني)) له مزيد من المزية.

10033 — Khālid ibn Maʿdān narrated:
Al-Miqdām ibn Maʿdīkarib, ʿAmr ibn al-Aswad, and a man from Banū Asad who lived in Qinnasrīn came as a delegation to Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān.
Muʿāwiyah said to al-Miqdām:
“Have you learned that al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī has died?”
Al-Miqdām began reciting the words said when a calamity occurs. A man asked him:
“Do you regard it as a calamity?”
He replied:
“Why should I not regard it as a calamity when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed him in his lap and said:
‘This one is from me, and Ḥusayn is from ʿAlī’?”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4131), Aḥmad (17189), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (20/269).
The Prophet’s statement in this hadith, “This one is from me,” refers to al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī. It was an expression of special affection, because al-Ḥasan was older than al-Ḥusayn and because the Prophet ﷺ said concerning him:
“Allah will bring reconciliation through him between two great groups.”
Therefore, the statement “This one is from me” indicates an additional distinction.

He replied:

١٠٠٣٤ — عن عبد الله بن عمر، وسأله عن المحرم - قال شعبة: أحسبه يقتل الذباب؟ - فقال: أهل العراق يسألون عن الذباب، وقد قتلوا ابن ابنة رسول الله ﷺ، وقال النبي ﷺ: ((هما ريحانتاي من الدنيا)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٧٥٣).
وفي لفظ له (٥٩٩٤): قال ابن أبي نُعْم: كنت شاهدًا لابن عمر، وسأله رجل عن دم البعوض؟ فقال: من أنت؟ فقال: من أهل العراق. قال: انظروا إلى هذا، يسألني عن دم البعوض، وقد قتلوا ابن النبي ﷺ…

english_source:
10034 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar was asked about a person in the state of iḥrām. Shuʿbah said:
“I think he was asked whether such a person could kill flies.”
Ibn ʿUmar replied:
“The people of Iraq ask about flies, although they killed the son of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“They are my two fragrant flowers in this world.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3753).
In another wording recorded by al-Bukhārī (5994), Ibn Abī Nuʿm said:
I was present with Ibn ʿUmar when a man asked him about the blood of a mosquito.
He asked:
“Where are you from?”
The man replied:
“From Iraq.”
Ibn ʿUmar said:
“Look at this man! He asks me about the blood of a mosquito, although they killed the grandson of the Prophet ﷺ…”

I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn were playing upon his stomach.
I asked:
“O Messenger of Allah, do you love them?”
He replied:
“Why should I not love them? They are my two fragrant flowers.”

١٠٠٣٧ — عن حذيفة قال: سألتني أمي: متى عهدك؟ تعني بالنبي ﷺ، فقلت: ما لي به عهد منذ كذا وكذا. فنالت مني، فقلت لها: دعيني آتي النبي ﷺ، فأصلي معه المغرب، وأسأله أن يستغفر لي ولك.
فأتيت النبي ﷺ فصليت معه المغرب، فصلى حتى صلى العشاء، ثم انفتل فتبعته، فسمع صوتي فقال: ((من هذا؟ حذيفة؟)). قلت: نعم. قال: ((ما حاجتك؟ غفر الله لك ولأمك)).
قال: ((إن هذا ملك لم ينزل الأرض قط قبل هذه الليلة، استأذن ربه أن يسلم علي ويبشرني بأن فاطمة سيدة نساء أهل الجنة، وأن الحسن والحسين سيدا شباب أهل الجنة)).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٣٧٨١)، وابن خزيمة (١١٩٤)، وابن حبان (٦٩٦٠)، والحاكم (٣/٣٨١).
ورواه أحمد (٢٣٣٣٠) من وجه آخر، عن إسرائيل، عن أبي السفر، عن الشعبي، عن حذيفة قال: أتيت النبي ﷺ، فصليت معه الظهر والعصر والمغرب والعشاء، ثم تبعته وهو يريد أن يدخل بعض حجره، فقام وأنا خلفه، كأنه يكلم أحدًا. قال: ثم قال: ((من هذا؟)). قلت: حذيفة. قال: ((أتدري من كان معي؟)). قلت: لا. قال: ((فإن جبريل جاء يبشرني أن الحسن والحسين سيدا شباب أهل الجنة)). قال: فقال حذيفة: فاستغفر لي ولأمي. قال: ((غفر الله لك يا حذيفة ولأمك)).
رجال إسناده ثقات، وابن أبي السفر هو عبد الله بن أبي السفر الثوري الكوفي، من رجال الجماعة، إلا أن الشعبي - وهو عامر بن شراحيل أبو عمرو الكوفي - أدرك زمان حذيفة وهو صغير، فإن صح قول ابن السمعاني بأنه ولد سنة عشرين، فيكون عمره عند وفاة حذيفة ست عشرة سنة؛ لأنه توفي في أول خلافة علي سنة ست وثلاثين. ولذا لم أجد من جزم بعدم سماعه منه.

10037 — Ḥudhayfah narrated:
My mother asked me:
“When was the last time you met him?”
She meant the Prophet ﷺ.
I replied:
“I have not met him for such-and-such a period.”
She reproached me, so I said to her:
“Let me go to the Prophet ﷺ, pray Maghrib with him, and ask him to seek forgiveness for you and me.”
I went to the Prophet ﷺ and prayed Maghrib with him. He continued praying until he prayed ʿIshāʾ. Then he departed, and I followed him.
He heard my footsteps and said:
“Who is this? Is it Ḥudhayfah?”
I replied:
“Yes.”
He asked:
“What do you need? May Allah forgive you and your mother.”
He then said:
“This is an angel who had never descended to the earth before this night. He sought permission from his Lord to greet me and give me the glad tidings that Fāṭimah is the leader of the women of Paradise, and that al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn are the leaders of the youth of Paradise.”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3781), Ibn Khuzaymah (1194), Ibn Ḥibbān (6960), and al-Ḥākim (3/381).
Aḥmad (23330) also recorded it through another chain from Isrāʾīl, from Abū al-Safar, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ḥudhayfah, who said:
I came to the Prophet ﷺ and prayed Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr, Maghrib, and ʿIshāʾ with him. Then I followed him as he intended to enter one of his rooms. He stopped while I stood behind him, and it appeared that he was speaking to someone.
He then asked:
“Who is this?”
I replied:
“Ḥudhayfah.”
He asked:
“Do you know who was with me?”
I replied:
“No.”
He said:
“Jibrīl came to give me the glad tidings that al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn are the leaders of the youth of Paradise.”
Ḥudhayfah said:
“Then seek forgiveness for me and my mother.”
He replied:
“May Allah forgive you, O Ḥudhayfah, and your mother.”
The narrators in its chain are trustworthy. Ibn Abī al-Safar is ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī al-Safar al-Thawrī al-Kūfī, one of the narrators relied upon by the major hadith compilers.
However, al-Shaʿbī—ʿĀmir ibn Sharāḥīl Abū ʿAmr al-Kūfī—lived during the time of Ḥudhayfah while still young. If Ibn al-Samʿānī’s statement that he was born in the year 20 AH is correct, he would have been sixteen years old when Ḥudhayfah died, because Ḥudhayfah died at the beginning of ʿAlī’s caliphate in the year 36 AH. Therefore, I have not found anyone who conclusively stated that al-Shaʿbī did not hear from him.

10038 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn are the leaders of the youth of Paradise, and Fāṭimah is the leader of the women of Paradise, except for Maryam, the daughter of ʿImrān.”
Good: Narrated by al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (8416), Aḥmad in his Musnad (11618, 11756), and al-Ḥākim (3/154).

١٠٠٣٩ — عن أبي موسى قال: كنت عند النبي ﷺ وهو نازل بالجعرانة بين مكة والمدينة، ومعه بلال، فأتى النبي ﷺ أعرابي فقال: ألا تنجز لي ما وعدتني؟ فقال له: ((أبشر)). فقال: قد أكثرت علي من “أبشر”. فأقبل على أبي موسى وبلال كهيئة الغضبان، فقال: ((رد البشرى، فاقبلا أنتما)). قالا: قبلنا. ثم دعا بقدح فيه ماء، فغسل يديه ووجهه فيه، ومج فيه، ثم قال: ((اشربا منه، وأفرغا على وجوهكما ونحوركما، وأبشرا)). فأخذا القدح ففعلا، فنادت أم سلمة من وراء الستر: أن أفضلا لأمكما، فأفضلا لها منه طائفة.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٣٢٨)، ومسلم (٢٤٩٧).

١٠٠٤٠ — عن أنس أن رجلين خرجا من عند النبي ﷺ في ليلة مظلمة، وإذا نور بين أيديهما حتى تفرقا، فتفرق النور معهما. وقال معمر: عن ثابت، عن أنس: إن أسيد بن حضير، ورجلًا من الأنصار. وقال حماد: أخبرنا ثابت عن أنس: كان أسيد بن حضير، وعباد بن بشر عند النبي ﷺ.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٨٠٥).

10040 — Anas narrated:
Two men departed from the Prophet ﷺ on a very dark night, and a light appeared before them. When they separated, the light also separated with them.
Maʿmar narrated from Thābit, from Anas, that they were Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr and another man from the Anṣār.
Ḥammād narrated from Thābit, from Anas, that the two men were Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr and ʿAbbād ibn Bishr.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3805).

١٠٠٤١ — عن عائذ بن عمرو أن أبا سفيان أتى على سلمان وصهيب وبلال في نفر، فقالوا: والله ما أخذت سيوف الله من عنق عدو الله مأخذها. قال: فقال أبو بكر: أتقولون هذا لشيخ قريش وسيدهم؟ فأتى النبي ﷺ فأخبره، فقال: ((يا أبا بكر، لعلك أغضبتهم، لئن كنت أغضبتهم لقد أغضبت ربك)). فأتاهم أبو بكر فقال: يا إخوتاه، أغضبتكم؟ قالوا: لا، يغفر الله لك يا أخي.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٥٠٤).

10041 — ʿĀʾidh ibn ʿAmr narrated:
Abū Sufyān passed by Salmān, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl, and a group of others.
They said:
“By Allah, the swords of Allah have not yet taken their full due from the neck of the enemy of Allah.”
Abū Bakr said to them:
“Do you say this to the elder of Quraysh and their chief?”
He then went to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“O Abū Bakr, perhaps you have offended them. If you have indeed offended them, then you have offended your Lord.”
Abū Bakr went back to them and said:
“My brothers, have I offended you?”
They replied:
“No. May Allah forgive you, our brother.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2504).

١٠٠٤٢ — عن البراء قال: اعتمر النبي ﷺ في ذي القعدة… وفيه قصة ابنة حمزة، وأنها تبعتهم حين الخروج من مكة، فتناولها علي فأخذ بيدها، وقال لفاطمة: دونك ابنة عمك، حملتها. فاختصم فيها علي وزيد وجعفر، فقال علي: أنا أحق بها، وهي ابنة عمي. وقال جعفر: ابنة عمي، وخالتها تحتي. وقال زيد: ابنة أخي. فقضى بها النبي ﷺ لخالتها، وقال: ((الخالة بمنزلة الأم)). وقال لعلي: ((أنت مني وأنا منك)). وقال لجعفر: ((أشبهت خلقي وخُلقي)). وقال لزيد: ((أنت أخونا ومولانا)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٦٩٩).

english_source:
10042 — Al-Barāʾ narrated:
The Prophet ﷺ performed ʿUmrah during the month of Dhū al-Qaʿdah…
The narration includes the story of the daughter of Ḥamzah, who followed them as they were leaving Makkah.
ʿAlī took her by the hand and said to Fāṭimah:
“Take charge of your cousin.”
Fāṭimah carried her.
Then ʿAlī, Zayd, and Jaʿfar disputed over who had the greater right to care for her.
ʿAlī said:
“I have the greatest right to her, for she is my cousin.”
Jaʿfar said:
“She is my cousin, and her maternal aunt is my wife.”
Zayd said:
“She is the daughter of my brother.”
The Prophet ﷺ awarded custody to her maternal aunt and said:
“The maternal aunt is in the position of the mother.”
He then said to ʿAlī:
“You are from me, and I am from you.”
He said to Jaʿfar:
“You resemble me in both appearance and character.”
And he said to Zayd:
“You are our brother and our freedman.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2699).
