١٠٢٢١ — عن عبد الله بن عباس قال: حدَّثني سلمان الفارسي حديثه من فيه، قال:
كنت رجلًا فارسيًا من أهل أصبهان، من أهل قرية منها يقال لها: جَيُّ، وكان أبي دهقان قريته، وكنت أحب خلق الله إليه، فلم يزل به حبه إياي حتى حبسني في بيته كما تحبس الجارية، واجتهدت في المجوسية حتى كنت قَطَنَ النار الذي يوقدها لا يتركها تخبو ساعة.
قال: وكانت لأبي ضيعة عظيمة، فشُغل في بنيان له يومًا، فقال لي: يا بني، إني قد شُغلت في بنياني هذا اليوم عن ضيعتي، فاذهب فاطلعها. وأمرني فيها ببعض ما يريد.
فخرجت أريد ضيعته، فمررت بكنيسة من كنائس النصارى، فسمعت أصواتهم فيها وهم يصلون، وكنت لا أدري ما أمر الناس لحبس أبي إياي في بيته، فلما مررت بهم وسمعت أصواتهم دخلت عليهم أنظر ما يصنعون.
فلما رأيتهم أعجبتني صلاتهم، ورغبت في أمرهم، وقلت: هذا والله خير من الدين الذي نحن عليه. فوالله ما تركتهم حتى غربت الشمس، وتركت ضيعة أبي ولم آتها.
فقلت لهم: أين أصل هذا الدين؟
قالوا: بالشام.
ثم رجعت إلى أبي، وقد بعث في طلبي، وشغلته عن عمله كله. فلما جئته قال: يا بني، أين كنت؟ ألم أكن عهدت إليك ما عهدت؟
قلت: يا أبت، مررت بناس يصلون في كنيسة لهم، فأعجبني ما رأيت من دينهم، فوالله ما زلت عندهم حتى غربت الشمس.
قال: يا بني، ليس في ذلك الدين خير، دينك ودين آبائك خير منه.
قلت: كلا والله، إنه خير من ديننا.
فخافني، فجعل في رجلي قيدًا، ثم حبسني في بيته.
قال: وبعثت إلى النصارى، فقلت لهم: إذا قدم عليكم ركب من الشام تجار من النصارى فأخبروني بهم.
قال: فقدم عليهم ركب من الشام تجار من النصارى، فأخبروني بهم.
قال: فقلت لهم: إذا قضوا حوائجهم وأرادوا الرجعة إلى بلادهم فآذنوني بهم.
قال: فلما أرادوا الرجعة إلى بلادهم أخبروني بهم، فألقيت الحديد من رجلي، ثم خرجت معهم حتى قدمت الشام.
فلما قدمتها قلت: من أفضل أهل هذا الدين؟
قالوا: الأسقف في الكنيسة.
قال: فجئته، فقلت: إني قد رغبت في هذا الدين، وأحببت أن أكون معك أخدمك في كنيستك، وأتعلم منك، وأصلي معك.
قال: ادخل.
فدخلت معه.
قال: فكان رجل سوء، يأمرهم بالصدقة، ويرغبهم فيها، فإذا جمعوا إليه منها أشياء اكتنزها لنفسه، ولم يعط المساكين منها شيئًا، حتى جمع سبع قلال من ذهب وورق.
قال: وأبغضته بغضًا شديدًا لما رأيته يصنع، ثم مات.
فاجتمعت إليه النصارى ليدفنوه، فقلت لهم: إن هذا كان رجل سوء، يأمركم بالصدقة ويرغبكم فيها، فإذا جئتموه بها اكتنزها لنفسه، ولم يعط المساكين منها شيئًا.
قالوا: وما علمك بذلك؟
قال: قلت: أنا أدلكم على كنزه.
قالوا: فدلنا عليه.
قال: فأريتهم موضعه، فاستخرجوا منه سبع قلال مملوءة ذهبًا وورقًا.
قال: فلما رأوها قالوا: والله لا ندفنه أبدًا.
فصلبوه، ثم رجموه بالحجارة.
ثم جاؤوا برجل آخر، فجعلوه مكانه.
قال يقول سلمان: فما رأيت رجلًا لا يصلي الخمس، أرى أنه أفضل منه، أزهد في الدنيا، ولا أرغب في الآخرة، ولا أدأب ليلًا ونهارًا منه.
قال: فأحببته حبًّا ما أحببت أحدًا قبله، فأقمت معه زمانًا، ثم حضرته الوفاة، فقلت له: يا فلان، إني كنت معك وأحببتك حبًّا ما أحببت أحدًا قبلك، وقد حضرك ما ترى من أمر الله، فإلى من توصي بي؟ وما تأمرني؟
قال: أي بني، والله ما أعلم أحدًا اليوم على ما كنت عليه، لقد هلك الناس، وبدلوا، وتركوا أكثر ما كانوا عليه، إلا رجلًا بالموصل، وهو فلان، فهو على ما كنت عليه، فالحق به.
قال: فلما مات وغُيِّب، لحقت بصاحب الموصل، فقلت له: يا فلان، إن فلانًا أوصاني عند موته أن ألحق بك، وأخبرني أنك على أمره.
فقال لي: أقم عندي.
فأقمت عنده، فوجدته خير رجل على أمر صاحبه، فلم يلبث أن مات.
فلما حضرته الوفاة قلت له: يا فلان، إن فلانًا أوصى بي إليك، وأمرني باللحوق بك، وقد حضرك من أمر الله ما ترى، فإلى من توصي بي؟ وما تأمرني؟
قال: أي بني، والله ما أعلم رجلًا على مثل ما كنا عليه إلا رجلًا بنصيبين، وهو فلان، فالحق به.
قال: فلما مات وغُيِّب، لحقت بصاحب نصيبين، فجئته فأخبرته بخبري وما أمرني به صاحبي.
قال: فأقم عندي.
فأقمت عنده، فوجدته على أمر صاحبه، فأقمت مع خير رجل.
فوالله ما لبث أن نزل به الموت.
فلما حُضر قلت له: يا فلان، إن فلانًا كان أوصى بي إلى فلان، ثم أوصى بي فلان إليك، فإلى من توصي بي؟ وما تأمرني؟
قال: أي بني، والله ما نعلم أحدًا بقي على أمرنا آمرك أن تأتيه إلا رجلًا بعمورية، فإنه على مثل ما نحن عليه، فإن أحببت فأته، فإنه على أمرنا.
قال: فلما مات وغُيِّب، لحقت بصاحب عمورية، وأخبرته خبري، فقال: أقم عندي.
فأقمت مع رجل على هدي أصحابه وأمرهم، واكتسبت حتى كان لي بقرات وغنيمة.
قال: ثم نزل به أمر الله، فلما حُضر قلت له: يا فلان، إني كنت مع فلان، فأوصى بي فلان إلى فلان، وأوصى بي فلان إلى فلان، ثم أوصى بي فلان إليك، فإلى من توصي بي؟ وما تأمرني؟
قال: أي بني، والله ما أعلمه أصبح على ما كنا عليه أحد من الناس آمرك أن تأتيه، ولكنه قد أظلك زمان نبي هو مبعوث بدين إبراهيم، يخرج بأرض العرب، مهاجرًا إلى أرض بين حرتين بينهما نخل، به علامات لا تخفى: يأكل الهدية، ولا يأكل الصدقة، وبين كتفيه خاتم النبوة، فإن استطعت أن تلحق بتلك البلاد فافعل.
قال: ثم مات وغُيِّب، فمكثت بعمورية ما شاء الله أن أمكث، ثم مرَّ بي نفر من كلب تجار، فقلت لهم: تحملوني إلى أرض العرب، وأعطيكم بقراتي هذه وغنيمتي هذه؟
قالوا: نعم.
فأعطيتهموها، وحملوني، حتى إذا قدموا بي وادي القرى ظلموني، فباعوني من رجل من يهود عبدًا، فكنت عنده.
ورأيت النخل، فرجوت أن تكون البلد التي وصف لي صاحبي، ولم يحق لي في نفسي.
فبينما أنا عنده، قدم عليه ابن عم له من المدينة من بني قريظة، فابتاعني منه، فاحتملني إلى المدينة.
فوالله ما هو إلا أن رأيتها، فعرفتها بصفة صاحبي، فأقمت بها، وبعث الله رسوله ﷺ، فأقام بمكة ما أقام، لا أسمع له بذكر مع ما أنا فيه من شغل الرق.
ثم هاجر إلى المدينة، فوالله إني لفي رأس عذق لسيدي أعمل فيه بعض العمل، وسيدي جالس، إذ أقبل ابن عم له حتى وقف عليه، فقال: يا فلان، قاتل الله بني قيلة، والله إنهم الآن لمجتمعون بقباء على رجل قدم عليهم من مكة اليوم، يزعمون أنه نبي.
قال: فلما سمعتها أخذتني العرواء، حتى ظننت أني سأسقط على سيدي.
قال: ونزلت عن النخلة، فجعلت أقول لابن عمه: ماذا تقول؟ ماذا تقول؟
قال: فغضب سيدي، فلكمني لكمة شديدة، ثم قال: ما لك ولهذا؟ أقبل على عملك.
قال: قلت: لا شيء، إنما أردت أن أستثبت عما قال.
وقد كان عندي شيء قد جمعته، فلما أمسيت أخذته، ثم ذهبت به إلى رسول الله ﷺ وهو بقباء.
فدخلت عليه، فقلت له: إنه قد بلغني أنك رجل صالح، ومعك أصحاب لك غرباء ذوو حاجة، وهذا شيء كان عندي للصدقة، فرأيتكم أحق به من غيركم.
قال: فقربته إليه.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ لأصحابه:
(( كلوا. ))
وأمسك يده فلم يأكل.
قال: فقلت في نفسي: هذه واحدة.
ثم انصرفت عنه، فجمعت شيئًا، وتحول رسول الله ﷺ إلى المدينة، ثم جئته به، فقلت: إني رأيتك لا تأكل الصدقة، وهذه هدية أكرمتك بها.
قال: فأكل رسول الله ﷺ منها، وأمر أصحابه، فأكلوا معه.
قال: فقلت في نفسي: هاتان اثنتان.
ثم جئت رسول الله ﷺ، وهو ببقيع الغرقد، وقد تبع جنازة من أصحابه، عليه شملتان له، وهو جالس في أصحابه.
فسلمت عليه، ثم استدرت أنظر إلى ظهره، هل أرى الخاتم الذي وصف لي صاحبي.
فلما رآني رسول الله ﷺ استدبرته، عرف أني أستثبت في شيء وُصف لي.
قال: فألقى رداءه عن ظهره، فنظرت إلى الخاتم، فعرفته، فانكببت عليه أقبله وأبكي.
فقال لي رسول الله ﷺ:
(( تحوَّل. ))
فتحولت، فقصصت عليه حديثي كما حدثتك يا ابن عباس.
قال: فأعجب رسول الله ﷺ أن يسمع ذلك أصحابه.
قال: ثم شغل سلمان الرق حتى فاته مع رسول الله ﷺ بدر وأحد.
قال: ثم قال لي رسول الله ﷺ:
(( كاتب يا سلمان. ))
قال: فكاتبت صاحبي على ثلاثمائة نخلة أحييها له بالفقير، وأربعين أوقية.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ لأصحابه:
(( أعينوا أخاكم. ))
فأعانوه بالنخل: الرجل بثلاثين ودية، والرجل بعشرين، والرجل بخمس عشرة، والرجل بعشر، يعني الرجل على قدر ما عنده، حتى اجتمعت لي ثلاثمائة ودية.
فقال لي رسول الله ﷺ:
(( اذهب يا سلمان ففقر لها، فإذا فرغت فأتني أكن أنا أضعها بيدي. ))
قال: ففقرت لها، وأعانني أصحابي، حتى إذا فرغت منها جئت إليه، فأخبرته، فخرج معي إليها، فجعلنا نقرب إليه الودي، ويضعه رسول الله ﷺ بيده، حتى فرغ منها.
قال سلمان: فوالذي نفس سلمان بيده، ما ماتت منها ودية واحدة.
فبقي المال، فأُتي رسول الله ﷺ بمثل بيضة من ذهب من بعض المغازي.
فقال:
(( ما فعل الفارسي المكاتب؟ ))
قال: فدعيت له.
فقال:
(( خذ هذه فأدِّ بها ما عليك يا سلمان. ))
قلت: يا رسول الله، وأين تقع هذه مما علي؟
قال:
(( خذها، فإن الله سيؤدي بها عنك. ))
قال: فأخذتها، فوزنت لهم منها، فوالذي نفس سلمان بيده، أربعين أوقية، فأوفيتهم حقهم، وعُتقت، فشهدت مع رسول الله ﷺ الخندق، ثم لم يفتني معه مشهد.
رواه أحمد بإسناد حسن، وابن إسحاق، والحاكم وصححه.
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٣٧٣٧)، والبزار في مسنده (٢٤٩٩، ٢٥٠٠)، والطبراني في المعجم الكبير (٦/٢٧٢، ٢٣٧٦).
10221 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās reported:
Salmān al-Fārisī narrated his own story to me directly. He said:
I was a Persian man from Iṣfahān, from a village called Jayy. My father was the chief landowner of our village, and I was the dearest of Allah’s creation to him. His love for me became so great that he kept me confined in the house just as a young girl would be confined. I devoted myself to the Magian religion until I became the keeper of the sacred fire, ensuring that it never went out for even a single moment.
He continued:
My father owned a large estate. One day he became occupied with construction work and said to me, “My son, I am busy today with this building project and cannot inspect my estate. Go and look after it for me,” giving me instructions regarding what he wanted done.
So I set out for the estate. On my way I passed one of the churches of the Christians. I heard their voices as they prayed inside. Because my father had always kept me confined at home, I knew nothing about the religions of other people. When I heard them, I went inside to see what they were doing.
When I observed them, I was deeply impressed by their worship. I became attracted to their religion and said to myself:
“By Allah, this religion is better than the one we follow.”
By Allah, I remained with them until sunset and never reached my father’s estate.
I asked them,
“Where did this religion originate?”
They replied,
“In al-Shām (Greater Syria).”
I then returned to my father, who had already sent people searching for me, and because of me all of his work had been interrupted.
When I came to him, he asked,
“My son, where have you been? Did I not entrust you with a task?”
I replied,
“My father, I passed by some people praying in their church. I was amazed by their religion, and by Allah I remained with them until sunset.”
He said,
“My son, there is no good in that religion. Your religion and the religion of your forefathers are better.”
I answered,
“No, by Allah! It is better than our religion.”
Fearing that I would leave his religion, he placed shackles on my feet and confined me in his house.
Salmān continued:
I sent word to the Christians, saying, “When a caravan of Christian merchants arrives from Syria, let me know.”
When a caravan from Syria arrived, they informed me.
I told them,
“When they finish their business and prepare to return to their land, inform me.”
When they were about to depart, they notified me. I removed the shackles from my feet and left with them until we arrived in Syria.
After reaching Syria, I asked,
“Who is the most knowledgeable and righteous follower of this religion?”
They replied,
“The bishop in the church.”
So I went to him and said,
“I have become interested in this religion and wish to remain with you, serving you in your church, learning from you, and praying alongside you.”
He said,
“Come in.”
So I stayed with him.
However, he was an evil man. He would encourage people to give charity and urge them to do so, but whenever they brought their charity to him, he hoarded it for himself and gave nothing to the poor. Eventually he accumulated seven large jars filled with gold and silver.
I came to hate him intensely because of what I saw him doing.
When he died, the Christians gathered to bury him. I said to them,
“This was an evil man. He used to command you to give charity and encourage you to do so, but whenever you brought it to him, he hoarded it for himself and never gave any of it to the poor.”
They asked,
“How do you know that?”
I replied,
“I can show you where his treasure is.”
They said,
“Show us.”
So I led them to its location. They uncovered seven large jars filled with gold and silver.
When they saw them, they declared,
“By Allah, we will never bury him.”
So they crucified him and then stoned him.
 Then they brought another man and appointed him in his place.
Salmān said:
I never saw a man—although he did not perform the five daily prayers—whom I considered better than him. No one was more detached from this world, more eager for the Hereafter, or more devoted in worship day and night than he was.
I loved him more than I had ever loved anyone before him. I remained with him for some time until death approached him. I said:
“So-and-so, I stayed with you and came to love you more than anyone before you. Now the decree of Allah has come upon you. To whom do you entrust me, and what do you command me to do?”
He replied:
“My son, by Allah, I do not know anyone today who remains upon what I am upon. The people have perished, altered their religion, and abandoned most of what they once followed, except for a man in al-Mawṣil (Mosul). He remains upon what I follow, so go to him.”
When he died and was buried, I traveled to the man in Mosul and said:
“So-and-so, before his death, so-and-so instructed me to come to you and told me that you follow the same way as he did.”
He said:
“Stay with me.”
So I stayed with him and found him to be an excellent man, firmly following the same path as his predecessor. Before long, however, he too passed away.
As death approached him, I said:
“So-and-so, so-and-so entrusted me to you and instructed me to come to you. Now the decree of Allah has come upon you. To whom do you entrust me, and what do you command me to do?”
He replied:
“My son, by Allah, I know no one who remains upon what we follow except a man in Naṣībīn. He is upon the same path, so go to him.”
When he died and was buried, I traveled to the man in Naṣībīn and informed him of my story and of the instructions given to me by my former teacher.
He said:
“Stay with me.”
So I remained with him and found that he too faithfully followed the same path as his predecessor. I stayed with another righteous man, but before long death came to him as well.
As he lay dying, I asked:
“So-and-so, so-and-so entrusted me to another, who then entrusted me to you. To whom do you now entrust me, and what do you command me to do?”
He replied:
“My son, by Allah, we know of no one remaining upon our way except a man in ʿAmmūriyyah (Amorium). He is upon the same path as we are. If you wish, then go to him.”
Salmān continued:
When he died and was buried, I traveled to the man in ʿAmmūriyyah (Amorium) and told him my story. He said:
“Stay with me.”
So I remained with him. He followed the same guidance and way as his predecessors. During my stay with him, I worked until I acquired some cows and a flock of sheep.
Then Allah decreed that his death should come. As he lay dying, I said:
“So-and-so, I stayed with so-and-so, who entrusted me to another, then another entrusted me to another, and finally I was sent to you. Now to whom do you entrust me, and what do you command me to do?”
He replied:
“My son, by Allah, I know of no one left upon what we follow to whom I can direct you. However, the time of a Prophet has now drawn near. He will be sent with the religion of Ibrāhīm (Abraham). He will emerge in the land of the Arabs and migrate to a land situated between two lava fields, with date palms growing between them. He has unmistakable signs: he accepts gifts but does not eat charity, and between his shoulders is the Seal of Prophethood. If you are able to reach that land, then do so.”
Salmān said:
He then died and was buried.
I remained in ʿAmmūriyyah for as long as Allah willed. Later, a group of merchants from the tribe of Kalb passed by. I said to them:
“Will you take me to the land of the Arabs if I give you these cows and this flock of sheep?”
They replied:
“Yes.”
So I gave them everything I owned, and they took me with them. But when we reached Wādī al-Qurā, they betrayed me and sold me as a slave to a Jewish man.
I stayed with him. When I saw the date palms, I hoped that this might be the land my companion had described, but I was not yet certain.
Salmān continued:
While I was with that Jewish man, a cousin of his from Madinah, belonging to Banū Qurayẓah, came to him. He purchased me from him and took me to Madinah.
By Allah, as soon as I saw it, I recognized it from the description my companion had given me. So I remained there.
Then Allah sent His Messenger ﷺ. He remained in Makkah for as long as Allah willed, but because I was occupied with slavery, I heard nothing about him.
Then he migrated to Madinah.
By Allah, one day I was at the top of a date palm working for my master while he was sitting below. A cousin of his came and said to him:
“May Allah fight Banū Qaylah! By Allah, they are gathered right now at Qubāʾ around a man who arrived today from Makkah, claiming to be a Prophet.”
The moment I heard those words, I began trembling so violently that I thought I would fall from the tree onto my master.
I quickly climbed down and kept asking the man,
“What did you say? What did you say?”
My master became angry, struck me a hard blow, and said,
“What concern is this of yours? Get back to your work!”
I replied,
“Nothing. I only wanted to make sure of what he said.”
I had some food that I had been saving. When evening came, I took it and went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was at Qubāʾ.
I entered and said:
“I have heard that you are a righteous man, and that you have companions who are strangers and in need. I had this set aside as charity, and I thought that you were more deserving of it than anyone else.”
I placed it before him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his Companions:
“Eat.”
But he himself kept his hand back and did not eat.
I said to myself:
“This is one sign.”
Salmān continued:
I then left him, gathered something else, and after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had moved to Madinah, I brought it to him and said:
“I noticed that you do not eat charity. This is a gift that I have brought to honor you.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ate from it and instructed his Companions to eat with him, and they all ate together.
I said to myself:
“Now there are two signs.”
Then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was at Baqīʿ al-Gharqad after attending the funeral of one of his Companions. He was sitting among his Companions wearing two cloaks.
I greeted him with salām, then walked around behind him, looking at his back to see whether I could find the Seal of Prophethood that my companion had described to me.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ noticed me moving behind him, he realized that I was trying to verify something that had previously been described to me.
So he uncovered his back by moving his cloak aside.
I looked at the Seal of Prophethood, recognized it immediately, then threw myself toward him, kissing it and weeping.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
“Come around and sit.”
So I came around, and I related my entire story to him exactly as I have related it to you, O Ibn ʿAbbās.
Salmān said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was pleased that his Companions were able to hear my story.
Salmān said:
My slavery kept me occupied, and because of it I missed being with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the Battles of Badr and Uḥud.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
“Arrange a contract of emancipation (mukātabah), O Salmān.”
So I made an agreement with my master that I would plant three hundred date palms, ensuring each one took root successfully, and pay him forty uqiyyahs of silver.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then said to his Companions:
“Help your brother.”
So the Companions helped me with the date palms. One man contributed thirty young palm trees, another twenty, another fifteen, another ten—each according to what he was able to give—until I had gathered three hundred young date palms.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
“Go, O Salmān, and prepare the holes for them. When you have finished, come to me, and I will plant them with my own hands.”
I prepared the holes, and my Companions helped me until everything was ready. Then I went to inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He came out with me. We handed him each young palm one by one, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ planted every single one with his own hands until all three hundred had been planted.
Salmān said:
By the One in Whose Hand is Salmān’s soul, not a single one of those trees died.
Only the monetary payment remained.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ received a piece of gold, about the size of an egg, from the spoils of one of the military expeditions.
He asked:
“Where is the Persian who has the emancipation contract?”
I was called to him.
He said:
“Take this and pay off what you owe, O Salmān.”
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, how could this possibly be enough to cover what I owe?”
He replied:
“Take it, for Allah will settle your debt with it.”
So I took it and weighed it out for them.
By the One in Whose Hand is Salmān’s soul, it weighed forty uqiyyahs, exactly what I owed. I paid them in full, and I was set free.
After that, I took part with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Battle of the Trench (al-Khandaq), and from then on I never missed any campaign alongside him.
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (23737), al-Bazzār in his Musnad (2499, 2500), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (6/272, no. 2376).

١٠٢٢٢ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: اشتكى سلمان فعاده سعد، فرآه يبكي، فقال له سعد: ما يبكيك يا أخي؟ أليس قد صحبت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ؟ أليس؟ أليس؟ قال سلمان: ما أبكي واحدة من ثنتين، ما أبكي حبًّا للدنيا، ولا كراهيةً للآخرة، ولكن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ عهد إليَّ عهدًا، فما أُراني إلا قد تعدَّيت. قال: وما عهد إليك؟ قال: عهد إليَّ: ((أنه يكفي أحدكم مثل زاد الراكب، ولا أُراني إلا قد تعدَّيت)). وأما أنت يا سعد، فاتقِ اللّٰه عند حكمك إذا حكمت، وعند قسمك إذا قسمت، وعند همِّك إذا هممت.
قال ثابت: فبلغني أنه ما ترك إلا بضعةً وعشرين درهمًا، من نُفَيْقةٍ كانت عنده.
حسن: رواه ابن ماجه (٤١٠٤)، والطبراني في المعجم الكبير (٦/٢٧٩)، وأبو نعيم في حلية الأولياء (١/١٩٧).

10222 — Anas ibn Mālik reported:
Salmān became ill, and Saʿd came to visit him. He found him weeping and said:
“Why are you crying, my brother? Did you not accompany the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Did you not? Did you not?”
Salmān replied:
“I am not crying for either of two reasons. I am not crying out of love for this world, nor out of dislike for the Hereafter. Rather, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entrusted me with an instruction, and I fear that I have gone beyond it.”
Saʿd asked:
“What instruction did he give you?”
Salmān replied:
“He instructed me:
‘For one of you, provisions equal to those of a traveler are sufficient.’
Yet I fear that I have exceeded that.”
Then he said to Saʿd:
“As for you, O Saʿd, fear Allah when you judge, when you distribute, and when you resolve upon a matter.”
Thābit said:
“It reached me that when Salmān died, he left behind no more than a little over twenty dirhams from a small amount of savings that he possessed.”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (4104), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (6/279), and Abū Nuʿaym in Ḥilyat al-Awliyāʾ (1/197).

10223 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ reported:
Zinbāʿ al-Judhāmī had a slave named Sandar. He found him kissing one of his slave girls, so he mutilated him by cutting off his male organ and severing his nose.
Sandar went to the Prophet ﷺ, who summoned Zinbāʿ and said:
“Do not burden them with what they cannot bear. Feed them from what you yourselves eat, clothe them with what you yourselves wear. If you are pleased with them, then keep them; and if you dislike them, then sell them. Do not torture the creation of Allah. Whoever is mutilated or burned with fire becomes free. He is the freed servant of Allah and the freed servant of His Messenger ﷺ.”
Sandar was therefore emancipated.
He then said:
“O Messenger of Allah, entrust me to someone’s care.”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“I entrust you to the care of every Muslim.”
After the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away, Sandar went to Abū Bakr and said:
“Honor the instruction of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning me.”
Abū Bakr continued providing for him until his own death.
Then Sandar went to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and said:
“Honor the instruction of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning me.”
ʿUmar replied:
“Certainly. If you wish to remain with me, I will continue providing for you just as Abū Bakr did. Otherwise, choose a place that you would like to live, and I will write a letter on your behalf.”
Sandar replied:
“Egypt, for it is a fertile land.”
So ʿUmar wrote to ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ:
“Honor the instruction of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning him.”
When Sandar arrived in Egypt, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ granted him a spacious tract of land and a house, and he lived there supported from the public treasury until he passed away. After his death, the property was reclaimed.
Good: Narrated by Muḥammad ibn Saʿd in al-Ṭabaqāt (7/506) and al-Bayhaqī (8/36).

١٠٢٢٤ — عن يزيد بن أبي عبيد قال: رأيت أثر ضربة في ساق سلمة، فقلت: يا أبا مسلم، ما هذه الضربة؟ فقال: هذه ضربة أصابتني يوم خيبر، فقال الناس: أصيب سلمة. فأتيت النبي ﷺ، فنفث فيها ثلاث نفثات، فما اشتكيتها حتى الساعة.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٢٠٦).
وتوفي سلمة بن عمرو بن الأكوع سنة ٧٤ هـ.

10224 — Yazīd ibn Abī ʿUbayd said:
I saw the scar of a wound on Salamah’s leg, so I asked,
“O Abū Muslim, what is this wound?”
He replied:
“It is a wound that I received on the Day of Khaybar. The people said, ‘Salamah has been wounded.’ So I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he blew lightly upon it three times. From that day until this very moment, it has never caused me any pain.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4206).
Salamah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Akwaʿ passed away in 74 AH.

١٠٢٢٦ — عن ابن عباس أن ضمادًا قدم مكة، وكان من أزد شنوءة، وكان يرقي من هذه الريح، فسمع سفهاء من أهل مكة يقولون: إن محمدًا مجنون، فقال: لو أني رأيت هذا الرجل لعل الله يشفيه على يدي. قال: فلقيه، فقال: يا محمد، إني أرقي من هذه الريح، وإن الله يشفي على يدي من شاء، فهل لك؟ فقال رسول الله ﷺ:
((إن الحمد لله، نحمده ونستعينه، من يهده الله فلا مضل له، ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأن محمدًا عبده ورسوله، أما بعد)).
قال: فقال: أعد عليَّ كلماتك هؤلاء. فأعادهن عليه رسول الله ﷺ ثلاث مرات. فقال: لقد سمعت قول الكهنة، وقول السحرة، وقول الشعراء، فما سمعت مثل كلمات هؤلاء، ولقد بلغن ناعوس البحر.
ثم قال: هات يدك أبايعك على الإسلام. فبايعه.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((وعلى قومك)).
قال: وعلى قومي.

10226 — Ibn ʿAbbās reported:
Ḍimād came to Makkah. He belonged to the tribe of Azd Shanūʾah and was known for treating people through ruqyah for what was believed to be madness or possession by jinn.
He heard the foolish people of Makkah saying,
“Muḥammad is insane.”
Ḍimād said to himself:
“If only I could meet this man, perhaps Allah would cure him through me.”
He met the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Muḥammad, I perform ruqyah for this affliction, and Allah grants healing through my hands to whom He wills. Would you like me to treat you?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“Indeed, all praise belongs to Allah. We praise Him and seek His help. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whomever He leaves astray, none can guide. I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner, and that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. To proceed…”
Ḍimād said:
“Repeat those words to me.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ repeated them three times.
Ḍimād then said:
“I have heard the words of soothsayers, magicians, and poets, but I have never heard speech like these words. They have reached the very depths of the sea.”
He then said:
“Give me your hand so that I may pledge allegiance to you upon Islam.”
So he pledged allegiance.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then said:
“And on behalf of your people as well?”
Ḍimād replied:
“And on behalf of my people.”
Later, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dispatched a military expedition that passed by the people of Ḍimād. The commander asked:
“Did you take anything from these people?”
One of the soldiers replied:
“I took a water vessel from them.”
The commander said:
“Return it, for these are the people of Ḍimād.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (868).
The phrase “this wind (الريح)” refers to madness or possession by jinn.
“Would you like me to treat you?” means: Would you like me to perform ruqyah for you?

10227 — Ḍamrah ibn Thaʿlabah reported:
He came to the Prophet ﷺ wearing two garments from Yemen.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“O Ḍamrah, do you think these two garments will admit you into Paradise?”
Ḍamrah replied:
“O Messenger of Allah, if you seek Allah’s forgiveness for me, I will not sit down until I take them off.”
The Prophet ﷺ supplicated:
“O Allah, forgive Ḍamrah ibn Thaʿlabah.”
Ḍamrah immediately hurried away and removed the two garments.
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (18979), al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr (4/337), and al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (2740).

The Prophet ﷺ said:
“O Ḍamrah, do you think these two garments will admit you into Paradise?”
Ḍamrah replied:
“O Messenger of Allah, if you seek Allah’s forgiveness for me, I will not sit down until I take them off.”
The Prophet ﷺ supplicated:
“O Allah, forgive Ḍamrah ibn Thaʿlabah.”
Ḍamrah immediately hurried away and removed the two garments.
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (18979), al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr (4/337), and al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (2740).

اللهم لولا أنت ما اهتدينا ولا تصدقنا ولا صلينا فاغفر فداءً لك ما أبقينا وثبت الأقدام إن لاقينا وألقين سكينةً علينا إنا إذا صيح بنا أبينا وبالصياح عولوا علينا

10228 — Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ reported:
We set out with the Prophet ﷺ on the expedition to Khaybar, traveling during the night.
A man from among the people said to ʿĀmir:
“O ʿĀmir, won’t you entertain us with some of your verses?”
ʿĀmir was known for chanting to encourage travelers, so he began reciting:
O Allah, were it not for You, we would never have been guided; Nor would we have given charity or offered prayer. So forgive us—we would sacrifice ourselves for You—for what we have committed. Make our feet firm when we meet the enemy. Send tranquility down upon us. Whenever we are called to battle, we respond. And they have relied upon shouting against us.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“Who is this camel-driver?”
They replied:
“ʿĀmir ibn al-Akwaʿ.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“May Allah have mercy upon him.”
One of the Companions remarked:
“It has become certain, O Messenger of Allah. If only you could let us benefit from him a little longer.”
(The narration then continues:)
When the two armies met, ʿĀmir’s sword was short. He struck at the leg of a Jewish fighter, but the blade rebounded and struck his own knee, causing the wound from which he later died.
Salamah said:
When the army was returning, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw me while holding my hand and asked:
“What is the matter with you?”
I replied:
“May my father and mother be sacrificed for you. They claim that ʿĀmir’s deeds have become void.”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“Whoever said that has lied. He will receive two rewards.”
He joined two of his fingers together and added:
“He was truly a striving warrior in Allah’s cause. Few Arabs have ever walked the earth equal to him.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4196) and Muslim (1802); the wording here is that of al-Bukhārī.

١٠٢٢٩ — عن أبي هريرة قال: بعث رسول الله ﷺ عمر على الصدقة، فقيل: منع ابن جميل، وخالد بن الوليد، والعباس عم رسول الله ﷺ، فذكر الحديث، وفيه: ثم قال: ((يا عمر، أما شعرت أن عم الرجل صنو أبيه؟)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري في الزكاة (١٤٦٨)، ومسلم في الزكاة (٩٨٣-١١)، كلاهما من طريق أبي الزناد، عن الأعرج، عن أبي هريرة فذكره، والسياق لمسلم، وليس عند البخاري: ((يا عمر، أما شعرت أن عم الرجل صنو أبيه؟)).

10229 — Abū Hurayrah reported:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed ʿUmar to collect the zakāh.
It was said:
“Ibn Jamīl, Khālid ibn al-Walīd, and al-ʿAbbās, the uncle of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, have withheld their zakāh.”
The narration continues, and in it the Prophet ﷺ said:
“O ʿUmar, do you not know that a man’s uncle is like his father?”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī in the Book of Zakāh (1468) and Muslim in the Book of Zakāh (983, no. 11), both through Abū al-Zinād from al-Aʿraj from Abū Hurayrah. This wording is Muslim’s. Al-Bukhārī does not contain the words: “O ʿUmar, do you not know that a man’s uncle is like his father?”

10230 — Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said regarding al-ʿAbbās:
“This is al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib—the most generous of Quraysh in giving, and the one who maintains family ties better than any of them.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (1610), al-Nasāʾī in Faḍāʾil al-Ṣaḥābah (71), Abū Yaʿlā (820), Ibn Ḥibbān (7052), and al-Ḥākim (3/328–329).

حسن: رواه أحمد (١٦١٠)، والنسائي في فضائل الصحابة (٧١)، وأبو يعلى (٨٢٠)، وابن حبان (٧٠٥٢)، والحاكم (٣/٣٢٨-٣٢٩).
10230 — Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said regarding al-ʿAbbās:
“This is al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib—the most generous of Quraysh in giving, and the one who maintains family ties better than any of them.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (1610), al-Nasāʾī in Faḍāʾil al-Ṣaḥābah (71), Abū Yaʿlā (820), Ibn Ḥibbān (7052), and al-Ḥākim (3/328–329).

١٠٢٣١ — عن عمر قال: كُتب إلى رسول الله ﷺ كتاب، فقال لعبد الله بن أرقم: ((أجب هؤلاء)). فأخذ عبد الله بن أرقم فكتبه، ثم جاء بالكتاب فعرضه على رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: ((أحسنت)). فما نال ذلك في نفسي حتى وُلِّيت، فجعلته على بيت المال.
حسن: رواه البزار (٢٦٧).

10231 — ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb reported:
A letter was sent to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said to ʿAbdullāh ibn Arqam:
“Reply to these people.”
ʿAbdullāh ibn Arqam wrote the reply and then presented it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“You have done well.”
ʿUmar said:
Those words remained with me until I became Caliph, so I appointed him in charge of the Bayt al-Māl (Public Treasury).
Good: Narrated by al-Bazzār (267).

١٠٢٣٢ — عن عبد الله بن ثعلبة بن صعير – وكان رسول الله ﷺ قد مسح عليه – أنه رأى سعد بن أبي وقاص يوتر بركعة.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٣٥٦).
ورواه أحمد (٢٣٦٦٧)، ولفظه: “وكان رسول الله ﷺ قد مسح وجهه زمن الفتح، أنه رأى سعد بن أبي وقاص – وكان سعد قد شهد بدرًا مع رسول الله ﷺ – يوتر بركعة واحدة بعد صلاة العشاء – يعني العتمة – لا يزيد عليها حتى يقوم من جوف الليل.”

10232 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Ṣuʿayr—upon whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had passed his hand—reported:
He saw Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ perform the Witr prayer with a single rakʿah.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6356).
Aḥmad (23667) narrates with the wording:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiped over his face during the Conquest of Makkah. He later saw Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ—who had fought at Badr alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—performing Witr with one rakʿah after the ʿIshāʾ prayer, without adding anything further until he rose later in the night.”

١٠٢٣٣ — عن ابن أبي مليكة قال: قال ابن الزبير لابن جعفر رضي الله عنهما: أتذكر إذ تلقينا رسول الله ﷺ أنا وأنت وابن عباس؟ قال: نعم، فحملنا وتركك.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٠٨٢)، ومسلم (٢٤٢٧/٦٥).

10233 — Ibn Abī Mulaykah reported:
Ibn al-Zubayr said to Ibn Jaʿfar:
“Do you remember when you, Ibn ʿAbbās, and I went out to meet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?”
He replied:
“Yes. He picked us up to ride with him and left you.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3082) and Muslim (2427).

١٠٢٣٤ — عن عبد الله بن جعفر قال: كان رسول الله ﷺ إذا قدم من سفر تُلُقِّي بصبيان أهل بيته، قال: وإنه قدم من سفر فسبق بي إليه، فحملني بين يديه، ثم جيء بأحد ابني فاطمة، فأردفه خلفه، قال: فأدخلنا المدينة ثلاثة على دابة.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤٢٨/٦٦).
وفي لفظ له (٢٤٢٨/٦٧): “كان النبي ﷺ إذا قدم من سفر تُلُقِّي بنا، قال: فتلقي بي وبالحسن أو بالحسين، قال: فحمل أحدنا بين يديه، والآخر خلفه حتى دخلنا المدينة.”

10234 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar reported:
Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from a journey, the children of his household would go out to welcome him.
On one such occasion, I reached him first, so he seated me in front of him on his mount. Then one of Fāṭimah’s two sons was brought to him, and he seated him behind him.
Thus, the three of us entered Madinah together on a single riding animal.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2428).
In another wording recorded by Muslim:
Whenever the Prophet ﷺ returned from a journey, we would go out to meet him. I was brought along with al-Ḥasan or al-Ḥusayn. He seated one of us in front of him and the other behind him until we entered Madinah.

One day, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seated me behind him on his riding animal and confided to me something privately that I have never disclosed to anyone.

10235 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar reported:
One day, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seated me behind him on his riding animal and confided to me something privately that I have never disclosed to anyone.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2429).

10236 — Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr reported:
When I was pregnant with ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr, I left Makkah near the end of my pregnancy and came to Madinah. I stayed at Qubāʾ, where I gave birth to him.
I then brought him to the Prophet ﷺ, who placed him in his lap. He asked for a date, chewed it, and then put some of it into the infant’s mouth.
Thus, the very first thing to enter his stomach was the saliva of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He then performed taḥnīk by rubbing the chewed date against the roof of his mouth, supplicated for him, invoked blessings upon him, and he became the first child born to the Muslims after the Hijrah.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3909) and Muslim (2146).
Muslim also narrates through another chain that ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr and Fāṭimah bint al-Mundhir reported:
Asmāʾ emigrated while pregnant with ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr and gave birth to him at Qubāʾ. She then brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that he could perform taḥnīk.
The Prophet ﷺ placed him in his lap and asked for a date.
ʿĀʾishah said:
“We searched for some time before we found one.”
The Prophet ﷺ chewed it and placed it into the baby’s mouth, so the first thing to enter his stomach was the saliva of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Asmāʾ added:
He then gently wiped over him, supplicated for him, and named him ʿAbdullāh.
Later, when he was seven or eight years old, al-Zubayr instructed him to give the pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
When the Prophet ﷺ saw him approaching, he smiled and accepted his pledge.

“His father is al-Zubayr, his mother is Asmāʾ, his maternal aunt is ʿĀʾishah, his grandfather is Abū Bakr, and his grandmother is Ṣafiyyah.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4664).

١٠٢٣٩ — عن ابن أبي مليكة قال: وكان بينهما شيء - أي بين ابن عباس وابن الزبير -، فغدوت على ابن عباس فقلت: أتريد أن تقاتل ابن الزبير، فتحل حرم الله؟ فقال: معاذ الله، إن الله كتب ابن الزبير وبني أمية محلِّين، وإني والله لا أُحِلُّه أبدًا. قال: قال الناس: بايع لابن الزبير، فقلت: وأين بهذا الأمر عنه؟ أما أبوه فحواري النبي ﷺ، يريد الزبير، وأما جده فصاحب الغار، يريد أبا بكر، وأمه فذات النطاقين، يريد أسماء، وأما خالته فأم المؤمنين، يريد عائشة، وأما عمته فزوج النبي ﷺ، يريد خديجة، وأما عمة النبي ﷺ فجدته، يريد صفية، ثم هو عفيف في الإسلام، قارئ للقرآن. والله إن وصلوني وصلوني من قريب، وإن ربُّوني ربُّوني أكفاء كرام، فآثر عليَّ التُّوَيْتات والأُسامات والحُمَيْدات، يريد بطونًا من بني أسد: بني تُوَيْت، وبني أسامة، وبني حميد. إن ابن أبي العاص برز يمشي القَدَمِيَّة، يعني عبد الملك بن مروان، وإنه لوى ذنبه، يعني ابن الزبير.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٦٦٥).

10239 — Ibn Abī Mulaykah reported:
There was a dispute between Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn al-Zubayr. I went to Ibn ʿAbbās and said:
“Do you intend to fight Ibn al-Zubayr and thereby violate the sacred sanctuary of Allah?”
He replied:
“Allah forbid! Allah has decreed that Ibn al-Zubayr and Banū Umayyah will be the ones involved in making it lawful to fight there, but by Allah, I will never be the one to violate it.”
He continued:
“People said to me, ‘Pledge allegiance to Ibn al-Zubayr.’
I replied, ‘How could anyone compare with him in this matter? His father was the disciple of the Prophet ﷺ’—meaning al-Zubayr.
‘His grandfather was the Companion of the Cave’—meaning Abū Bakr.
‘His mother was Dhāt al-Niṭāqayn’—meaning Asmāʾ.
‘His maternal aunt was the Mother of the Believers’—meaning ʿĀʾishah.
‘His paternal aunt was the wife of the Prophet ﷺ’—meaning Khadījah.
‘The Prophet’s paternal aunt was his grandmother’—meaning Ṣafiyyah.
‘Furthermore, he is chaste in Islam and a reciter of the Qur’an.’
By Allah, if my relatives honor me, then it is my own close relatives honoring me; and if they raise me in rank, they are honorable equals doing so.
Yet they preferred over me members of Banū Asad—Banū Tuwayt, Banū Usāmah, and Banū Ḥumayd.”
He then said:
“The son of Abī al-ʿĀṣ”—meaning ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān—“has come forward walking proudly, while Ibn al-Zubayr has withdrawn.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4665).

١٠٢٤٠ — عن ابن أبي مليكة قال: دخلنا على ابن عباس فقال: ألا تعجبون لابن الزبير، قام في أمره هذا؟ فقلت: لأحاسبنَّ نفسي له ما حاسبتها لأبي بكر ولا لعمر، ولهما كانا أولى بكل خير منه، وقلت: ابن عمة النبي ﷺ، وابن الزبير، وابن أبي بكر، وابن أخي خديجة، وابن أخت عائشة، فإذا هو يتعالى عني ولا يريد ذلك. فقلت: ما كنت أظن أن أعرض هذا من نفسي فيدعه، وما أراه يريد خيرًا، وإن كان لا بد أن يربَّني بنو عمي أحب إليَّ من أن يربَّني غيرهم.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٦٦٦).

10240 — Ibn Abī Mulaykah reported:
We entered upon Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said:
“Are you not amazed by Ibn al-Zubayr and what he has undertaken?”
He continued:
“I examined myself concerning him more carefully than I ever examined myself regarding Abū Bakr or ʿUmar, even though those two were more deserving of every good than he was.
I reflected that he is the son of the Prophet’s paternal aunt, the son of al-Zubayr, the grandson of Abū Bakr, the nephew of Khadījah, and the nephew of ʿĀʾishah.
Yet he behaved proudly toward me and did not desire reconciliation.
I never imagined that I would humble myself in this way only for him to reject it.
I do not think that he intends good.
Nevertheless, if I must be humbled, I would rather it be at the hands of my own relatives than at the hands of others.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4666).

١٠٢٤١ — عن أنس قال: سمع عبد الله بن سلام بقدوم رسول الله ﷺ وهو في أرضٍ يخترف فيها، فأتى النبي ﷺ فقال: إني سائلك عن ثلاث لا يعلمهن إلا نبي: فما أول أشراط الساعة؟ وما أول طعام أهل الجنة؟ وما ينزع الولد إلى أبيه أو إلى أمه؟ قال: ((أخبرني بهن جبريل آنفًا)). قال: جبريل؟ قال: ((نعم)). قال: ذاك عدو اليهود من الملائكة. فقرأ هذه الآية: ﴿قُلْ مَنْ كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِجِبْرِيلَ فَإِنَّهُ نَزَّلَهُ عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ [البقرة: ٩٧].
((أما أول أشراط الساعة: فنار تحشر الناس من المشرق إلى المغرب. وأما أول طعام أهل الجنة فزيادة كبد حوت. وإذا سبق ماء الرجل ماء المرأة نزع الولد، وإذا سبق ماء المرأة ماء الرجل نزعت)).
قال: أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وأشهد أنك رسول الله. يا رسول الله، إن اليهود قوم بُهْت، وإنهم إن يعلموا بإسلامي قبل أن تسألهم يبهتوني. فجاءت اليهود، فقال النبي ﷺ: ((أي رجل عبد الله فيكم؟)) قالوا: خيرنا وابن خيرنا، وسيدنا وابن سيدنا. قال: ((أرأيتم إن أسلم عبد الله بن سلام؟)) فقالوا: أعاذه الله من ذلك. فخرج عبد الله فقال: أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وأن محمدًا رسول الله. فقالوا: شرنا وابن شرنا، وانتقصوه. قال: فهذا الذي كنت أخاف يا رسول الله.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٤٨٠).

10241 — Anas ibn Mālik reported:
When ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām heard of the arrival of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he was working in his orchard. He came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“I am going to ask you about three matters that no one knows except a Prophet:
What is the first sign of the Hour?
What will be the first food of the people of Paradise?
And what causes a child to resemble his father or his mother?”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“Jibrīl has just informed me of them.”
He asked:
“Jibrīl?”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“Yes.”
ʿAbdullāh said:
“He is the enemy of the Jews among the angels.”
The Prophet ﷺ then recited:
‘Say: Whoever is an enemy to Jibrīl—for indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah…’ (Qur’an 2:97)
The Prophet ﷺ then said:
“As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather the people from the east to the west.
As for the first food of the people of Paradise, it will be the extra lobe of a whale’s liver.
If the man’s fluid precedes the woman’s fluid, the child will resemble his father; and if the woman’s fluid precedes the man’s fluid, the child will resemble his mother.”
ʿAbdullāh said:
“I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah.
O Messenger of Allah, the Jews are a people who slander others. If they learn of my accepting Islam before you ask them about me, they will falsely accuse me.”
The Jews then came.
The Prophet ﷺ asked them:
“What kind of man is ʿAbdullāh among you?”
They replied:
“He is the best of us, the son of the best of us, our leader and the son of our leader.”
The Prophet ﷺ asked:
“What if ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām were to embrace Islam?”
They replied:
“May Allah protect him from such a thing!”
Then ʿAbdullāh came out and declared:
“I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah.”
Immediately they said:
“He is the worst of us and the son of the worst of us,”
and they began speaking ill of him.
ʿAbdullāh then said:
“O Messenger of Allah, this is exactly what I feared.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4480).

١٠٢٤١ — عن أنس قال: سمع عبد الله بن سلام بقدوم رسول الله ﷺ وهو في أرضٍ يخترف فيها، فأتى النبي ﷺ فقال: إني سائلك عن ثلاث لا يعلمهن إلا نبي: فما أول أشراط الساعة؟ وما أول طعام أهل الجنة؟ وما ينزع الولد إلى أبيه أو إلى أمه؟ قال: ((أخبرني بهن جبريل آنفًا)). قال: جبريل؟ قال: ((نعم)). قال: ذاك عدو اليهود من الملائكة. فقرأ هذه الآية: ﴿قُلْ مَنْ كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِجِبْرِيلَ فَإِنَّهُ نَزَّلَهُ عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ [البقرة: ٩٧].
((أما أول أشراط الساعة: فنار تحشر الناس من المشرق إلى المغرب. وأما أول طعام أهل الجنة فزيادة كبد حوت. وإذا سبق ماء الرجل ماء المرأة نزع الولد، وإذا سبق ماء المرأة ماء الرجل نزعت)).
قال: أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وأشهد أنك رسول الله. يا رسول الله، إن اليهود قوم بُهْت، وإنهم إن يعلموا بإسلامي قبل أن تسألهم يبهتوني. فجاءت اليهود، فقال النبي ﷺ: ((أي رجل عبد الله فيكم؟)) قالوا: خيرنا وابن خيرنا، وسيدنا وابن سيدنا. قال: ((أرأيتم إن أسلم عبد الله بن سلام؟)) فقالوا: أعاذه الله من ذلك. فخرج عبد الله فقال: أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وأن محمدًا رسول الله. فقالوا: شرنا وابن شرنا، وانتقصوه. قال: فهذا الذي كنت أخاف يا رسول الله.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٤٤٨٠).

١٠٢٤٢ — عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال: ما سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول لأحد يمشي على الأرض: إنه من أهل الجنة، إلا لعبد الله بن سلام. قال: وفيه نزلت هذه الآية: ﴿وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ [الأحقاف: ١٠]. قال: لا أدري، قال مالك: الآية، أو في الحديث.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٨١٢)، ومسلم (٢٤٨٣).
قوله: “ما سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول لأحد يمشي على الأرض…” وقد علم سعد بن أبي وقاص أنه ﷺ قال لجماعة إنهم من أهل الجنة، فأجيب بأنه قال ذلك بعد موت المبشرين بالجنة، لأن عبد الله بن سلام عاش بعدهم، ولم يبق معه من العشرة غير سعد وسعيد بن زيد، ويؤيد ذلك بعض ألفاظ الحديث، كقوله عند مسلم: ((لحيٍّ يمشي…)). انظر: الفتح.

10242 — Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ said:
I never heard the Prophet ﷺ say about anyone walking upon the earth,
“He is one of the people of Paradise,”
except regarding ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām.
He also said:
Concerning him, the following verse was revealed:
“And a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to its truth…” (Qur’an 46:10)
Mālik said:
“I am not certain whether the statement about the verse was part of the hadith itself or the narrator’s own comment.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3812) and Muslim (2483).
The statement,
“I never heard the Prophet ﷺ say about anyone walking upon the earth that he is among the people of Paradise…”
does not contradict the glad tidings given to the ten Companions promised Paradise. The scholars explained that Saʿd was referring to a later time, after most of those ten had already passed away. At that point, ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām was still alive, and among the ten only Saʿd and Saʿīd ibn Zayd remained. This understanding is supported by Muslim’s wording:
“a living man walking upon the earth.”
See Fatḥ al-Bārī.

قال: والرجل عبد الله بن سلام.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٨١٣)، ومسلم (٢٤٨٤/١٤٨).
وفي لفظ: ((يموت عبد الله وهو آخذ بالعروة الوثقى)). رواه البخاري (٧٠١٠)، ومسلم (٢٤٨٤/١٤٩).

10243 — Qays ibn ʿAbbād said:
I was in Madinah among some people, among whom were some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ. Then a man came whose face bore the marks of humility and devotion. Some of the people said:
“This is a man from the people of Paradise.”
He prayed two rakʿahs, making them brief, then left. I followed him until he entered his house, and I entered as well. We talked together, and when he became at ease with me, I said to him:
“When you entered earlier, a man said such-and-such about you.”
He said:
“Subḥān Allāh! It is not appropriate for anyone to say what he does not know. I will tell you why that is.”
He continued:
“I saw a dream during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I related it to him. I saw myself in a garden”—and he mentioned its vastness, its grass, and its greenery—“and in the middle of the garden was a pillar of iron, its base in the earth and its top in the sky. At its top was a handhold. It was said to me, ‘Climb it.’ I said, ‘I cannot.’ Then a helper came to me.”
Ibn ʿAwn said:
“The helper was a servant.”
“He took hold of my garments from behind”—and he described that he lifted him from behind with his hand—“and I climbed until I reached the top of the pillar. I grasped the handhold, and it was said to me:
‘Hold on firmly.’
When I awoke, it was still in my hand. I related it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said:
‘That garden is Islam. That pillar is the pillar of Islam. That handhold is the Firmest Handhold. And you will remain upon Islam until you die.’”
He said:
“The man was ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3813) and Muslim (2484/148).
In another wording:
“ʿAbdullāh will die while holding firmly to the Firmest Handhold.”
Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7010) and Muslim (2484/149).

١٠٢٤٤ — عن خرشة بن الحر قال: كنت جالسا في حلقة في مسجد المدينة، قال: وفيها شيخ حسن الهيئة، وهو عبد اللّٰه بن سلام، قال: فجعل يحدثهم حديثا حسنا، قال: فلما قام، قال القوم: من سره أن ينظر إلى رجل من أهل الجنة فلينظر إلى هذا، قلت: والله لأتبعنه فلأعلمن مكان بيته، قال: فتبعته، فانطلق حتى كاد أن يخرج من المدينة، ثم دخل منزله، قال: فاستأذنت عليه، فأذن لي، فقال: ما حاجتك يا ابن أخي؟ قال: قلت له: سمعت القوم يقولون لك لما قمت: من سره أن ينظر إلى رجل من أهل الجنة فلينظر إلى هذا، فأعجبني أن أكون معك، قال: الله أعلم بأهل الجنة، وسأحدثك مم قالوا ذاك، إني بينما أنا نائم إذ أتاني رجل، فقال لي: قم، فأخذ بيدي فانطلقت معه، قال: فإذا أنا بجواد عن شمالي، قال: فأخذت لآخذ فيها، فقال لي: لا تأخذ فيها، فإنها طرق أصحاب الشمال، قال: فإذا جواد منهج على يميني، فقال لي: خذ ههنا، فأتى بي جبلا، فقال لي: اصعد، قال: فجعلت إذا أردت أن أصعد خررت على استي، قال: حتى فعلت ذلك مرارا، قال: ثم انطلق بي حتى أتى بي عمودا رأسه في السماء، وأسفله في الأرض، في أعلاه حلقة، فقال لي: اصعد فوق هذا، قال: قلت: كيف أصعد هذا ورأسه في السماء؟ قال: فأخذ بيدي فزجل بي، قال: فإذا أنا متعلق بالحلقة، قال: ثم ضرب العمود فخر، قال: وبقيت متعلقا بالحلقة حتى أصبحت، قال: فأتيت النبي ﷺ فقصصتها عليه، فقال: ((أما الطرق التي رأيت عن يسارك فهي طرق أصحاب الشمال، وأما الطرق التي عن يمينك فهي طرق أصحاب اليمين، وأما الجبل فهو منزل الشهداء، ولن تناله، وأما العمود فهو عمود الإسلام، وأما العروة فهي عروة الإسلام، ولن تزال متمسكا بها حتى تموت)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤٨٤/١٥٠).

10244 — Kharashah ibn al-Ḥurr said:
I was sitting in a gathering in the Mosque of Madinah. In it was an elderly man of fine appearance, and he was ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām. He began relating good narrations to them.
When he stood to leave, the people said:
“Whoever wishes to look at a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this man.”
I said:
“By Allah, I will follow him until I learn where his house is.”
So I followed him. He continued until he nearly left Madinah, then entered his house.
I sought permission to enter, and he gave me permission.
He said:
“What is your need, my nephew?”
I said:
“I heard the people say, when you stood up, ‘Whoever wishes to look at a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this man,’ so I wished to be with you.”
He said:
“Allah knows best who the people of Paradise are. I will tell you why they said that.
While I was sleeping, a man came to me and said, ‘Get up.’ He took me by the hand, and I went with him.
Then I saw paths on my left. I was about to take them, but he said to me:
‘Do not take them, for they are the paths of the people of the left.’
Then I saw a clear path on my right, and he said to me:
‘Take this way.’
He brought me to a mountain and said:
‘Climb.’
Whenever I tried to climb, I fell upon my backside. This happened repeatedly.
Then he took me until he brought me to a pillar whose top was in the sky and whose base was in the earth. At its top was a ring. He said to me:
‘Climb above this.’
I said:
‘How can I climb it when its top is in the sky?’
He took me by the hand and lifted me up forcefully. Suddenly I was holding onto the ring. Then he struck the pillar and it fell, while I remained holding onto the ring until morning.
I then came to the Prophet ﷺ and related it to him.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“As for the paths that you saw on your left, they are the paths of the people of the left. As for the paths on your right, they are the paths of the people of the right. As for the mountain, it is the station of the martyrs, and you will not attain it. As for the pillar, it is the pillar of Islam. As for the ring, it is the handhold of Islam. You will continue holding firmly to it until you die.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2484/150).

I was sitting in a gathering in the Mosque of Madinah. In it was an elderly man of fine appearance, and he was ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām. He began relating good narrations to them.
When he stood to leave, the people said:
“Whoever wishes to look at a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this man.”
I said:
“By Allah, I will follow him until I learn where his house is.”
So I followed him. He continued until he nearly left Madinah, then entered his house.
I sought permission to enter, and he gave me permission.
He said:
“What is your need, my nephew?”
I said:
“I heard the people say, when you stood up, ‘Whoever wishes to look at a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this man,’ so I wished to be with you.”
He said:
“Allah knows best who the people of Paradise are. I will tell you why they said that.
While I was sleeping, a man came to me and said, ‘Get up.’ He took me by the hand, and I went with him.
Then I saw paths on my left. I was about to take them, but he said to me:
‘Do not take them, for they are the paths of the people of the left.’
Then I saw a clear path on my right, and he said to me:
‘Take this way.’
He brought me to a mountain and said:
‘Climb.’
Whenever I tried to climb, I fell upon my backside. This happened repeatedly.
Then he took me until he brought me to a pillar whose top was in the sky and whose base was in the earth. At its top was a ring. He said to me:
‘Climb above this.’
I said:
‘How can I climb it when its top is in the sky?’
He took me by the hand and lifted me up forcefully. Suddenly I was holding onto the ring. Then he struck the pillar and it fell, while I remained holding onto the ring until morning.
I then came to the Prophet ﷺ and related it to him.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“As for the paths that you saw on your left, they are the paths of the people of the left. As for the paths on your right, they are the paths of the people of the right. As for the mountain, it is the station of the martyrs, and you will not attain it. As for the pillar, it is the pillar of Islam. As for the ring, it is the handhold of Islam. You will continue holding firmly to it until you die.”

١٠٢٤٤ — عن خرشة بن الحر قال: كنت جالسا في حلقة في مسجد المدينة، قال: وفيها شيخ حسن الهيئة، وهو عبد اللّٰه بن سلام، قال: فجعل يحدثهم حديثا حسنا، قال: فلما قام، قال القوم: من سره أن ينظر إلى رجل من أهل الجنة فلينظر إلى هذا، قلت: والله لأتبعنه فلأعلمن مكان بيته، قال: فتبعته، فانطلق حتى كاد أن يخرج من المدينة، ثم دخل منزله، قال: فاستأذنت عليه، فأذن لي، فقال: ما حاجتك يا ابن أخي؟ قال: قلت له: سمعت القوم يقولون لك لما قمت: من سره أن ينظر إلى رجل من أهل الجنة فلينظر إلى هذا، فأعجبني أن أكون معك، قال: الله أعلم بأهل الجنة، وسأحدثك مم قالوا ذاك، إني بينما أنا نائم إذ أتاني رجل، فقال لي: قم، فأخذ بيدي فانطلقت معه، قال: فإذا أنا بجواد عن شمالي، قال: فأخذت لآخذ فيها، فقال لي: لا تأخذ فيها، فإنها طرق أصحاب الشمال، قال: فإذا جواد منهج على يميني، فقال لي: خذ ههنا، فأتى بي جبلا، فقال لي: اصعد، قال: فجعلت إذا أردت أن أصعد خررت على استي، قال: حتى فعلت ذلك مرارا، قال: ثم انطلق بي حتى أتى بي عمودا رأسه في السماء، وأسفله في الأرض، في أعلاه حلقة، فقال لي: اصعد فوق هذا، قال: قلت: كيف أصعد هذا ورأسه في السماء؟ قال: فأخذ بيدي فزجل بي، قال: فإذا أنا متعلق بالحلقة، قال: ثم ضرب العمود فخر، قال: وبقيت متعلقا بالحلقة حتى أصبحت، قال: فأتيت النبي ﷺ فقصصتها عليه، فقال: ((أما الطرق التي رأيت عن يسارك فهي طرق أصحاب الشمال، وأما الطرق التي عن يمينك فهي طرق أصحاب اليمين، وأما الجبل فهو منزل الشهداء، ولن تناله، وأما العمود فهو عمود الإسلام، وأما العروة فهي عروة الإسلام، ولن تزال متمسكا بها حتى تموت)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤٨٤/١٥٠).

١٠٢٤٥ — عن يزيد بن عميرة قال: لما حضر معاذ بن جبل الموت قيل له: يا أبا عبد الرحمن أوصنا، قال: أجلسوني، فقال: إن العلم والإيمان مكانهما، من ابتغاهما وجدهما، يقول ذلك ثلاث مرات، والتمسوا العلم عند أربعة رهط: عند عويمر أبي الدرداء، وعند سلمان الفارسي، وعند عبد الله بن مسعود، وعند عبد الله بن سلام الذي كان يهوديا فأسلم، فإني سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((إنه عاشر عشرة في الجنة)).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٣٨٠٤)، وأحمد (٢٢١٠٤)، وصححه ابن حبان (٧١٦٥)، والحاكم (٣/٢٧٠).

10245 — Yazīd ibn ʿUmayrah said:
When death approached Muʿādh ibn Jabal, it was said to him:
“O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, advise us.”
He said:
“Seat me.”
Then he said:
“Knowledge and faith remain in their place. Whoever seeks them will find them.”
He repeated that three times.
Then he said:
“Seek knowledge from four men: from ʿUwaymir Abū al-Dardāʾ, from Salmān al-Fārisī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, and from ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām, who was a Jew and then accepted Islam. For I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
‘Indeed, he is the tenth of ten in Paradise.’”
Good: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3804), Aḥmad (22104), authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (7165), and al-Ḥākim (3/270).

10246 — Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ reported:
A bowl of tharīd was brought to the Prophet ﷺ. He ate from it, and some food remained.
He said:
“A man from the people of Paradise will enter through this mountain pass and eat what remains of this food.”
Saʿd said:
I had left my brother, ʿUmayr ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, preparing to come to the Prophet ﷺ, so I hoped that it would be him.
Then ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām came and ate it.
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (1458, 1591), authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (7164), and al-Ḥākim (3/416).

١٠٢٤٦ — عن سعد بن أبي وقاص أن النبي ﷺ أُتي بقصعة من ثريد فأكل، ففضل منها فضلة، فقال: ((يدخل من هذا الفج رجل من أهل الجنة، يأكل هذه الفضلة)). قال سعد: وقد كنت تركت أخي عمير بن أبي وقاص يتهيأ لأن يأتي النبي ﷺ، فطمعت أن يكون هو، فجاء عبد الله بن سلام فأكلها.
حسن: رواه أحمد (١٤٥٨، ١٥٩١)، وصححه ابن حبان (٧١٦٤)، والحاكم (٣/٤١٦).
10246 — Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ reported:
A bowl of tharīd was brought to the Prophet ﷺ. He ate from it, and some food remained.
He said:
“A man from the people of Paradise will enter through this mountain pass and eat what remains of this food.”
Saʿd said:
I had left my brother, ʿUmayr ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, preparing to come to the Prophet ﷺ, so I hoped that it would be him.
Then ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām came and ate it.
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (1458, 1591), authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (7164), and al-Ḥākim (3/416).

10247 — Ibn ʿAbbās reported:
The Prophet ﷺ went to relieve himself, and I placed water for his ablution.
When he came out, he said:
“Who placed this?”
In another wording:
“They said: ‘Ibn ʿAbbās.’”
He said:
“O Allah, grant him understanding.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (143) and Muslim (2477). This is the wording of Muslim. The wording of al-Bukhārī is:
“O Allah, grant him understanding of the religion.”

١٠٢٤٨ — عن ابن عباس قال: ضمني رسول الله ﷺ وقال: ((اللهم علِّمه الكتاب)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٧٥).
ورواه أيضًا (٣٧٥٦) من وجه آخر بلفظ: ((ضمني النبي ﷺ إلى صدره وقال: اللهم علمه الحكمة)).
ورواه ابن ماجه (١٦٦) بلفظ: ((اللهم علمه الحكمة، وتأويل الكتاب)).

10248 — Ibn ʿAbbās said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ embraced me and said:
“O Allah, teach him the Book.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (75).
Al-Bukhārī also narrated it (3756) through another chain with the wording:
“The Prophet ﷺ drew me to his chest and said: ‘O Allah, teach him wisdom.’”
Ibn Mājah (166) narrated it with the wording:
“O Allah, teach him wisdom and the interpretation of the Book.”

١٠٢٥٠ — عن عبد الرحمن بن عابس قال: سئل ابن عباس: أشهدت العيد مع النبي ﷺ؟ قال: نعم، ولولا منزلتي منه ما شهدته من الصغر، فأتى العَلَم الذي عند دار كثير بن الصلت، فصلى، ثم خطب، ولم يذكر أذانًا ولا إقامة، ثم أمر بالصدقة، فجعل النساء يشرن إلى آذانهن وحلوقهن، فأمر بلالًا فأتاهن، ثم رجع إلى النبي ﷺ.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٧٣٢٥).

10250 — ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀbis said:
Ibn ʿAbbās was asked:
“Did you attend the ʿĪd prayer with the Prophet ﷺ?”
He replied:
“Yes. Had it not been for my closeness to him, I would not have attended because I was so young.
He came to the landmark near the house of Kathīr ibn al-Ṣalt and led the prayer. Then he delivered the sermon. He made no mention of an adhān or an iqāmah.
Then he commanded that charity be given. The women began pointing to their earrings and their necklaces.
He instructed Bilāl, who went to them.
Then he returned to the Prophet ﷺ.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7325).

١٠٢٥١ — عن ابن عباس قال: كنت مع أبي عند رسول الله ﷺ وعنده رجل يناجيه، فكان كالمعرض عن أبي، فخرجنا من عنده، فقال لي أبي: أي بني، ألم تر إلى ابن عمك كان كالمعرض عني؟ فقلت: يا أبت، إنه كان عنده رجل يناجيه. قال: فرجعنا إلى النبي ﷺ، فقال أبي: يا رسول الله، لقد قلت لعبد الله كذا وكذا، فأخبرني أنه كان عندك رجل يناجيك، فهل كان عندك أحد؟ فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((وهل رأيته يا عبد الله؟)) قال: قلت: نعم. قال: ((فإن ذلك جبريل، وهو الذي شغلني عنك)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود الطيالسي (٢٨٣١)، وأحمد (٢٦٧٩)، والطبراني (١٠/٢٣٦).

english_source:
10251 — Ibn ʿAbbās said:
I was with my father in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and there was a man with him speaking to him privately.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ seemed as though he was occupied from giving attention to my father.
When we left him, my father said to me:
“My son, did you not notice that your cousin seemed occupied from me?”
I said:
“My father, there was a man with him speaking privately to him.”
So we returned to the Prophet ﷺ.
My father said:
“O Messenger of Allah, I said such-and-such to ʿAbdullāh, and he told me that there was a man with you speaking privately to you. Was there someone with you?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Did you see him, O ʿAbdullāh?”
I replied:
“Yes.”
He said:
“That was Jibrīl, and he was the one who occupied me from giving attention to you.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī (2831), Aḥmad (2679), and al-Ṭabarānī (10/236).

١٠٢٥١ — عن ابن عباس قال: كنت مع أبي عند رسول الله ﷺ وعنده رجل يناجيه، فكان كالمعرض عن أبي، فخرجنا من عنده، فقال لي أبي: أي بني، ألم تر إلى ابن عمك كان كالمعرض عني؟ فقلت: يا أبت، إنه كان عنده رجل يناجيه. قال: فرجعنا إلى النبي ﷺ، فقال أبي: يا رسول الله، لقد قلت لعبد الله كذا وكذا، فأخبرني أنه كان عندك رجل يناجيك، فهل كان عندك أحد؟ فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((وهل رأيته يا عبد الله؟)) قال: قلت: نعم. قال: ((فإن ذلك جبريل، وهو الذي شغلني عنك)).
صحيح: رواه أبو داود الطيالسي (٢٨٣١)، وأحمد (٢٦٧٩)، والطبراني (١٠/٢٣٦).
10251 — Ibn ʿAbbās said:
I was with my father in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and there was a man with him speaking to him privately.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ seemed as though he was occupied from giving attention to my father.
When we left him, my father said to me:
“My son, did you not notice that your cousin seemed occupied from me?”
I said:
“My father, there was a man with him speaking privately to him.”
So we returned to the Prophet ﷺ.
My father said:
“O Messenger of Allah, I said such-and-such to ʿAbdullāh, and he told me that there was a man with you speaking privately to you. Was there someone with you?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Did you see him, O ʿAbdullāh?”
I replied:
“Yes.”
He said:
“That was Jibrīl, and he was the one who occupied me from giving attention to you.”
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī (2831), Aḥmad (2679), and al-Ṭabarānī (10/236).

متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٠١٥، ٧٠١٦)، ومسلم (٢٤٧٨/١٣٩).

10252 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar said:
I saw in a dream as though there was a piece of silk in my hand. Whenever I lowered it toward any place in Paradise, it carried me flying to that place.
I related it to Ḥafṣah, and Ḥafṣah related it to the Prophet ﷺ.
He said:
“Indeed, your brother is a righteous man.”
Or he said:
“Indeed, ʿAbdullāh is a righteous man.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7015, 7016) and Muslim (2478/139).

١٠٢٥٣ — عن نافع أن ابن عمر قال: إن رجالا من أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ كانوا يرون الرؤيا على عهد رسول الله ﷺ، فيقصونها على رسول الله ﷺ، فيقول فيها رسول الله ﷺ ما شاء الله، وأنا غلام حديث السن، وبيتي المسجد قبل أن أنكح، فقلت في نفسي: لو كان فيك خير لرأيت مثل ما يرى هؤلاء، فلما اضطجعت ليلة قلت: اللهم إن كنت تعلم فيَّ خيرًا فأرني رؤيا، فبينما أنا كذلك إذ جاءني ملكان، في يد كل واحد منهما مقمعة من حديد، يقبلان بي إلى جهنم، وأنا بينهما أدعو الله: اللهم أعوذ بك من جهنم، ثم لقيني ملك في يده مقمعة من حديد، فقال: لن تُرَع، نعم الرجل أنت لو تكثر الصلاة، فانطلقوا بي حتى وقفوا على شفير جهنم، فإذا هي مطوية كطي البئر، لها قرون كقرون البئر، بين كل قرنين ملك بيده مقمعة من حديد، وأرى فيها رجالًا معلقين بالسلاسل، رؤوسهم أسفلهم، عرفت فيها رجالًا من قريش، فانصرفوا بي عن ذات اليمين، فقصصتها على حفصة، فقصتها على رسول الله ﷺ، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((إن عبد الله رجل صالح)).
فقال نافع: فلم يزل بعد ذلك يكثر الصلاة.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٠٢٨، ٧٠٢٩)، ومسلم (٢٤٧٨/١٤٠).
ورواه البخاري (٧٠٣٠)، ومسلم (٢٤٧٩/١٤٠)، وفيه قال النبي ﷺ: ((نعم الرجل عبد الله لو كان يصلي من الليل)). قال سالم: فكان عبد الله بعد ذلك لا ينام من الليل إلا قليلا.

10253 — Nāfiʿ reported that Ibn ʿUmar said:
Some men among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to see dreams during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they would relate them to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say concerning them whatever Allah willed.
At that time I was a young boy, and before I married, my home was the mosque.
I said to myself:
“If there is any good in you, you will see something like what these people see.”
When I lay down one night, I said:
“O Allah, if You know that there is any good in me, then show me a dream.”
While I was in that state, two angels came to me. In the hand of each of them was an iron mace. They took me toward Hell, while I was between them saying:
“O Allah, I seek refuge in You from Hell.”
Then an angel met me, carrying an iron mace in his hand, and he said:
“Do not be afraid. You are a good man, if only you would pray more.”
They took me until they stopped at the edge of Hell.
It was folded like a folded well. It had side-posts like the side-posts of a well, and between every two side-posts was an angel holding an iron mace.
I saw in it men hanging by chains with their heads downward.
I recognized among them some men from Quraysh.
Then they took me away toward the right.
I related the dream to Ḥafṣah, and Ḥafṣah related it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Indeed, ʿAbdullāh is a righteous man.”
Nāfiʿ said:
After that, he never ceased increasing his prayer.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (7028, 7029) and Muslim (2478/140).
Al-Bukhārī (7030) and Muslim (2479/140) also narrated it, in which the Prophet ﷺ said:
“What an excellent man ʿAbdullāh would be, if only he prayed during the night.”
Sālim said:
After that, ʿAbdullāh would sleep only a little during the night.

١٠٢٥٤ — عن مجاهد قال: شهد ابن عمر الفتح وهو ابن عشرين سنة، ومعه فرس حرور ورمح ثقيل، فذهب ابن عمر يختلي لفرسه، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((إن عبد الله، إن عبد الله)).
صحيح: رواه أحمد (٤٦٠٠).
وقوله: ((إن عبد الله، إن عبد الله)) يعني به: رجل صالح، كما جاء في الصحيح، وإن لم يثبت هذا اللفظ هاهنا.

10254 — Mujāhid said:
Ibn ʿUmar attended the Conquest while he was twenty years old. He had with him a spirited horse and a heavy spear.
Ibn ʿUmar went to cut fodder for his horse.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Indeed, ʿAbdullāh, indeed, ʿAbdullāh.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (4600).
The author’s statement:
His saying, “Indeed, ʿAbdullāh, indeed, ʿAbdullāh,” means: “a righteous man,” as has come in the authentic narrations, although this wording itself is not established here.

10255 — Mujāhid said:
We were traveling with Ibn ʿUmar.
He passed by a place and turned away from it.
He was asked:
“Why did you do that?”
He replied:
“I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do this, so I did it.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (4870) and al-Bazzār (128).

١٠٢٥٦ — عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: جيء بأبي يوم أحد قد مُثِّل به حتى وضع بين يدي رسول الله ﷺ وقد سجي ثوبًا، فذهبت أريد أن أكشف عنه، فنهاني قومي، ثم ذهبت أكشف عنه فنهاني قومي، فأمر رسول الله ﷺ فرفع، فسمع صوت صائحة، فقال: ((من هذه؟)). فقالوا: ابنة عمرو، أو أخت عمرو، قال: ((فلم تبكي؟ فما زالت الملائكة تظله بأجنحتها حتى رفع)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٢٩٣)، ومسلم (٢٤٧١/١٢٩). وهذا لفظ البخاري، ولفظ مسلم نحوه، وفيه بعد قوله: “فنهاني قومي”: “فرفعه رسول الله ﷺ، أو أمر به فرفع، فسمع صوت باكية أو صائحة.” والباقي مثله.
وفي لفظ: “أصيب أبي يوم أحد فجعلت أكشف الثوب عن وجهه وأبكي، وجعلوا ينهوني، ورسول الله ﷺ لا ينهاني، قال: وجعلت فاطمة بنت عمرو تبكيه، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((تبكيه أو لا تبكيه، ما زالت الملائكة تظله بأجنحتها حتى رفعتموه)).”
رواه البخاري (١٢٤٤)، ومسلم (٢٤٧١/١٣٠).

10256 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh said:
My father was brought on the Day of Uḥud after his body had been mutilated. He was placed before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he had been covered with a cloth.
I went, intending to uncover him, but my people stopped me.
Then I went again to uncover him, but my people stopped me.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the order, and he was lifted.
Then he heard the voice of a woman crying.
He said:
“Who is this?”
They replied:
“The daughter of ʿAmr,” or, “the sister of ʿAmr.”
He said:
“Why is she weeping? The angels continued shading him with their wings until he was lifted.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1293) and Muslim (2471/129).
This is the wording of al-Bukhārī. The wording of Muslim is similar, and after the words, “My people stopped me,” it states:
“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ lifted him, or ordered that he be lifted, and he heard the voice of a woman weeping or crying aloud.”
The remainder is the same.
In another wording:
“My father was struck down on the Day of Uḥud. I began uncovering the cloth from his face and weeping, while the people kept stopping me, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not stop me.
Fāṭimah bint ʿAmr also began weeping for him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
‘Whether you weep for him or do not weep for him, the angels continued shading him with their wings until you lifted him.’”
Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1244) and Muslim (2471/130).

١٠٢٥٧ — عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: لقيني رسول الله ﷺ فقال لي: ((يا جابر، ما لي أراك منكسرًا؟)) قلت: يا رسول الله، استشهد أبي، وترك عيالًا ودينًا، قال: ((أفلا أبشرك بما لقي الله به أباك؟)) قال: بلى يا رسول الله، قال: ((ما كلم الله أحدًا قط إلا من وراء حجاب، وأحيا أباك فكلمه كفاحًا، فقال: يا عبدي تمنَّ عليَّ أعطك، قال: يا رب، تحييني فأقتل فيك ثانية، قال الرب عز وجل: إنه قد سبق مني أنهم لا يرجعون، قال: وأنزلت هذه الآية: ﴿وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَمْوَاتًا﴾ [آل عمران: 169])).
حسن: رواه الترمذي (٣٠١٠)، وابن ماجه (١٩٠)، وصححه ابن حبان (٧٠٢٢)، والحاكم (٣/٢٠٣).
وقوله: كفاحًا أي: مواجهة ومشافهة بدون حجاب.

10257 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ met me and said:
“O Jābir, why do I see you broken with grief?”
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, my father was martyred, and he left behind dependents and debt.”
He said:
“Shall I not give you glad tidings of how Allah received your father?”
I said:
“Certainly, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said:
“Allah has never spoken to anyone except from behind a veil, but He brought your father to life and spoke to him directly, face to face.

١٠٢٥٨ — عن جابر بن عبد الله، قال: خرج رسول الله ﷺ من المدينة إلى المشركين ليقاتلهم، وقال لي أبي عبد الله: يا جابر، لا عليك أن تكون في نظّار أهل المدينة حتى تعلم إلى ما يصير أمرنا، فإن والله لولا أني أترك بنات لي بعدي، لأحببت أن تُقتل بين يدي.
قال: فبينما أنا في النُّظَّار إذ جاءت عمتي بأبي، وخالي عادلتاهما على ناضح، فدخلت بهما المدينة تدفنهما في مقابرنا، إذ لحق رجل ينادي: ((ألا إن النبي ﷺ يأمركم أن ترجعوا بالقتلى، فتدفنوها في مصارعها حيث قتلت)). فرجعنا بهما، فدفناهما حيث قُتلا.
فبينما أنا في خلافة معاوية بن أبي سفيان إذ جاءني رجل فقال: يا جابر بن عبد الله، والله لقد أثار أباك عمَّالُ معاوية، فبدا، فخرج طائفة منه، فأتيته فوجدته على النحو الذي دفنته، لم يتغير إلا ما لم يدعِ القتل - أو القتيل - فواريته.
قال: وترك أبي عليه دينا من التمر، فاشتد علي بعض غرمائه في التقاضي، فأتيت نبي الله ﷺ فقلت: يا نبي الله، إن أبي أصيب يوم كذا وكذا، وترك عليه دينا من التمر، وقد اشتد علي بعض غرمائه في التقاضي، فأحب أن تعينني عليه، لعله أن ينظرني طائفة من تمره إلى هذا الصرام المقبل.
فقال: ((نعم، آتيك إن شاء الله قريبًا من وسط النهار)).
وجاء معه حواريوه، ثم استأذن، فدخل، وقد قلت لامرأتي: إن النبي ﷺ جاءني اليوم قريبًا من وسط النهار، فلا أرينك، ولا تؤذي رسول الله ﷺ في بيتي بشيء، ولا تكلميه.
فدخل، ففرشت له فراشًا ووسادة، فوضع رأسه فنام، قال: وقلت لمولى لي: اذبح هذه العناق - وهي داجن سمينة - والوَحَى، والعَجَل، افرغ منها قبل أن يستيقظ رسول الله ﷺ وأنا معك.
فلم نزل فيها حتى فرغنا منها، وهو نائم، فقلت له: إن رسول الله ﷺ إذا استيقظ يدعو بالطهور، وإني أخاف إذا فرغ أن يقوم، فلا يفرغن من وضوئه حتى تضع العناق بين يديه.
فلما قام قال: ((يا جابر، ائتني بطهور)). فلم يفرغ من طهوره حتى وضعت العناق عنده، فنظر إلي فقال: ((كأنك قد علمت حبنا للحم، ادع لي أبا بكر)).
قال: ثم دعا حوارييه الذين معه، فدخلوا، فضرب رسول الله ﷺ بيديه وقال: ((بسم الله، كلوا)). فأكلوا حتى شبعوا، وفضل لحم منها كثير.
قال: والله إن مجلس بني سلمة لينظرون إليه، وهو أحب إليهم من أعينهم، ما يقربه رجل منهم مخافة أن يؤذوه.
فلما فرغوا قام، وقام أصحابه، فخرجوا بين يديه، وكان يقول: ((خلوا ظهري للملائكة)).
واتبعتهم حتى بلغوا أسكفة الباب، قال: وأخرجت امرأتي صدرها، وكانت مستترة بسقيفة في البيت، فقالت: يا رسول الله، صلِّ عليَّ، وعلى زوجي، صلى الله عليك.
فقال: ((اللهم صلِّ عليها، وعلى زوجها)).
ثم قال: ((ادع لي فلانًا))، لغريمي الذي اشتد عليَّ في الطلب.
قال: فجاء، فقال: ((أخِّر جاري عبد الله - يعني إلى الميسرة - طائفةً من دينك الذي على أبيه، إلى هذا الصرام المقبل)).
قال: ما أنا بفاعل، واعتلَّ، وقال: إنما هو مال يتامى.
فقال: ((أين جابر؟))
فقال: أنا ذا يا رسول الله.
قال: ((كِلْ له، فإن الله سوف يوفيه)).
فنظرت إلى السماء، فإذا الشمس قد دلكت، قال: ((الصلاة يا أبا بكر)).
فاندفعوا إلى المسجد، فقلت: قرِّب أوعيتك.
فكلت له من العجوة، فوفاه الله، وفضل لنا من التمر كذا وكذا.
فجئت أسعى إلى رسول الله ﷺ في مسجده، كأني شرارة، فوجدت رسول الله ﷺ قد صلى.
قلت: يا رسول الله، ألم تر أني كلت لغريمي تمره، فوفاه الله، وفضل لنا من التمر كذا وكذا؟
فقال: ((أين عمر بن الخطاب؟))
فجاء يهرول.
فقال: ((سل جابر بن عبد الله عن غريمه وتمره)).
فقال: ما أنا بسائله، قد علمت أن الله سوف يوفيه، إذ أخبرت أن الله سوف يوفيه.
فكرر عليه هذه الكلمة ثلاث مرات، كل ذلك يقول: ما أنا بسائله، وكان لا يراجع بعد المرة الثالثة.
فقال: ((يا جابر، ما فعل غريمك وتمرك؟))
قال: قلت: وفاه الله، وفضل لنا من التمر كذا وكذا.
فرجع إلى امرأته، فقال: ألم أكن نهيتك أن تكلمي رسول الله ﷺ؟
قالت: أكنت تظن أن الله يورد رسول الله ﷺ بيتي، ثم يخرج، ولا أسأله الصلاة عليَّ، وعلى زوجي، قبل أن يخرج؟
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٥٢٨١)، وأبو داود (١٥٣٣)، وصححه ابن حبان (٩١٦، ٩٨٤).
وقوله: ((والوَحَى، والعَجَل)) أي: السرعة، السرعة.

10258 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out from Madinah to fight the polytheists.
My father, ʿAbdullāh, said to me:
“O Jābir, it is your duty to remain among those watching over the people of Madinah until you learn what becomes of us. For by Allah, were it not that I would leave daughters behind after me, I would have loved for you to be killed before me.”
He said:
While I was among those keeping watch, my paternal aunt came with my father, and my maternal uncle. They had placed them equally upon a camel used for drawing water.
She entered Madinah with them so that she might bury them in our graveyards.
Then a man caught up with them, calling out:
“Indeed, the Prophet ﷺ commands you to return with those who have been killed and bury them where they were killed.”
So we returned with them and buried them where they had been killed.
Then, during the caliphate of Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān, a man came to me and said:
“O Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh, by Allah, the workers of Muʿāwiyah have uncovered your father.”
Part of his body became exposed.
So I went to him and found him in the same condition in which I had buried him. Nothing had changed except what the killing—or the slain body—had left unchanged.
So I buried him again.
He said:
My father left behind a debt that was to be paid in dates.
Some of his creditors became severe with me in demanding repayment.
So I went to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Prophet of Allah, my father was killed on such-and-such a day, and he left behind a debt to be paid in dates. Some of his creditors have become severe with me in demanding repayment. I would like you to help me with them, so that perhaps they may defer part of the payment until the coming date harvest.”
He said:
“Yes. I shall come to you, if Allah wills, around the middle of the day.”
His close companions came with him.
He sought permission to enter, and he entered.
I had already said to my wife:
“The Prophet ﷺ is coming to me today around the middle of the day. I do not want him to see you. Do not do anything in my house that may offend the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and do not speak to him.”
He entered, and I spread out bedding and a pillow for him.
He placed his head down and went to sleep.
I said to one of my servants:
“Slaughter this young she-goat—it is a fat domesticated one—and quickly, quickly, finish preparing it before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wakes up, and I will help you.”
