١٠٢٥٨ — عن جابر بن عبد الله، قال: خرج رسول الله ﷺ من المدينة إلى المشركين ليقاتلهم، وقال لي أبي عبد الله: يا جابر، لا عليك أن تكون في نظّار أهل المدينة حتى تعلم إلى ما يصير أمرنا، فإن والله لولا أني أترك بنات لي بعدي، لأحببت أن تُقتل بين يدي.
قال: فبينما أنا في النُّظَّار إذ جاءت عمتي بأبي، وخالي عادلتاهما على ناضح، فدخلت بهما المدينة تدفنهما في مقابرنا، إذ لحق رجل ينادي: ((ألا إن النبي ﷺ يأمركم أن ترجعوا بالقتلى، فتدفنوها في مصارعها حيث قتلت)). فرجعنا بهما، فدفناهما حيث قُتلا.
فبينما أنا في خلافة معاوية بن أبي سفيان إذ جاءني رجل فقال: يا جابر بن عبد الله، والله لقد أثار أباك عمَّالُ معاوية، فبدا، فخرج طائفة منه، فأتيته فوجدته على النحو الذي دفنته، لم يتغير إلا ما لم يدعِ القتل - أو القتيل - فواريته.
قال: وترك أبي عليه دينا من التمر، فاشتد علي بعض غرمائه في التقاضي، فأتيت نبي الله ﷺ فقلت: يا نبي الله، إن أبي أصيب يوم كذا وكذا، وترك عليه دينا من التمر، وقد اشتد علي بعض غرمائه في التقاضي، فأحب أن تعينني عليه، لعله أن ينظرني طائفة من تمره إلى هذا الصرام المقبل.
فقال: ((نعم، آتيك إن شاء الله قريبًا من وسط النهار)).
وجاء معه حواريوه، ثم استأذن، فدخل، وقد قلت لامرأتي: إن النبي ﷺ جاءني اليوم قريبًا من وسط النهار، فلا أرينك، ولا تؤذي رسول الله ﷺ في بيتي بشيء، ولا تكلميه.
فدخل، ففرشت له فراشًا ووسادة، فوضع رأسه فنام، قال: وقلت لمولى لي: اذبح هذه العناق - وهي داجن سمينة - والوَحَى، والعَجَل، افرغ منها قبل أن يستيقظ رسول الله ﷺ وأنا معك.
فلم نزل فيها حتى فرغنا منها، وهو نائم، فقلت له: إن رسول الله ﷺ إذا استيقظ يدعو بالطهور، وإني أخاف إذا فرغ أن يقوم، فلا يفرغن من وضوئه حتى تضع العناق بين يديه.
فلما قام قال: ((يا جابر، ائتني بطهور)). فلم يفرغ من طهوره حتى وضعت العناق عنده، فنظر إلي فقال: ((كأنك قد علمت حبنا للحم، ادع لي أبا بكر)).
قال: ثم دعا حوارييه الذين معه، فدخلوا، فضرب رسول الله ﷺ بيديه وقال: ((بسم الله، كلوا)). فأكلوا حتى شبعوا، وفضل لحم منها كثير.
قال: والله إن مجلس بني سلمة لينظرون إليه، وهو أحب إليهم من أعينهم، ما يقربه رجل منهم مخافة أن يؤذوه.
فلما فرغوا قام، وقام أصحابه، فخرجوا بين يديه، وكان يقول: ((خلوا ظهري للملائكة)).
واتبعتهم حتى بلغوا أسكفة الباب، قال: وأخرجت امرأتي صدرها، وكانت مستترة بسقيفة في البيت، فقالت: يا رسول الله، صلِّ عليَّ، وعلى زوجي، صلى الله عليك.
فقال: ((اللهم صلِّ عليها، وعلى زوجها)).
ثم قال: ((ادع لي فلانًا))، لغريمي الذي اشتد عليَّ في الطلب.
قال: فجاء، فقال: ((أخِّر جاري عبد الله - يعني إلى الميسرة - طائفةً من دينك الذي على أبيه، إلى هذا الصرام المقبل)).
قال: ما أنا بفاعل، واعتلَّ، وقال: إنما هو مال يتامى.
فقال: ((أين جابر؟))
فقال: أنا ذا يا رسول الله.
قال: ((كِلْ له، فإن الله سوف يوفيه)).
فنظرت إلى السماء، فإذا الشمس قد دلكت، قال: ((الصلاة يا أبا بكر)).
فاندفعوا إلى المسجد، فقلت: قرِّب أوعيتك.
فكلت له من العجوة، فوفاه الله، وفضل لنا من التمر كذا وكذا.
فجئت أسعى إلى رسول الله ﷺ في مسجده، كأني شرارة، فوجدت رسول الله ﷺ قد صلى.
قلت: يا رسول الله، ألم تر أني كلت لغريمي تمره، فوفاه الله، وفضل لنا من التمر كذا وكذا؟
فقال: ((أين عمر بن الخطاب؟))
فجاء يهرول.
فقال: ((سل جابر بن عبد الله عن غريمه وتمره)).
فقال: ما أنا بسائله، قد علمت أن الله سوف يوفيه، إذ أخبرت أن الله سوف يوفيه.
فكرر عليه هذه الكلمة ثلاث مرات، كل ذلك يقول: ما أنا بسائله، وكان لا يراجع بعد المرة الثالثة.
فقال: ((يا جابر، ما فعل غريمك وتمرك؟))
قال: قلت: وفاه الله، وفضل لنا من التمر كذا وكذا.
فرجع إلى امرأته، فقال: ألم أكن نهيتك أن تكلمي رسول الله ﷺ؟
قالت: أكنت تظن أن الله يورد رسول الله ﷺ بيتي، ثم يخرج، ولا أسأله الصلاة عليَّ، وعلى زوجي، قبل أن يخرج؟
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٥٢٨١)، وأبو داود (١٥٣٣)، وصححه ابن حبان (٩١٦، ٩٨٤).
وقوله: ((والوَحَى، والعَجَل)) أي: السرعة، السرعة.

وجاء معه حواريوه، ثم استأذن، فدخل، وقد قلت لامرأتي: إن النبي ﷺ جاءني اليوم قريبًا من وسط النهار، فلا أرينك، ولا تؤذي رسول الله ﷺ في بيتي بشيء، ولا تكلميه.
فدخل، ففرشت له فراشًا ووسادة، فوضع رأسه فنام، قال: وقلت لمولى لي: اذبح هذه العناق - وهي داجن سمينة - والوَحَى، والعَجَل، افرغ منها قبل أن يستيقظ رسول الله ﷺ وأنا معك.
فلم نزل فيها حتى فرغنا منها، وهو نائم، فقلت له: إن رسول الله ﷺ إذا استيقظ يدعو بالطهور، وإني أخاف إذا فرغ أن يقوم، فلا يفرغن من وضوئه حتى تضع العناق بين يديه.
فلما قام قال: ((يا جابر، ائتني بطهور)). فلم يفرغ من طهوره حتى وضعت العناق عنده، فنظر إلي فقال: ((كأنك قد علمت حبنا للحم، ادع لي أبا بكر)).
قال: ثم دعا حوارييه الذين معه، فدخلوا، فضرب رسول الله ﷺ بيديه وقال: ((بسم الله، كلوا)). فأكلوا حتى شبعوا، وفضل لحم منها كثير.
قال: والله إن مجلس بني سلمة لينظرون إليه، وهو أحب إليهم من أعينهم، ما يقربه رجل منهم مخافة أن يؤذوه.
فلما فرغوا قام، وقام أصحابه، فخرجوا بين يديه، وكان يقول: ((خلوا ظهري للملائكة)).
واتبعتهم حتى بلغوا أسكفة الباب، قال: وأخرجت امرأتي صدرها، وكانت مستترة بسقيفة في البيت، فقالت: يا رسول الله، صلِّ عليَّ، وعلى زوجي، صلى الله عليك.
فقال: ((اللهم صلِّ عليها، وعلى زوجها)).
ثم قال: ((ادع لي فلانًا))، لغريمي الذي اشتد عليَّ في الطلب.
قال: فجاء، فقال: ((أخِّر جاري عبد الله - يعني إلى الميسرة - طائفةً من دينك الذي على أبيه، إلى هذا الصرام المقبل)).
قال: ما أنا بفاعل، واعتلَّ، وقال: إنما هو مال يتامى.
فقال: ((أين جابر؟))
فقال: أنا ذا يا رسول الله.
قال: ((كِلْ له، فإن الله سوف يوفيه)).
فنظرت إلى السماء، فإذا الشمس قد دلكت، قال: ((الصلاة يا أبا بكر)).
فاندفعوا إلى المسجد، فقلت: قرِّب أوعيتك.
فكلت له من العجوة، فوفاه الله، وفضل لنا من التمر كذا وكذا.
فجئت أسعى إلى رسول الله ﷺ في مسجده، كأني شرارة، فوجدت رسول الله ﷺ قد صلى.
قلت: يا رسول الله، ألم تر أني كلت لغريمي تمره، فوفاه الله، وفضل لنا من التمر كذا وكذا؟
فقال: ((أين عمر بن الخطاب؟))
فجاء يهرول.
فقال: ((سل جابر بن عبد الله عن غريمه وتمره)).
فقال: ما أنا بسائله، قد علمت أن الله سوف يوفيه، إذ أخبرت أن الله سوف يوفيه.
فكرر عليه هذه الكلمة ثلاث مرات، كل ذلك يقول: ما أنا بسائله، وكان لا يراجع بعد المرة الثالثة.
فقال: ((يا جابر، ما فعل غريمك وتمرك؟))
قال: قلت: وفاه الله، وفضل لنا من التمر كذا وكذا.
فرجع إلى امرأته، فقال: ألم أكن نهيتك أن تكلمي رسول الله ﷺ؟
قالت: أكنت تظن أن الله يورد رسول الله ﷺ بيتي، ثم يخرج، ولا أسأله الصلاة عليَّ، وعلى زوجي، قبل أن يخرج؟
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٥٢٨١)، وأبو داود (١٥٣٣)، وصححه ابن حبان (٩١٦، ٩٨٤).
وقوله: ((والوَحَى، والعَجَل)) أي: السرعة، السرعة.
10258 — Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out from Madinah to fight the polytheists.
My father, ʿAbdullāh, said to me:
“O Jābir, it is your duty to remain among those watching over the people of Madinah until you learn what becomes of us. For by Allah, were it not that I would leave daughters behind after me, I would have loved for you to be killed before me.”
He said:
While I was among those keeping watch, my paternal aunt came with my father, and my maternal uncle. They had placed them equally upon a camel used for drawing water.
She entered Madinah with them so that she might bury them in our graveyards.
Then a man caught up with them, calling out:
“Indeed, the Prophet ﷺ commands you to return with those who have been killed and bury them where they were killed.”
So we returned with them and buried them where they had been killed.
Then, during the caliphate of Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān, a man came to me and said:
“O Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh, by Allah, the workers of Muʿāwiyah have uncovered your father.”
Part of his body became exposed.
So I went to him and found him in the same condition in which I had buried him. Nothing had changed except what the killing—or the slain body—had left unchanged.
So I buried him again.
He said:
My father left behind a debt that was to be paid in dates.
Some of his creditors became severe with me in demanding repayment.
So I went to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Prophet of Allah, my father was killed on such-and-such a day, and he left behind a debt to be paid in dates. Some of his creditors have become severe with me in demanding repayment. I would like you to help me with them, so that perhaps they may defer part of the payment until the coming date harvest.”
He said:
“Yes. I shall come to you, if Allah wills, around the middle of the day.”
His close companions came with him.
He sought permission to enter, and he entered.
I had already said to my wife:
“The Prophet ﷺ is coming to me today around the middle of the day. I do not want him to see you. Do not do anything in my house that may offend the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and do not speak to him.”
He entered, and I spread out bedding and a pillow for him.
He placed his head down and went to sleep.
I said to one of my servants:
“Slaughter this young she-goat—it is a fat domesticated one—and quickly, quickly, finish preparing it before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wakes up, and I will help you.”
We continued preparing it until we had finished, while he was still asleep.
I said to him:
“When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wakes up, he will ask for water for purification. I fear that once he finishes, he will stand up. So do not let him complete his ablution until you have placed the young goat before him.”
When he got up, he said:
“O Jābir, bring me water for purification.”
Before he had finished his purification, I placed the young goat before him.
He looked at me and said:
“It is as though you knew of our love for meat. Call Abū Bakr for me.”
He then called those of his close companions who were with him, and they entered.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck his hands together and said:
“In the Name of Allah. Eat.”
They ate until they were satisfied, and a great amount of the meat remained.
He said:
By Allah, the gathering-place of Banū Salamah kept looking toward it. It was more beloved to them than their own eyes, yet none of them came near it for fear of causing inconvenience.
When they had finished, the Prophet ﷺ stood up, and his companions also stood up.
They went out ahead of him.
He used to say:
“Leave my back for the angels.”
I followed them until they reached the threshold of the door.
My wife uncovered her face from behind a screen in the house and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, pray for me and for my husband. May Allah send blessings upon you.”
He said:
“O Allah, send blessings upon her and upon her husband.”
Then he said:
“Call so-and-so for me,”
meaning my creditor who had become severe in demanding payment from me.
He came, and the Prophet ﷺ said:
“Give my neighbor, ʿAbdullāh”—meaning until he is able to pay—“a postponement for part of the debt that his father owes you until this coming date harvest.”
He replied:
“I will not do that.”
He offered an excuse and said:
“It is only the property of orphans.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Where is Jābir?”
I replied:
“Here I am, O Messenger of Allah.”
He said:
“Measure out for him, for Allah will surely repay it in full.”
I looked toward the sky, and the sun had begun to decline.
He said:
“The prayer, O Abū Bakr.”
They then proceeded to the mosque.
I said:
“Bring your containers near.”
So I measured out the ʿajwah dates for him.
Allah repaid him in full, and there remained for us such-and-such an amount of dates.
Then I hurried to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his mosque, as though I were a spark.
I found that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had already prayed.
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, have you not seen that I measured out the dates for my creditor, Allah repaid him in full, and there remained for us such-and-such an amount of dates?”
He said:
“Where is ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb?”
He came running.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Ask Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh about his creditor and his dates.”
ʿUmar replied:
“I will not ask him. I already know that Allah will repay him in full, since you informed us that Allah would repay him in full.”
He repeated this statement to him three times.
Each time, ʿUmar said:
“I will not ask him.”
He would not answer him again after the third time.
Then the Prophet ﷺ said:
“O Jābir, what happened with your creditor and your dates?”
I said:
“Allah repaid him in full, and there remained for us such-and-such an amount of dates.”
Then he returned to his wife and said:
“Did I not forbid you from speaking to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?”
She replied:
“Did you think that Allah would bring the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into my house and then let him leave before I asked him to pray for me and for my husband?”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (15281) and Abū Dāwūd (1533). It was authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (916, 984).
His statement, “al-waḥā, al-ʿajal,” means: haste, haste.

١٠٢٥٩ — عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص قال: كنت أصوم الدهر وأقرأ القرآن كل ليلة، قال: فإما ذُكرت للنبي ﷺ، وإما أرسل إليَّ فأتيته، فقال لي: ((ألم أُخبر أنك تصوم الدهر وتقرأ القرآن كل ليلة؟)). قلت: بلى يا نبي الله، ولم أرد بذلك إلا الخير. قال: ((فصم صوم ثلاثة أيام)). قلت: يا نبي الله، إني أطيق أفضل من ذلك. قال: ((فإن لزوجك عليك حقا، ولزورك عليك حقا، ولجسدك عليك حقا)). قال: ((فصم صوم داود نبي الله، فإنه كان أعبد الناس)). قال: قلت: يا نبي الله، وما صوم داود؟ قال: ((كان يصوم يوما ويفطر يوما)). قال: ((واقرأ القرآن في كل شهر)). قال: قلت: يا نبي الله، إني أطيق أفضل من ذلك. قال: ((فاقرأه في كل عشرين)). قال: قلت: يا نبي الله، إني أطيق أفضل من ذلك. قال: ((فاقرأه في كل عشر)). قال: قلت: يا نبي الله، إني أطيق أفضل من ذلك. قال: ((فاقرأه في كل سبع، ولا تزد على ذلك، فإن لزوجك عليك حقا، ولزورك عليك حقا، ولجسدك عليك حقا)). قال: فشددت، فشدد علي، وقال لي النبي ﷺ: ((إنك لا تدري لعلك يطول بك عمر)). قال: فصرت إلى الذي قال لي النبي ﷺ، فلما كبرت وددت أن كنت قبلت رخصة نبي الله ﷺ.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٩٧٥)، ومسلم (١١٥٩/١٢٨).

10259 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said:
I used to fast every day and recite the Qur’an every night.
He said:
Either news of that reached the Prophet ﷺ, or he sent for me, and I came to him.
He said to me:
“Have I not been informed that you fast every day and recite the Qur’an every night?”
I said:
“Yes, O Prophet of Allah, and I intended nothing by that except good.”
He said:
“Then fast three days.”
I said:
“O Prophet of Allah, I am able to do more than that.”
He said:
“Your wife has a right over you, your visitor has a right over you, and your body has a right over you.”
He said:
“Then observe the fast of Dāwūd, the Prophet of Allah, for he was the most devoted of people in worship.”
I said:
“O Prophet of Allah, what was the fast of Dāwūd?”
He said:
“He would fast one day and break the fast the next day.”
He said:
“Recite the Qur’an once every month.”
I said:
“O Prophet of Allah, I am able to do more than that.”
He said:
“Then recite it once every twenty days.”
I said:
“O Prophet of Allah, I am able to do more than that.”
He said:
“Then recite it once every ten days.”
I said:
“O Prophet of Allah, I am able to do more than that.”
He said:
“Then recite it once every seven days, and do not exceed that. Your wife has a right over you, your visitor has a right over you, and your body has a right over you.”
He said:
I insisted on doing more, so it was made stricter for me.
The Prophet ﷺ also said to me:
“You do not know; perhaps your life will be long.”
He said:
So I eventually followed what the Prophet ﷺ had told me.
When I grew old, I wished that I had accepted the concession of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1975) and Muslim (1159/128).

١٠٢٥٩ — عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص قال: كنت أصوم الدهر وأقرأ القرآن كل ليلة، قال: فإما ذُكرت للنبي ﷺ، وإما أرسل إليَّ فأتيته، فقال لي: ((ألم أُخبر أنك تصوم الدهر وتقرأ القرآن كل ليلة؟)). قلت: بلى يا نبي الله، ولم أرد بذلك إلا الخير. قال: ((فصم صوم ثلاثة أيام)). قلت: يا نبي الله، إني أطيق أفضل من ذلك. قال: ((فإن لزوجك عليك حقا، ولزورك عليك حقا، ولجسدك عليك حقا)). قال: ((فصم صوم داود نبي الله، فإنه كان أعبد الناس)). قال: قلت: يا نبي الله، وما صوم داود؟ قال: ((كان يصوم يوما ويفطر يوما)). قال: ((واقرأ القرآن في كل شهر)). قال: قلت: يا نبي الله، إني أطيق أفضل من ذلك. قال: ((فاقرأه في كل عشرين)). قال: قلت: يا نبي الله، إني أطيق أفضل من ذلك. قال: ((فاقرأه في كل عشر)). قال: قلت: يا نبي الله، إني أطيق أفضل من ذلك. قال: ((فاقرأه في كل سبع، ولا تزد على ذلك، فإن لزوجك عليك حقا، ولزورك عليك حقا، ولجسدك عليك حقا)). قال: فشددت، فشدد علي، وقال لي النبي ﷺ: ((إنك لا تدري لعلك يطول بك عمر)). قال: فصرت إلى الذي قال لي النبي ﷺ، فلما كبرت وددت أن كنت قبلت رخصة نبي الله ﷺ.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (١٩٧٥)، ومسلم (١١٥٩/١٢٨).
10259 — ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said:
I used to fast every day and recite the Qur’an every night.
He said:
Either news of that reached the Prophet ﷺ, or he sent for me, and I came to him.
He said to me:
“Have I not been informed that you fast every day and recite the Qur’an every night?”
I said:
“Yes, O Prophet of Allah, and I intended nothing by that except good.”
He said:
“Then fast three days.”
I said:
“O Prophet of Allah, I am able to do more than that.”
He said:
“Your wife has a right over you, your visitor has a right over you, and your body has a right over you.”
He said:
“Then observe the fast of Dāwūd, the Prophet of Allah, for he was the most devoted of people in worship.”
I said:
“O Prophet of Allah, what was the fast of Dāwūd?”
He said:
“He would fast one day and break the fast the next day.”
He said:
“Recite the Qur’an once every month.”
I said:
“O Prophet of Allah, I am able to do more than that.”
He said:
“Then recite it once every twenty days.”
I said:
“O Prophet of Allah, I am able to do more than that.”
He said:
“Then recite it once every ten days.”
I said:
“O Prophet of Allah, I am able to do more than that.”
He said:
“Then recite it once every seven days, and do not exceed that. Your wife has a right over you, your visitor has a right over you, and your body has a right over you.”
He said:
I insisted on doing more, so it was made stricter for me.
The Prophet ﷺ also said to me:
“You do not know; perhaps your life will be long.”
He said:
So I eventually followed what the Prophet ﷺ had told me.
When I grew old, I wished that I had accepted the concession of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1975) and Muslim (1159/128).

١٠٢٦٠ — عن أبي هريرة قال: ما من أصحاب النبي ﷺ أحد أكثر حديثا عنه مني إلا ما كان من عبد الله بن عمرو، فإنه كان يكتب ولا أكتب.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (١١٣).

١٠٢٦١ — عن عبد الله قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ جُنَاحٌ فِيمَا طَعِمُوا إِذَا مَا اتَّقَوْا وَآمَنُوا﴾ [المائدة: ٩٣] إلى آخر الآية، قال لي رسول الله ﷺ: ((أنت منهم)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤٥٩).

10261 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said:
When this verse was revealed:
“There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have consumed, provided they fear Allah, believe…” until the end of the verse.
 (Sūrat al-Mā’idah 5:93)
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me:
“You are among them.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2459).

١٠٢٦٢ — عن قيس بن مروان أنه أتى عمر فقال: جئت يا أمير المؤمنين من الكوفة، وتركت بها رجلاً يملي المصاحف عن ظهر قلبه، فغضب وانتفخ حتى كاد يملأ ما بين شعبتي الرحل، قال: ومن هو ويحك؟ قال: عبد الله بن مسعود، فما زال يطفأ ويسرى عنه الغضب حتى عاد إلى حاله التي كان عليها.
ثم قال: ويحك، والله ما أعلمه بقي من الناس أحد هو أحق بذلك منه، وسأحدثك عن ذلك.
كان رسول الله ﷺ لا يزال يسمر عند أبي بكر الليلة كذلك في الأمر من أمر المسلمين، وإنه سمر عنده ذات ليلة وأنا معه، فخرج رسول الله ﷺ وخرجنا معه، فإذا رجل قائم يصلي في المسجد، فقام رسول الله ﷺ يستمع قراءته، فلما كدنا أن نعرفه قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((من سره أن يقرأ القرآن رطباً كما أنزل فليقرأه على قراءة ابن أم عبد)).
قال: ثم جلس الرجل يدعو، فجعل رسول الله ﷺ يقول له: ((سل تعط، سل تعط)).
قال عمر: قلت: والله لأغدون إليه فلأبشرنه.
قال: فغدوت إليه لأبشره، فوجدت أبا بكر قد سبقني إليه فبشره، ولا والله ما سابقته إلى خير قط إلا سبقني إليه.
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٧٥)، وأبو يعلى (١/١٢٢ رقم ١٨٩) (تحقيق الأثري).

10262 — Qays ibn Marwān narrated that he came to ʿUmar and said:
“O Commander of the Believers, I have come from Kūfah, where I left a man dictating copies of the Qur’an entirely from memory.”
ʿUmar became angry, and his anger swelled until it seemed to fill the space between the two sides of his saddle.
He said:
“Who is he? Woe to you!”
The man replied:
“ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd.”
Then ʿUmar’s anger gradually subsided until he returned to his normal state.
He then said:
“Woe to you! By Allah, I do not know of anyone still living who is more deserving of that than him. Let me tell you why.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would often spend part of the night with Abū Bakr discussing matters concerning the Muslims.
One night he stayed with him, and I was with them.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then left, and we left with him.
There was a man standing in the mosque praying.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood listening to his recitation.
When we were about to recognize who he was, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever wishes to recite the Qur’an fresh as it was revealed, let him recite according to the recitation of Ibn Umm ʿAbd.”
He said:
The man then sat making supplication.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept saying to him:
“Ask, and you will be given. Ask, and you will be given.”
ʿUmar said:
“By Allah, I will go to him in the morning and give him this glad tiding.”
He said:
I went to him the next morning to give him the good news, but I found that Abū Bakr had reached him before me and had already informed him.
By Allah, I never raced Abū Bakr to any good deed except that he reached it before me.
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (175) and Abū Yaʿlā (1/122, no. 189), in the edition edited by al-Atharī.

“O Commander of the Believers, I have come from Kūfah, where I left a man dictating copies of the Qur’an entirely from memory.”
ʿUmar became angry, and his anger swelled until it seemed to fill the space between the two sides of his saddle.
He said:
“Who is he? Woe to you!”
The man replied:
“ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd.”
Then ʿUmar’s anger gradually subsided until he returned to his normal state.
He then said:
“Woe to you! By Allah, I do not know of anyone still living who is more deserving of that than him. Let me tell you why.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would often spend part of the night with Abū Bakr discussing matters concerning the Muslims.
One night he stayed with him, and I was with them.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then left, and we left with him.
There was a man standing in the mosque praying.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood listening to his recitation.
When we were about to recognize who he was, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Whoever wishes to recite the Qur’an fresh as it was revealed, let him recite according to the recitation of Ibn Umm ʿAbd.”
He said:
The man then sat making supplication.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept saying to him:
“Ask, and you will be given. Ask, and you will be given.”
ʿUmar said:
“By Allah, I will go to him in the morning and give him this glad tiding.”
He said:
I went to him the next morning to give him the good news, but I found that Abū Bakr had reached him before me and had already informed him.
By Allah, I never raced Abū Bakr to any good deed except that he reached it before me.
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (175) and Abū Yaʿlā (1/122, no. 189), in the edition edited by al-Atharī.

١٠٢٦٣ — عن علي قال: كنت مع النبي ﷺ ومعه أبو بكر ومن شاء من أصحابه، فمررنا بعبد الله بن مسعود وهو يصلي، فقال النبي ﷺ: ((من هذا؟)) فقيل: عبد الله بن مسعود، فقال: ((إن عبد الله يقرأ القرآن غضًّا كما أنزل)). فأثنى عبد الله على ربه وحمده، فأحسن في حمده على ربه، ثم سأله فأجمل المسألة، وسأله كأحسن مسألة سألها عبد ربه، ثم قال: ((اللهم إني أسألك إيمانًا لا يرتد، ونعيمًا لا ينفد، ومرافقة نبيك محمد ﷺ في أعلى عليين في جنات الخلد)). قال: وكان رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((سل تعط، سل تعط)). مرتين، فانطلقت لأبشره، فوجدت أبا بكر قد سبقني، وكان سباقًا للخير.
صحيح: رواه الحاكم (٣/٣١٧).

١٠٢٦٥ — عن قرة بن إياس أن عبد الله بن مسعود رقي في شجرة يجتني منها سواكًا، فوضع رجليه عليها، فضحك أصحاب النبي ﷺ من دقة ساقيه، فقال رسول الله ﷺ لهم: ((أثقل في الميزان من أحد)).
حسن: رواه البزار (٣٣٠٥)، والطبراني في الكبير (١٩/٢٨)، وصححه الحاكم (٣/٣١٧).

10265 — Qurrah ibn Iyās narrated:
ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd climbed a tree to gather twigs for using as siwāk.
As he climbed, his legs became visible.
The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ laughed because of how thin his shins were.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them:
“They are heavier on the Scale than Mount Uḥud.”
Good: Narrated by al-Bazzār (3305) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (19/28). It was authenticated by al-Ḥākim (3/317).

١٠٢٦٦ — عن أبي موسى الأشعري يقول: قدمت أنا وأخي من اليمن، فمكثنا حينًا، ما نرى إلا أن عبد الله بن مسعود رجل من أهل بيت النبي ﷺ، لما نرى من دخوله ودخول أمه على النبي ﷺ.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٧٦٣)، ومسلم (٢٤٦٠/١١٠).

10266 — Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī said:
My brother and I came from Yemen.
We stayed for some time, and we thought that ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd was one of the members of the Prophet’s ﷺ household because we so often saw him and his mother entering upon the Prophet ﷺ.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3763) and Muslim (2460/110).

١٠٢٦٧ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: خرج رسول الله ﷺ في أضحى أو فطر إلى المصلى، ثم انصرف فوعظ الناس وأمرهم بالصدقة فقال: ((أيها الناس، تصدقوا)). فمر على النساء فقال: ((يا معشر النساء، تصدقن، فإني رأيتكن أكثر أهل النار)). فقلن: وبم ذلك يا رسول الله؟ قال: ((تكثرن اللعن، وتكفرن العشير، ما رأيت من ناقصات عقل ودين أذهب للبِّ الرجل الحازم من إحداكن يا معشر النساء)). ثم انصرف، فلما صار إلى منزله جاءت زينب امرأة ابن مسعود تستأذن عليه، فقيل: يا رسول الله، هذه زينب. فقال: ((أي الزيانب؟)) فقيل: امرأة ابن مسعود. قال: ((نعم، ائذنوا لها)). فأذن لها، فقالت: يا نبي الله، إنك أمرت اليوم بالصدقة، وكان عندي حليٌّ لي فأردت أن أتصدق بها، فزعم ابن مسعود أنه وولده أحق من تصدقت به عليهم. فقال النبي ﷺ: ((صدق ابن مسعود، زوجك وولدك أحق من تصدقت به عليهم)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٤٦٢).

10267 — Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on the day of al-Aḍḥā or al-Fiṭr to the prayer place.
After finishing, he turned to the people, admonished them, and instructed them to give charity, saying:
“O people, give charity.”
He then passed by the women and said:
“O gathering of women, give charity, for I have seen that you make up the majority of the people of the Fire.”
They asked:
“Why is that, O Messenger of Allah?”
He replied:
“You frequently curse, and you are ungrateful to your husbands. I have not seen anyone more capable of taking away the understanding of a resolute man than one of you, despite being deficient in intellect and religion, O gathering of women.”
He then departed.
When he reached his house, Zaynab, the wife of Ibn Masʿūd, came seeking permission to enter.
It was said:
“O Messenger of Allah, this is Zaynab.”
He asked:
“Which Zaynab?”
They replied:
“The wife of Ibn Masʿūd.”
He said:
“Yes, give her permission.”
She entered and said:
“O Prophet of Allah, today you commanded us to give charity. I had some jewelry of my own and wanted to give it in charity, but Ibn Masʿūd claims that he and his children have a greater right to receive my charity.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Ibn Masʿūd has spoken the truth. Your husband and your children have a greater right to receive your charity.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (1462).

١٠٢٦٨ — عن أبي الأحوص قال: كنا في دار أبي موسى مع نفر من أصحاب عبد الله، وهم ينظرون في مصحف، فقام عبد الله، فقال أبو مسعود: ما أعلم رسول الله ﷺ ترك بعده أعلم بما أنزل الله من هذا القائم. فقال أبو موسى: أما لئن قلت ذاك، لقد كان يؤذن له إذا حجبنا، ويشهد إذا غبنا.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٤٦١/١١٣).
وفي لفظ مسلم (٢٤٦١/١١٢): “شهدت أبا موسى وأبا مسعود حين مات ابن مسعود، فقال أحدهما لصاحبه: أتراه ترك بعده مثله؟ فقال: إن قلت ذاك، إن كان ليؤذن له إذا حجبنا، ويشهد إذا غبنا.”
وفي لفظ مسلم (٢٤٦١/١١٣): “كنت جالسًا مع حذيفة وأبي موسى…”

10268 — Abū al-Aḥwaṣ said:
We were in the house of Abū Mūsā with a group of the companions of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, and they were looking through a copy of the Qur’an.
Then ʿAbdullāh stood up.
Abū Masʿūd said:
“I do not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left behind anyone more knowledgeable about what Allah revealed than this man who has just stood up.”
Abū Mūsā said:
“If you say that, then indeed he used to be granted permission to enter when we were kept outside, and he would be present when we were absent.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2461/113).
Another wording in Muslim (2461/112):
“I was present with Abū Mūsā and Abū Masʿūd when Ibn Masʿūd passed away. One of them said to the other: ‘Do you think he has left behind anyone like him?’ The other replied: ‘If you say that, then indeed he used to be granted permission to enter when we were kept outside, and he would be present when we were absent.’”
Another wording in Muslim (2461/113):
“I was sitting with Ḥudhayfah and Abū Mūsā…”

١٠٢٦٩ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: والذي لا إله غيره، ما من كتاب الله سورة إلا أنا أعلم حيث نزلت، وما من آية إلا أنا أعلم فيما أنزلت، ولو أعلم أحداً هو أعلم بكتاب الله مني، تبلغه الإبل، لركبت إليه.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٠٠٢)، ومسلم (٢٤٦٣). وهذا لفظ مسلم، ولفظ البخاري نحوه.

10269 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said:
“By Him besides Whom there is no deity worthy of worship, there is no sūrah in the Book of Allah except that I know where it was revealed, and there is no verse except that I know concerning what it was revealed. If I knew of anyone more knowledgeable than I am regarding the Book of Allah, and the camels could reach him, I would ride to him.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5002) and Muslim (2463). This is the wording of Muslim, while the wording of al-Bukhārī is similar.

١٠٢٧٠ — عن عبد الله بن مسعود أنه قال: ﴿وَمَن يَغْلُلْ يَأْتِ بِمَا غَلَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾ [آل عمران: ١٦١]. ثم قال: على قراءة من تأمروني أن أقرأ؟ فلقد قرأت على رسول الله ﷺ بضعاً وسبعين سورة، ولقد علم أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ أني أعلمهم بكتاب الله، ولو أعلم أن أحداً أعلم مني لرحلت إليه.
قال شقيق: فجلست في حلق أصحاب محمد ﷺ، فما سمعت أحداً يرد ذلك عليه، ولا يعيبه.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٠٠٠)، ومسلم (٢٤٦٢).

10270 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said regarding the verse:
“And whoever betrays, will come with what he betrayed on the Day of Resurrection.”
 (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:161)
Then he said:
“According to whose recitation do you command me to recite? I recited more than seventy sūrahs directly to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ know that I am the most knowledgeable among them regarding the Book of Allah. If I knew that anyone was more knowledgeable than I am, I would travel to him.”
Shaqīq said:
I sat in the study circles of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ, and I did not hear any one of them reject what he said or criticize him for it.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5000) and Muslim (2462).

١٠٢٧١ — عن عبد الرحمن بن يزيد قال: سألنا حذيفة عن رجل قريب السمت والهدي من النبي ﷺ حتى نأخذ عنه، فقال: ما أعرف أحداً أقرب سمتاً وهدياً، ودلاً بالنبي ﷺ من ابن أم عبد.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٧٦٢).
وفي لفظ: “إن أشبه الناس دلاً وسمتاً، وهدياً برسول الله ﷺ لابن أم عبد، من حين يخرج من بيته إلى أن يرجع إليه، لا ندري ما يصنع في أهله إذا خلا”. رواه البخاري (٦٠٩٧).

10271 — ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd said:
We asked Ḥudhayfah about a man whose manner, guidance, and conduct most closely resembled that of the Prophet ﷺ so that we could learn from him.
He said:
“I do not know anyone whose manner, guidance, and conduct more closely resemble those of the Prophet ﷺ than Ibn Umm ʿAbd.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3762).
Another wording:
“The person who most closely resembled the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in demeanor, manner, and guidance was Ibn Umm ʿAbd, from the time he left his house until he returned to it. As for what he did with his family when he was alone with them, we did not know.”
Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6097).

١٠٢٧٢ — عن عمر بن الخطاب أن رجلاً كان على عهد النبي ﷺ كان اسمه عبد الله، وكان يلقب حماراً، وكان يضحك رسول الله ﷺ، وكان النبي ﷺ قد جلده في الشراب، فأتي به يوماً فأمر فجلد، فقال رجل من القوم: اللهم العنه، ما أكثر ما يؤتى به! فقال النبي ﷺ: ((لا تلعنوه، فوالله ما علمت إلا أنه يحب الله ورسوله)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٧٨٠).

10272 — ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb narrated:
During the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ there was a man named ʿAbdullāh, who was nicknamed al-Ḥimār (the Donkey). He used to make the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laugh.
The Prophet ﷺ had previously punished him for drinking alcohol.
One day he was brought again, and the Prophet ﷺ ordered that he be punished.
A man among the people said:
“O Allah, curse him! How often he is brought for this!”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Do not curse him. For by Allah, all that I know of him is that he loves Allah and His Messenger.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6780).

١٠٢٧٣ — عن عقبة بن عامر أن النبي ﷺ قال لرجل يقال له: ذو البجادين: ((إنه أواه)). وذلك أنه كان رجلاً كثير الذكر لله عز وجل في القرآن، ويرفع صوته في الدعاء.
حسن: رواه أحمد (١٧٤٥٣)، والطبراني في الكبير (١٧/٢٩٥).

10273 — ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said about a man known as Dhū al-Bijādayn:
“Indeed, he is awwāh (deeply humble, frequently supplicating, and devoted to Allah).”
This was because he was a man who remembered Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, abundantly while reciting the Qur’an, and he would raise his voice in supplication.
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (17453) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (17/295).

١٠٢٧٤ — عن عتاب بن أسيد قال: ما أصبت في عملي الذي استعملني عليه رسول الله ﷺ إلا بُردين معقدين كسوتهما مولاي كيسان.
حسن: رواه أبو داود الطيالسي (١٤٥٣)، والطبراني في الكبير (٧/١٦١).

10274 — ʿAttāb ibn Usayd said:
“From the office to which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed me, I gained nothing except two striped garments, which my freedman Kaysān clothed me with.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī (1453) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (7/161).

حسن: رواه أبو داود الطيالسي (١٤٥٣)، والطبراني في الكبير (٧/١٦١).
10274 — ʿAttāb ibn Usayd said:
“From the office to which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed me, I gained nothing except two striped garments, which my freedman Kaysān clothed me with.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī (1453) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (7/161).

١٠٢٧٥ — عن عثمان بن أبي العاص الثقفي أن النبي ﷺ قال له: ((أمَّ قومك)). قال: قلت: يا رسول الله، إني أجد في نفسي شيئًا. قال: ((ادنُه)). فجلسني بين يديه، ثم وضع كفه في صدري بين ثدييَّ، ثم قال: ((تحوَّل)). فوضعها في ظهري بين كتفي، ثم قال: ((أمَّ قومك، فمن أمَّ قومًا فليخفف، فإن فيهم الكبير، وإن فيهم المريض، وإن فيهم الضعيف، وإن فيهم ذا الحاجة، وإذا صلى أحدكم وحده، فليصلِّ كيف شاء)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٤٦٨/١٨٦).

10275 — ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ al-Thaqafī narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said to him:
“Lead your people in prayer.”
He said:
“O Messenger of Allah, I feel something within myself.”
He said:
“Come near.”
He seated me in front of him, then placed his hand upon my chest between my breasts.
Then he said:
“Turn around.”
So he placed it upon my back between my shoulder blades.
Then he said:
“Lead your people in prayer. Whoever leads people in prayer should make it light, for among them are the elderly, the sick, the weak, and those who have needs. But when one of you prays alone, let him pray as long as he wishes.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (468/186).

١٠٢٧٦ — عن عثمان بن أبي العاص أنه أتى النبي ﷺ فقال: يا رسول الله، إن الشيطان قد حال بيني وبين صلاتي وقراءتي يلبسها عليَّ. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((ذاك شيطان يقال له خنزب، فإذا أحسسته فتعوذ بالله منه، واتفل على يسارك ثلاثًا)). قال: ففعلت ذلك فأذهبه الله عني.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٢٠٣).

10276 — ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ narrated that he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, Satan comes between me and my prayer and my recitation, confusing me.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“That is a devil called Khinzab. Whenever you sense his presence, seek refuge in Allah from him and spit lightly to your left three times.”
He said:
I did that, and Allah removed him from me.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2203).

10277 — ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ said:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed me over Ṭāʾif, something began to come over me during my prayer until I no longer knew what I was praying.
When I saw that happening, I traveled to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said:
“Ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ?”
I replied:
“Yes, O Messenger of Allah.”
He asked:
“What has brought you here?”
I said:
“O Messenger of Allah, something comes over me during my prayers until I no longer know what I am praying.”
He said:
“That is Satan. Come near.”
I came close to him and sat on the fronts of my feet.
He struck my chest with his hand, spat lightly into my mouth, and said:
“Come out, O enemy of Allah!”
He did this three times.
Then he said:
“Return to your work.”
ʿUthmān said:
By my life, I do not think that it ever troubled me again after that.
Good: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (3548) and al-Rūyānī in his Musnad (1515).

١٠٢٧٨ — عن أم العلاء، وهي امرأة من نسائهم بايعت رسول الله ﷺ، قالت: طار لنا عثمان بن مظعون في السكنى حين اقترعت الأنصار على سكنى المهاجرين، فاشتكى، فمرضناه حتى إذا توفي جعلناه في أثوابه، فدخل علينا رسول الله ﷺ، فقلت: رحمة الله عليك يا أبا السائب، فشهادتي عليك لقد أكرمك الله. قال: ((وما يدريك؟)). قلت: لا أدري والله. قال: ((أما هو فقد جاءه اليقين، وإني لأرجو له الخير من الله، والله ما أدري ـ وأنا رسول الله ـ ما يفعل بي ولا بكم)). قالت أم العلاء: فوالله لا أزكي أحدًا بعده. قالت: ورأيت لعثمان في النوم عينًا تجري، فجئت رسول الله ﷺ فذكرت ذلك له، فقال: ((ذاك عمله يجري له)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٧٠١٨).

10278 — Umm al-ʿAlāʾ, one of the women who had pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said:
When the Anṣār drew lots to determine which of them would host the Muhājirūn, ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn came to stay with us.
He fell ill, and we cared for him until he passed away.
After he died, we wrapped him in his garments.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us, and I said:
“May the mercy of Allah be upon you, O Abū al-Sāʾib. My testimony concerning you is that Allah has surely honored you.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“How do you know that?”
I replied:
“By Allah, I do not know.”

١٠٢٧٨ — عن أم العلاء، وهي امرأة من نسائهم بايعت رسول الله ﷺ، قالت: طار لنا عثمان بن مظعون في السكنى حين اقترعت الأنصار على سكنى المهاجرين، فاشتكى، فمرضناه حتى إذا توفي جعلناه في أثوابه، فدخل علينا رسول الله ﷺ، فقلت: رحمة الله عليك يا أبا السائب، فشهادتي عليك لقد أكرمك الله. قال: ((وما يدريك؟)). قلت: لا أدري والله. قال: ((أما هو فقد جاءه اليقين، وإني لأرجو له الخير من الله، والله ما أدري ـ وأنا رسول الله ـ ما يفعل بي ولا بكم)). قالت أم العلاء: فوالله لا أزكي أحدًا بعده. قالت: ورأيت لعثمان في النوم عينًا تجري، فجئت رسول الله ﷺ فذكرت ذلك له، فقال: ((ذاك عمله يجري له)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٧٠١٨).

١٠٢٧٩ — عن عدي بن حاتم قال: بينا أنا عند النبي ﷺ إذ أتاه رجل فشكا إليه الفاقة، ثم أتاه آخر فشكا قطع السبيل، فقال: ((يا عدي، هل رأيت الحيرة؟)). قلت: لم أرها، وقد أنبئت عنها. قال: ((فإن طالت بك الحياة، لترين الظعينة ترتحل من الحيرة، حتى تطوف بالكعبة لا تخاف من أحد إلا الله)). قلت فيما بيني وبين نفسي: فأين دُعَّار طيء الذين قد سَعَّروا في البلاد؟ ((ولئن طالت بك حياة لتفتحن كنوز كسرى)). قلت: كسرى بن هرمز؟ قال: ((كسرى بن هرمز، ولئن طالت بك حياة، لترين الرجل يخرج ملء كفه من ذهب أو فضة يطلب من يقبله منه فلا يجد أحدًا يقبله منه، وليلقين الله أحدكم يوم يلقاه وليس بينه وبينه ترجمان يترجم له، فيقولن: ألم أبعث إليك رسولًا يبلغك؟ فيقول: بلى. فيقول: ألم أعطك مالًا وولدًا وأفضل عليك؟ فيقول: بلى. فينظر عن يمينه فلا يرى إلا جهنم، وينظر عن يساره فلا يرى إلا جهنم)).
قال عدي: سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول: ((اتقوا النار ولو بشق تمرة، فمن لم يجد شق تمرة فبكلمة طيبة)).
قال عدي: فرأيت الظعينة ترتحل من الحيرة حتى تطوف بالكعبة لا تخاف إلا الله، وكنت فيمن افتتح كنوز كسرى بن هرمز، ولئن طالت بكم الحياة، لترون ما قال النبي أبو القاسم ﷺ: ((يخرج ملء كفه)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٥٩٥)، ومسلم (١٠١٦/٦٧).

10279 — ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim said:
While I was with the Prophet ﷺ, a man came to him complaining of poverty.
Then another man came complaining that the roads had become unsafe because of bandits.
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“O ʿAdī, have you seen al-Ḥīrah?”
I replied:
“I have not seen it, though I have heard about it.”
He said:
“If you live long enough, you will surely see a woman traveling from al-Ḥīrah until she circumambulates the Kaʿbah, fearing no one except Allah.”
I said to myself:
“Then where will the bandits of Ṭayyiʾ, who have spread corruption throughout the land, be?”
He continued:
“And if you live long enough, the treasures of Kisrā will surely be opened.”
I asked:
“Kisrā, the son of Hurmuz?”
He replied:
“Kisrā, the son of Hurmuz. And if you live long enough, you will surely see a man holding a handful of gold or silver, searching for someone to accept it from him, yet he will find no one to accept it. Every one of you will meet Allah on the Day he meets Him, with no interpreter between himself and Allah. Allah will say: ‘Did I not send you a messenger to convey My message to you?’ He will reply: ‘Yes.’ Allah will say: ‘Did I not give you wealth and children and bestow My favor upon you?’ He will reply: ‘Yes.’ Then he will look to his right and see nothing but Hellfire, and he will look to his left and see nothing but Hellfire.”
ʿAdī said:
I heard the Prophet ﷺ say:
“Protect yourselves from the Fire, even if only with half of a date. And whoever cannot find even half a date, then with a good word.”
ʿAdī said:
I indeed saw a woman travel from al-Ḥīrah until she circumambulated the Kaʿbah fearing none but Allah.
I was among those who conquered the treasures of Kisrā ibn Hurmuz.
And if you live long enough, you too will witness what Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ said:
‘A man will come out holding a handful (of wealth).’
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (3595) and Muslim (1016/67).

١٠٢٨٠ — عن عدي بن حاتم قال: أتينا عمر في وفد، فجعل يدعو رجلًا رجلًا ويسميهم، فقلت: أما تعرفني يا أمير المؤمنين؟ قال: بلى، أسلمت إذ كفروا، وأقبلت إذ أدبروا، ووفيت إذ غدروا، وعرفت إذ أنكروا. فقال عدي: فلا أبالي إذًا.

١٠٢٨١ — عن حصين بن عبد الرحمن قال: كنت عند سعيد بن جبير فقال: أيكم رأى الكوكب الذي انقض البارحة؟ قلت: أنا، ثم قلت: أما إني لم أكن في صلاة، ولكني لُدغت، قال: فماذا صنعت؟ قلت: استرقيت، قال: فما حملك على ذلك؟ قلت: حديث حدثناه الشعبي، فقال: وما حدثكم الشعبي؟ قلت: حدثنا عن بريدة بن الحصيب الأسلمي أنه قال: لا رقية إلا من عين أو حُمَة، فقال: قد أحسن من انتهى إلى ما سمع، ولكن حدثنا ابن عباس عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((عرضت علي الأمم، فرأيت النبي ومعه الرهيط، والنبي ومعه الرجل والرجلان، والنبي ليس معه أحد، إذ رفع لي سواد عظيم فظننت أنهم أمتي، فقيل لي: هذا موسى ﷺ وقومه، ولكن انظر إلى الأفق، فنظرت فإذا سواد عظيم، فقيل لي: انظر إلى الأفق الآخر، فإذا سواد عظيم، فقيل لي: هذه أمتك، ومعهم سبعون ألفًا يدخلون الجنة بغير حساب ولا عذاب)). ثم نهض فدخل منزله، فخاض الناس في أولئك الذين يدخلون الجنة بغير حساب ولا عذاب، فقال بعضهم: فلعلهم الذين صحبوا رسول الله ﷺ، وقال بعضهم: فلعلهم الذين ولدوا في الإسلام ولم يشركوا بالله، وذكروا أشياء، فخرج عليهم رسول الله ﷺ فقال: ((ما الذي تخوضون فيه؟)). فأخبروه، فقال: ((هم الذين لا يرقون، ولا يسترقون، ولا يتطيرون، وعلى ربهم يتوكلون)). فقام عكاشة بن محصن فقال: ادع الله أن يجعلني منهم، فقال: ((أنت منهم)). ثم قام رجل آخر فقال: ادع الله أن يجعلني منهم، فقال: ((سبقك بها عكاشة)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٥٤١)، ومسلم (٢٢٠).

10281 — Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said:
I was with Saʿīd ibn Jubayr when he asked:
“Which of you saw the shooting star that fell last night?”
I replied:
“I did.”
Then I added:
“But I was not praying at the time. Rather, I had been stung.”
He asked:
“What did you do?”
I said:
“I sought ruqyah (treatment through supplication).”
He asked:
“What led you to do that?”
I replied:
“A ḥadīth that al-Shaʿbī narrated to us.”
He asked:
“And what did al-Shaʿbī narrate to you?”
I said:
He narrated to us from Buraydah ibn al-Ḥuṣayb al-Aslamī that he said:
“There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a venomous sting.”
Saʿīd said:
“Whoever acts according to what he has heard has done well. However, Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to us from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:”
“The nations were presented before me. I saw a prophet with only a small group following him, another prophet with one or two men, and another prophet with no followers at all. Then a huge multitude was raised before me, and I thought they were my nation. But I was told: ‘This is Mūsā and his people. Rather, look toward the horizon.’ I looked and saw a great multitude. Then I was told: ‘Look toward the other horizon.’ There was another great multitude. Then I was told: ‘This is your nation, and among them are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning and without punishment.’”
Then the Prophet ﷺ stood up and entered his house.
The people began discussing who those people would be who would enter Paradise without reckoning or punishment.
Some said:
“Perhaps they are those who accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
Others said:
“Perhaps they are those who were born into Islam and never associated anything with Allah.”
They mentioned various possibilities.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out and said:
“What are you discussing?”
They informed him.
He said:
“They are those who do not perform ruqyah, do not seek ruqyah, do not believe in evil omens, and place their trust entirely in their Lord.”
Then ʿUkkāshah ibn Miḥṣan stood and said:
“Supplicate to Allah that He makes me one of them.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“You are one of them.”
Then another man stood and said:
“Supplicate to Allah that He makes me one of them.”
The Prophet ﷺ replied:
“ʿUkkāshah has preceded you in that.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6541) and Muslim (220).

قال: فإذا ظراب من ظراب مكة قد سدَّت وجوه الرجال، قلت: رب، من هؤلاء؟ قال: ((أمتك)).
قال: ((فقيل لي: رضيت؟)). قال: ((قلت: رب رضيت، رب رضيت)).
قال: ((ثم قيل لي: إن مع هؤلاء سبعين ألفًا يدخلون الجنة لا حساب عليهم)).
قال: فأنشأ عكاشة بن محصن أخو بني أسد بن خزيمة فقال: يا نبي الله، ادع ربك أن يجعلني منهم. قال: ((اللهم اجعله منهم)).

قال: فكبرنا.
ثم قال: ((إني لأرجو أن يكونوا الثلث)).
قال: فكبرنا.
ثم قال: ((إني لأرجو أن يكونوا الشطر)).
قال: فكبرنا.

قال: فتراجع المسلمون على هؤلاء السبعين، فقالوا: نراهم أناسًا ولدوا في الإسلام، ثم لم يزالوا يعملون به حتى ماتوا عليه.

وقوله: “الظراب”: الجبال الصغيرة.
وقوله: “يتهارشون”: أي يتقاتلون، وورد بلفظ “يتهاوشون”: أي يختلطون.

10282 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said:
We were talking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one night until the conversation became prolonged.
Then we returned to our homes.
When morning came, we went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Last night the prophets were shown to me along with the followers from their nations. A prophet came with three of his people, another prophet came with a group from his people, another prophet came with only a few of his people, and another prophet came with no one from his people. Then Mūsā ibn ʿImrān came before me with a great multitude from the Children of Israel. When I saw them, I was impressed, so I said: ‘My Lord, who are these?’ He said: ‘This is your brother Mūsā ibn ʿImrān.’ I said: ‘My Lord, where is my nation?’ He said: ‘Look to your right, toward the hills.’”
He said:
I looked, and the hills of Makkah were filled with people.
I said:
“My Lord, who are these?”
He said:
“They are your nation.”
He said:
“Then it was said to me: ‘Are you pleased?’
I replied: ‘My Lord, I am pleased. My Lord, I am pleased.’”
He said:
“Then I was told: ‘Among them are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise with no reckoning upon them.’”
Then ʿUkkāshah ibn Miḥṣan, from Banū Asad ibn Khuzaymah, stood up and said:
“O Prophet of Allah, supplicate to your Lord that He makes me one of them.”
He said:
“O Allah, make him one of them.”
Then another man stood and said:
“O Prophet of Allah, supplicate to your Lord that He makes me one of them.”
He replied:
“ʿUkkāshah has preceded you in that.”
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“May my father and mother be sacrificed for you. If you are able to be among those seventy thousand, then be among them. If you fall short of that, then be among the people of the hills. If you fall short of that, then be among the people of the horizon, for I saw there people fighting one another in great numbers.”
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“I truly hope that those who follow me from my nation will make up one quarter of the people of Paradise.”
He said:
We proclaimed Allāhu Akbar.
Then he said:
“I truly hope that they will make up one third.”
So we proclaimed Allāhu Akbar.
Then he said:
“I truly hope that they will make up one half.”
So we proclaimed Allāhu Akbar.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited:
“A multitude of the former peoples, and a multitude of the later peoples.”
 (Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah 56:39–40)
He said:
The Muslims then discussed those seventy thousand, saying:
“We think they are people who were born into Islam and continued practicing it until they died.”
Their discussion reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said:
“It is not like that. Rather, they are those who do not seek ruqyah, do not cauterize themselves, do not believe in evil omens, and upon their Lord they place their trust.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (3989), al-Bazzār (1440, 1441). It was authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (6431) and al-Ḥākim (4/577).
His statement, “a kabkabah from the Children of Israel,” means: a densely gathered multitude of people.
His statement, “al-ẓirāb,” means: small hills.
His statement, “yatahārashūn,” means: they were fighting one another. Another narration has “yatahāwashūn,” meaning: they were mixing together.

قال: ثم قال نبي الله ﷺ: ((فداكم أبي وأمي، إن استطعتم أن تكونوا من السبعين فكونوا، فإن عجزتم وقصرتم فكونوا من أهل الظراب، فإن عجزتم وقصرتم فكونوا من أهل الأفق، فإني رأيت ثم أناسًا يتهارشون كثيرًا)).
قال: فقال نبي الله ﷺ: ((إني لأرجو أن يكون من تبعني من أمتي ربع أهل الجنة)).
قال: فكبرنا.
ثم قال: ((إني لأرجو أن يكونوا الثلث)).
قال: فكبرنا.
ثم قال: ((إني لأرجو أن يكونوا الشطر)).
قال: فكبرنا.
فتلا نبي الله ﷺ: ﴿ثُلَّةٌ مِّنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ ۝ وَثُلَّةٌ مِّنَ الْآخِرِينَ﴾ [الواقعة: ٣٩–٤٠].
قال: فتراجع المسلمون على هؤلاء السبعين، فقالوا: نراهم أناسًا ولدوا في الإسلام، ثم لم يزالوا يعملون به حتى ماتوا عليه.
قال: فنمى حديثهم إلى نبي الله ﷺ، فقال ﷺ: ((ليس كذلك، ولكنهم الذين لا يسترقون، ولا يكتوون، ولا يتطيرون، وعلى ربهم يتوكلون)).
صحيح: رواه أحمد (٣٩٨٩)، والبزار (١٤٤٠، ١٤٤١)، وصححه ابن حبان (٦٤٣١)، والحاكم (٤/٥٧٧).
قوله: “كبكبة من بني إسرائيل”: والكبكبة: الجماعة المتضامة من الناس.
وقوله: “الظراب”: الجبال الصغيرة.
وقوله: “يتهارشون”: أي يتقاتلون، وورد بلفظ “يتهاوشون”: أي يختلطون.
10282 — ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd said:
We were talking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one night until the conversation became prolonged.
Then we returned to our homes.
When morning came, we went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Last night the prophets were shown to me along with the followers from their nations. A prophet came with three of his people, another prophet came with a group from his people, another prophet came with only a few of his people, and another prophet came with no one from his people. Then Mūsā ibn ʿImrān came before me with a great multitude from the Children of Israel. When I saw them, I was impressed, so I said: ‘My Lord, who are these?’ He said: ‘This is your brother Mūsā ibn ʿImrān.’ I said: ‘My Lord, where is my nation?’ He said: ‘Look to your right, toward the hills.’”
He said:
I looked, and the hills of Makkah were filled with people.
I said:
“My Lord, who are these?”
He said:
“They are your nation.”
He said:
“Then it was said to me: ‘Are you pleased?’
I replied: ‘My Lord, I am pleased. My Lord, I am pleased.’”
He said:
“Then I was told: ‘Among them are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise with no reckoning upon them.’”
Then ʿUkkāshah ibn Miḥṣan, from Banū Asad ibn Khuzaymah, stood up and said:
“O Prophet of Allah, supplicate to your Lord that He makes me one of them.”
He said:
“O Allah, make him one of them.”
Then another man stood and said:
“O Prophet of Allah, supplicate to your Lord that He makes me one of them.”
He replied:
“ʿUkkāshah has preceded you in that.”
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“May my father and mother be sacrificed for you. If you are able to be among those seventy thousand, then be among them. If you fall short of that, then be among the people of the hills. If you fall short of that, then be among the people of the horizon, for I saw there people fighting one another in great numbers.”
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“I truly hope that those who follow me from my nation will make up one quarter of the people of Paradise.”
He said:
We proclaimed Allāhu Akbar.
Then he said:
“I truly hope that they will make up one third.”
So we proclaimed Allāhu Akbar.
Then he said:
“I truly hope that they will make up one half.”
So we proclaimed Allāhu Akbar.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited:
“A multitude of the former peoples, and a multitude of the later peoples.”
 (Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah 56:39–40)
He said:
The Muslims then discussed those seventy thousand, saying:
“We think they are people who were born into Islam and continued practicing it until they died.”
Their discussion reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said:
“It is not like that. Rather, they are those who do not seek ruqyah, do not cauterize themselves, do not believe in evil omens, and upon their Lord they place their trust.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (3989), al-Bazzār (1440, 1441). It was authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (6431) and al-Ḥākim (4/577).
His statement, “a kabkabah from the Children of Israel,” means: a densely gathered multitude of people.
His statement, “al-ẓirāb,” means: small hills.
His statement, “yatahārashūn,” means: they were fighting one another. Another narration has “yatahāwashūn,” meaning: they were mixing together.

١٠٢٨٣ — عن أبي هريرة قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((يدخل الجنة من أمتي زمرة هي سبعون ألفًا، تضيء وجوههم إضاءة القمر)). فقام عكاشة بن محصن الأسدي، يرفع نمرة عليه، فقال: يا رسول الله، ادع الله أن يجعلني منهم. فقال: ((اللهم اجعله منهم)). ثم قام رجل من الأنصار فقال: يا رسول الله، ادع الله أن يجعلني منهم. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((سبقك بها عكاشة)).
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٥٨١١)، ومسلم (٢١٦/٣٦٩). ورواه مسلم أيضًا من وجه آخر وفيه: ((يدخلون الجنة من أمتي سبعون ألفًا بغير حساب)).

10283 — Abū Hurayrah said:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“A group of seventy thousand from my nation will enter Paradise, their faces shining with the brightness of the moon.”
Then ʿUkkāshah ibn Miḥṣan al-Asadī, wearing a striped cloak, stood up and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah that He makes me one of them.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“O Allah, make him one of them.”
Then a man from the Anṣār stood and said:
“O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah that He makes me one of them.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied:
“ʿUkkāshah has preceded you in that.”
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (5811) and Muslim (216/369).
Muslim also narrated it through another chain with the wording:
“Seventy thousand from my nation will enter Paradise without reckoning.”

10285 — Hānīʾ ibn Hānīʾ said:
ʿAmmār entered upon ʿAlī.
ʿAlī said:
“Welcome to the pure one who has been made pure.”
Then he said:
“I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
‘ʿAmmār has been filled with faith up to his very bones.’”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Mājah (147). It was authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (7076), and it was also narrated by al-Nasāʾī (5007).

١٠٢٨٧ — عن بلال بن يحيى العبسي قال: لما حضر حذيفة الموت، وإنما عاش بعد قتل عثمان أربعين ليلة، فقيل له: يا أبا عبد الله، إن هذا الرجل قد قُتل - يعني عثمان - فما ترى؟ قال: أما إذا أبيتم فأجلسوني، فأسندوه إلى صدر رجل، ثم قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((أبو اليقظان على الفطرة، لن يدعها حتى يموت أو ينسيه الهرم)).
حسن: رواه ابن سعد (٣/٢٦٢–٢٦٣)، والبزار (٢٩٤٥).

10287 — Bilāl ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿAbsī said:
When death approached Ḥudhayfah, and he lived only forty nights after the killing of ʿUthmān, it was said to him:
“O Abū ʿAbdullāh, this man has been killed”—meaning ʿUthmān—“so what do you think?”
He replied:
“If you insist, then seat me.”
So they supported him by leaning him against a man’s chest.
He then said:
“I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
‘Abū al-Yaqẓān (ʿAmmār) is upon the fiṭrah. He will never abandon it until he dies, unless old age causes him to forget.’”
Good: Narrated by Ibn Saʿd (3/262–263) and al-Bazzār (2945).

١٠٢٨٨ — عن عطاء بن يسار قال: جاء رجل فوقع في علي وفي عمار رضي الله عنهما عند عائشة، فقالت: أما علي فلست قائلة لك فيه شيئًا، وأما عمار فإني سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((لا يُخيَّر بين أمرين إلا اختار أرشدهما)).
صحيح: رواه الترمذي (٣٧٩٩)، وابن ماجه (١٤٨)، وأحمد (٢٤٨٢٠)، وصححه الحاكم (٣/٣٨٨).

10288 — ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār said:
A man came and spoke ill of ʿAlī and ʿAmmār in the presence of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with them).
She said:
“As for ʿAlī, I will not say anything to you concerning him. But as for ʿAmmār, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
‘Whenever he is given a choice between two matters, he chooses the one that is more rightly guided.’”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (3799), Ibn Mājah (148), Aḥmad (24820), and authenticated by al-Ḥākim (3/388).

١٠٢٨٩ — عن عكرمة أن ابن عباس قال له ولعلي بن عبد الله: ائتيا أبا سعيد فاسمعا من حديثه. فأتيناه وهو وأخوه في حائط لهما يسقيانه، فلما رآنا جاء فاحتبى وجلس، فقال: كنا ننقل لبن المسجد لبنةً لبنةً، وكان عمار ينقل لبنتين لبنتين، فمر به النبي ﷺ ومسح عن رأسه الغبار وقال: ((ويح عمار، تقتله الفئة الباغية، عمار يدعوهم إلى الله ويدعونه إلى النار)).
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٨١٢).

10289 — ʿIkrimah narrated that Ibn ʿAbbās said to him and to ʿAlī ibn ʿAbdullāh:
“Go to Abū Saʿīd and listen to his narrations.”
So we went to him while he and his brother were watering their orchard.
When he saw us, he came, wrapped his garment around himself, and sat down.
He said:
We used to carry the bricks for building the mosque, one brick at a time.
But ʿAmmār would carry two bricks at a time.
The Prophet ﷺ passed by him, wiped the dust from his head, and said:
“Woe to ʿAmmār! The rebellious group will kill him. ʿAmmār calls them to Allah, while they call him to the Fire.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (2812).

arabic_source:
١٠٢٩١ — عن أبي قتادة الأنصاري أن رسول الله ﷺ قال لعمار حين جعل يحفر الخندق، وجعل يمسح رأسه ويقول: ((بؤس ابن سمية، تقتلك فئة باغية)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٩١٥).
ومن أخباره ما رواه إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال: سمعت عمار بن ياسر بصفين في اليوم الذي قتل فيه وهو ينادي: أزلفت الجنة، وزوجت الحور العين، اليوم نلقى حبيبنا محمدًا ﷺ، عهد إلي أن آخر زادي من الدنيا ضيح من لبن.
رواه الحاكم (٣/٣٨٩)، ومن طريقه البيهقي في الدلائل (٢/٥٥٢).

10291 — Abū Qatādah al-Anṣārī narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿAmmār while he was digging the trench, as the Prophet ﷺ wiped the dust from his head:
“Alas for the son of Sumayyah! A rebellious group will kill you.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2915).
From His Reports
Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said:
I heard ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir at Ṣiffīn, on the day he was killed, calling out:
“Paradise has been brought near, and the ḥūr al-ʿayn have been given in marriage. Today we shall meet our beloved Muḥammad ﷺ. He told me that the last provision I would have from this world would be a drink of milk.”
Narrated by al-Ḥākim (3/389), and through him by al-Bayhaqī in Dalāʾil al-Nubuwwah (2/552).

١٠٢٩١ — عن أبي قتادة الأنصاري أن رسول الله ﷺ قال لعمار حين جعل يحفر الخندق، وجعل يمسح رأسه ويقول: ((بؤس ابن سمية، تقتلك فئة باغية)).
صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢٩١٥).
ومن أخباره ما رواه إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال: سمعت عمار بن ياسر بصفين في اليوم الذي قتل فيه وهو ينادي: أزلفت الجنة، وزوجت الحور العين، اليوم نلقى حبيبنا محمدًا ﷺ، عهد إلي أن آخر زادي من الدنيا ضيح من لبن.

١٠٢٩٢ — عن أبي هريرة قال: كان يقول: حدثوني عن رجل دخل الجنة لم يصل قط، فإن لم يعرفه الناس سألوه: من هو؟ فيقول: أصيرم بني عبد الأشهل عمرو بن ثابت بن وقش.
قال الحصين: فقلت لمحمود بن لبيد: كيف كان شأن الأصيرم؟ قال: كان يأبى الإسلام على قومه، فلما كان يوم أحد وخرج رسول اللّٰه ﷺ إلى أحد، بدا له الإسلام فأسلم، فأخذ سيفه فغدا حتى أتى القوم، فدخل في عرض الناس، فقاتل حتى أثبتته الجراحة.
قال: فبينما رجال بني عبد الأشهل يلتمسون قتلاهم في المعركة إذا هم به، فقالوا: إنه للأصيرم، وما جاء؟ لقد تركناه وإنه لمنكر لهذا الحديث، فاسألوه ما جاء به؟
قالوا: ما جاء بك يا عمرو، أحدبًا على قومك أو رغبة في الإسلام؟ قال: بل رغبة في الإسلام، آمنت بالله ورسوله وأسلمت، ثم أخذت سيفي فغدوت مع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقاتلت حتى أصابني ما أصابني.
قال: ثم لم يلبث أن مات في أيديهم، فذكروه لرسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال: ((إنه لمن أهل الجنة)).
حسن: رواه أحمد (٢٣٦٣٤).
قوله: “أحدبًا على قومك”: الحدب: العطف والحنو.

english_source:
10292 — Abū Hurayrah said:
He used to say:
“Tell me about a man who entered Paradise without ever having performed a single prayer.”
If the people did not know who he was, they would ask:
“Who was he?”
He would reply:
“The little warrior (al-Uṣayrim) of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal, ʿAmr ibn Thābit ibn Waqsh.”
Al-Ḥuṣayn said:
I asked Maḥmūd ibn Labīd:
“What was the story of al-Uṣayrim?”
He said:
He had refused to accept Islam while his people had accepted it.
When the Day of Uḥud came and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to Uḥud, Allah opened his heart to Islam, so he embraced Islam.
He took up his sword and went out until he reached the battlefield. He entered into the midst of the fighting and continued fighting until he was overwhelmed by his wounds.
He said:
While the men of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal were searching the battlefield for their slain, they came upon him.
They said:
“This is al-Uṣayrim! Why did he come? We left him while he was rejecting this matter. Ask him what brought him here.”
They asked:
“O ʿAmr, what brought you here? Was it out of loyalty and affection for your people, or out of a desire for Islam?”
He replied:
“Rather, it was out of a desire for Islam. I believed in Allah and His Messenger and accepted Islam. Then I took my sword and went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and fought until I was afflicted with what you see.”
He did not live much longer after that and died in their hands.
They mentioned his case to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:
“Indeed, he is among the people of Paradise.”
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (23634).
Explanation: His words, “Aḥadaban ʿalā qawmik (أحدبًا على قومك)”, mean: out of affection, compassion, and loyalty toward your people.

١٠٢٩٣ — عن جابر قال: قال رسولُ اللّٰه ﷺ: ((مَن سَيِّدُكُم يا بَني سَلَمَةَ؟)) قُلنا: جَدُّ بنُ قَيْسٍ، على أنَّا نُبَخِّلُه. قال: ((وأيُّ داءٍ أدوى مِنَ البُخلِ، بَلْ سَيِّدُكُم: عَمرو بنُ الجَمُوح)).
وكانَ عَمرو على أَصنامِهم في الجاهلية، وكانَ يُولِمُ لرسولِ اللّٰه ﷺ إذا تزوَّج.
حسن: رواه البخاري في الأدب المفرد (٢٩٦).

10293 — Jābir narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Who is the chief of Banū Salamah?”
We replied:
“Jadd ibn Qays, although we consider him to be miserly.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“And what disease is worse than miserliness? Rather, your chief is ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ.”
ʿAmr had been the custodian of his people’s idols during the pre-Islamic period, and he would prepare wedding feasts for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whenever he married.
Good: Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Adab al-Mufrad (296).

١٠٢٩٤ — عن عمرو بن حريث قال: صليت مع النبي ﷺ الفجر فقرأ: ﴿إِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ﴾، كأني أسمع صوته يقول: ﴿فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالْخُنَّسِ ۝ الْجَوَارِ الْكُنَّسِ﴾.
وقال: ذهب بي أمي أو أبي إليه، فدعا لي بالرزق.
صحيح: رواه أبو يعلى (١٤٦٩)، وأبو داود (٨١٧)، وابن ماجه (٨١٧).

10294 — ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth said:
I prayed the Fajr prayer with the Prophet ﷺ, and he recited:
“When the sun is wrapped up…” (Sūrat al-Takwīr 81:1).
It is as though I can still hear his voice reciting:
“So I swear by the retreating stars, those that run and disappear.” (Sūrat al-Takwīr 81:15–16).
He also said:
My mother or my father took me to him, and he supplicated to Allah to bless me with provision.
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Yaʿlā (1469), Abū Dāwūd (817), and Ibn Mājah (817).

١٠٢٩٥ — عن ابن شماسة المهري قال: حضرنا عمرو بن العاص وهو في سياقة الموت، فبكى طويلًا وحوَّل وجهه إلى الجدار، فجعل ابنه يقول: يا أبتاه، أما بشرك رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بكذا؟ أما بشرك رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بكذا؟ قال: فأقبل بوجهه فقال: إن أفضل ما نعد شهادة أن لا إله إلا اللّٰه وأن محمدًا رسول الله. إني قد كنت على أطباق ثلاث، لقد رأيتني وما أحد أشد بغضًا لرسول اللّٰه ﷺ مني، ولا أحب إليَّ أن أكون قد استمكنت منه فقتلته، فلو متُّ على تلك الحال لكنت من أهل النار. فلما جعل الله الإسلام في قلبي أتيت النبي ﷺ، فقلت: ابسط يمينك فلأبايعك، فبسط يمينه، قال: فقبضت يدي، قال: ((ما لك يا عمرو؟)). قلت: أردت أن أشترط. قال: ((تشترط بماذا؟)). قلت: أن يغفر لي. قال: ((أما علمت أن الإسلام يهدم ما كان قبله، وأن الهجرة تهدم ما كان قبلها، وأن الحج يهدم ما كان قبله؟)). وما كان أحد أحب إليَّ من رسول الله ﷺ، ولا أجلَّ في عيني منه، وما كنت أطيق أن أملأ عيني منه إجلالًا له، ولو سئلت أن أصفه ما أطقت؛ لأني لم أكن أملأ عيني منه، ولو مت على ذلك الحال لرجوت أن أكون من أهل الجنة. ثم ولينا أشياء ما أدري ما حالي فيها، فإذا أنا مت فلا تصحبني نائحة ولا نار، فإذا دفنتموني فشنوا علي التراب شنًّا، ثم أقيموا حول قبري قدر ما تنحر جزور ويقسم لحمها حتى أستأنس بكم، وأنظر ماذا أراجع به رسل ربي.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٢١).

10295 — Ibn Shimāsah al-Mahrī said:
We visited ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ while he was in the agony of death.
He wept for a long time and turned his face toward the wall.
His son kept saying:
“Father, did not the Messenger of Allah ﷺ give you glad tidings of such-and-such? Did he not give you glad tidings of such-and-such?”
ʿAmr then turned toward him and said:
“The greatest thing we possess is the testimony that there is no god except Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah.
I have passed through three stages in my life.
There was a time when no one hated the Messenger of Allah ﷺ more than I did, and nothing was dearer to me than being able to overpower and kill him. Had I died in that state, I would certainly have been among the people of the Fire.
Then Allah placed Islam in my heart, so I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, ‘Extend your right hand so that I may pledge allegiance to you.’ He extended his hand, but I withdrew mine.
He asked, ‘What is the matter, O ʿAmr?’
I said, ‘I wish to make a condition.’
He said, ‘What condition?’
I replied, ‘That I be forgiven.’
He said, ‘Do you not know that Islam wipes away everything that came before it, that Hijrah wipes away everything that came before it, and that Ḥajj wipes away everything that came before it?’
After that, no one was more beloved to me than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor was anyone greater in my eyes. Out of reverence for him, I could not look at him directly for long. If I were asked to describe him, I would not be able to do so, because I never looked at him fully. Had I died in that state, I would have hoped to be among the people of Paradise.
Then we assumed positions of authority, and I do not know what my condition before Allah will be because of them.
Therefore, when I die, let no professional mourner and no fire accompany my funeral. When you bury me, pour the earth over me gently, then remain around my grave for the time it takes to slaughter a camel and distribute its meat, so that I may find comfort in your presence while I consider how I will answer the messengers of my Lord.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (121).

١٠٢٩٦ — عن عمرو بن العاص قال: بعث إليَّ رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال: ((خذ عليك ثيابك وسلاحك، ثم ائتني)). فأتيته وهو يتوضأ، فصعَّد فيَّ النظر ثم طأطأه فقال: ((إني أريد أن أبعثك على جيش فيسلمك الله ويغنمك، وأرغب لك من المال رغبة صالحة)). قال: فقلت: يا رسول الله، ما أسلمت من أجل المال، ولكني أسلمت رغبة في الإسلام، وأن أكون مع رسول الله ﷺ. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ((يا عمرو، نعم المال الصالح للرجل الصالح)).
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٧٧٦٣)، والطبراني في الأوسط (٣٢١٣)، وصححه ابن حبان (٣٢١٠)، والحاكم (٢/٦٣٢).
وقوله: ((أرغب لك رغبة))، وفي بعض الروايات: ((أزعب لك زعبة)) بالزاي والعين، بمعنى الدفع، يقال: زعب له من ماله زعبة؛ أي دفع له دفعة، والزعب قطعة من المال.

10296 — ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for me and said:
“Put on your clothes and take your weapon, then come to me.”
I came to him while he was performing ablution.
He looked at me carefully, then lowered his gaze and said:
“I intend to appoint you over an army. May Allah keep you safe, grant you victory and spoils, and give you a generous share of wealth.”
I replied:
“O Messenger of Allah, I did not accept Islam for the sake of wealth. Rather, I accepted Islam out of love for Islam and so that I could be with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“O ʿAmr, how excellent is righteous wealth for a righteous man.”
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (17763), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ (3213), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (3210) and al-Ḥākim (2/632).
Explanation: His statement “Azʿaba laka zaʿbah” (in some narrations) means to give someone a portion or payment. Zaʿbah refers to a portion or amount of wealth given to a person.

١٠٢٩٨ — عن أبي نوفل بن أبي عقرب قال: جزع عمرو بن العاص عند الموت جزعًا شديدًا، فلما رأى ذلك ابنه عبد الله بن عمرو قال: يا أبا عبد الله، ما هذا الجزع وقد كان رسول الله ﷺ يدنيك ويستعملك؟ قال: أي بني، قد كان ذلك، وسأخبرك عن ذلك: إني والله ما أدري أحبًّا كان ذلك أم تألُّفًا يتألَّفني، ولكني أشهد على رجلين أنه قد فارق الدنيا وهو يحبهما: ابن سمية، وابن أم عبد. ثم وضع يده موضع الغل من ذقنه، وقال: اللهم أمرتنا فتركنا، ونهيتنا فركبنا، ولا يسعنا إلا مغفرتك. وكانت تلك هجِّيراه حتى مات.
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٧٧٨١).
وقوله: “هجِّيراه”: أي دأبه وشأنه.

10298 — Abū Nawfal ibn Abī ʿAqrab said:
ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ became intensely distressed when death approached him.
When his son, ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, saw this, he said:
“O Abū ʿAbdullāh, why are you so distressed when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to bring you close to himself and appoint you to positions of responsibility?”
ʿAmr replied:
“My son, that is true, and I will tell you about it. By Allah, I do not know whether that was because of love for me or in order to win my affection. However, I bear witness concerning two men that they departed this world while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ truly loved them: the son of Sumayyah (ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir) and the son of Umm ʿAbd (ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd).”
Then he placed his hand beneath his chin, as though restrained by shackles, and repeatedly supplicated:
“O Allah, You commanded us, but we neglected; You forbade us, but we committed those deeds. Nothing can encompass us except Your forgiveness.”
He continued repeating these words until he passed away.
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (17781).
Explanation: The expression “هجِّيراه” means: his constant habit, regular practice, or continual refrain.

١٠٢٩٩ — عن مطرف قال: قال لي عمران بن حصين: أحدثك حديثًا عسى الله أن ينفعك به: إن رسول الله ﷺ جمع بين حجة وعمرة، ثم لم ينه عنه حتى مات، ولم ينزل فيه قرآن يحرمه، وقد كان يسلَّم عليَّ حتى اكتويت، فتركت، ثم تركت الكي فعاد.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٢٢٦/١٦٧).
ورواه مسلم (١٢٢٦/١٦٨) من وجه آخر عن مطرف قال: بعث إلي عمران بن حصين في مرضه الذي توفي فيه، فقال: إني كنت محدثك بأحاديث، لعل الله أن ينفعك بها بعدي، فإن عشت فاكتم عني، وإن مت فحدث بها إن شئت: إنه قد سلِّم علي… الحديث.
ورواه الدارمي (١٨٥٤) من وجه آخر قال عمران بن حصين: إني محدثك بحديث: إنه كان يسلَّم علي، وإن ابن زياد أمرني فاكتويت فاحتبس عني حتى ذهب أثر المكاوي، أي الكي.
ويقال: كانت به بواسير، فكان يصبر على ألمها، وكانت الملائكة تسلم عليه، فاكتوى فانقطع سلامهم عليه، ثم ترك الكي فعاد سلامهم عليه. ذكره النووي.

10299 — Muṭarrif said:
ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn said to me:
“I will narrate to you a ḥadīth by which Allah may benefit you.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ combined Ḥajj and ʿUmrah, and he did not forbid doing so until he passed away. Nor was any verse of the Qur’an revealed prohibiting it.
The angels used to greet me with salām until I underwent cauterization. Then the greetings ceased. When I abandoned cauterization, the greetings returned.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1226/167).
Muslim also narrated through another chain that Muṭarrif said:
ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn sent for me during the illness in which he died and said:
“I am going to tell you some narrations. Perhaps Allah will benefit you through them after my death. If I recover, keep them to yourself; but if I die, then narrate them if you wish.”
He then mentioned that the angels used to greet him with salām.
Al-Dārimī also narrated through another chain that ʿImrān said:
“The angels used to greet me with salām. Then Ibn Ziyād instructed me to undergo cauterization, so I was cauterized, and the greetings ceased until the effects of the cauterization disappeared.”
It is also reported that ʿImrān suffered from hemorrhoids and patiently endured their pain. The angels used to greet him with salām. When he underwent cauterization, their greetings stopped; after he abandoned cauterization, they resumed. This explanation was mentioned by al-Nawawī.
It is also reported that his supplications were answered, and that he could see the guardian angels, who spoke with him. When he underwent cauterization, this ceased, but it returned after he abandoned it. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr mentioned that this occurred about two years before his death.
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb had appointed him to teach the people of Baṣrah the religion.
Ibn Sīrīn said:
“None of the Companions who settled in Baṣrah was given precedence over ʿImrān.”
He also said:
“The best of the Companions who settled in Baṣrah were ʿImrān and Abū Bakrah.”
Al-Ḥasan used to swear:
“No one better than ʿImrān ever came to the people of Baṣrah.”
He passed away in the year 52 AH, and it is also said 53 AH.
This was a distinction specific to him and should not be used as a general ruling. Therefore, a person afflicted with hemorrhoids is encouraged to seek treatment because of the general statement of the Prophet ﷺ:
“Seek treatment, O servants of Allah, for Allah has not sent down any disease except that He has sent down a cure for it.”
This ḥadīth has been recorded in the Book of Medicine.

١٠٣٠٠ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: بعث رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بُسَيْسَةَ عينًا ينظر ما صنعت عير أبي سفيان، فجاء وما في البيت أحد غيري وغير رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، قال: لا أدري ما استثنى بعض نسائه، قال: فحدَّثه الحديث، قال: فخرج رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فتكلم، فقال: ((إن لنا طلبة، فمن كان ظهره حاضرًا فليركب معنا)). فجعل رجال يستأذنونه في ظهرانهم في علو المدينة، فقال: ((لا، إلا من كان ظهره حاضرًا)). فانطلق رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وأصحابه حتى سبقوا المشركين إلى بدر، وجاء المشركون، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((لا يقدمن أحد منكم إلى شيء حتى أكون أنا دونه)). فدنا المشركون، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((قوموا إلى جنة عرضها السماوات والأرض)). قال: يقول عمير بن الحمام الأنصاري: يا رسول اللّٰه، جنة عرضها السماوات والأرض؟ قال: ((نعم)). قال: بخٍ بخٍ. فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((ما يحملك على قولك: بخٍ بخٍ؟)). قال: لا والله يا رسول اللّٰه، إلا رجاء أن أكون من أهلها. قال: ((فإنك من أهلها)).
فأخرج تمرات من قرنه، فجعل يأكل منهن، ثم قال: لئن أنا حييت حتى آكل تمراتي هذه، إنها لحياة طويلة. قال: فرمى بما كان معه من التمر، ثم قاتلهم حتى قتل.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٩٠١).
قوله: “طلبة”: أي شيئًا نطلبه. وقوله: “ظهره”: الظهر، أي الدواب التي تركب.

فأخرج تمرات من قرنه، فجعل يأكل منهن، ثم قال: لئن أنا حييت حتى آكل تمراتي هذه، إنها لحياة طويلة. قال: فرمى بما كان معه من التمر، ثم قاتلهم حتى قتل.
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٩٠١).
قوله: “طلبة”: أي شيئًا نطلبه. وقوله: “ظهره”: الظهر، أي الدواب التي تركب.
english_source:
10300 — Anas ibn Mālik said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Busaysah as a scout to find out what had happened to the caravan of Abū Sufyān.
He returned while no one was in the house except myself and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Anas said:
I do not know whether he excluded some of his wives.
The scout informed him of the news.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out and addressed the people, saying:
“We have an objective to pursue, so whoever has his riding mount ready should ride with us.”
Some men began asking his permission to go back for their riding animals, which were in the upper part of Madinah.
He replied:
“No, only those whose mounts are already present may come with us.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions set out until they reached Badr before the polytheists.
When the polytheists arrived, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Let none of you advance toward anything until I am there before him.”
As the enemy approached, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“Rise to a Paradise whose width is that of the heavens and the earth.”
ʿUmayr ibn al-Ḥumām al-Anṣārī said:
“O Messenger of Allah, a Paradise whose width is that of the heavens and the earth?”
He replied:
“Yes.”
ʿUmayr exclaimed:
“Bakhin! Bakhin!” (an expression of admiration and delight).
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked:
“What makes you say, ‘Bakhin! Bakhin!’?”
He replied:
“No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, except that I hope to be among its people.”
The Prophet ﷺ said:
“Indeed, you are among its people.”
ʿUmayr then took out some dates from his quiver and began eating them.
Then he said:
“If I were to live until I finish eating these dates, it would indeed be a long life.”
He threw away the dates he was holding, then fought until he was killed.
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1901).
Explanation: The word “ṭalabah (طلبة)” means something that we are pursuing or seeking. The word “ẓahr (ظهر)” refers to riding animals used for travel.

١٠٣٠١ — عن قرة بن إياس قال: أتيت رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فاستأذنته أن أدخل يدي في جربانه، وإنه ليدعو لي، فما منعه أن ألمسه إذ دعا لي. قال: فوجدت على نغض كتفه مثل السلعة.
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٥٥٨٢)، والطيالسي (١١٦٧)، والطبراني في الكبير (٢٥/١٩).
قوله: “الجربان”: جيب القميص. وقوله: “النغض”: أعلى الكتف، وقيل: عظم رقيق على طرفه.

10301 — Qurrah ibn Iyās said:
I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and sought his permission to place my hand inside the opening of his garment while he was supplicating for me.
Nothing prevented me from touching him while he was making duʿāʾ for me.
I found on the upper part of his shoulder something like a small raised swelling.
Authentic: Narrated by Aḥmad (15582), al-Ṭayālisī (1167), and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (25/19).
Explanation: “Al-Jirbān” refers to the opening or collar of a shirt. “Al-Naghḍ” refers to the upper part of the shoulder; it is also said to be the small bone at its tip.

١٠٣٠٣ — عن خليفة بن حصين أن جده قيسًا لما أسلم، أمره النبي ﷺ أن يغتسل بماء وسدر.
وقال النبي ﷺ لقيس: ((هذا سيد أهل الوبر)).
صحيح: رواه العجلي في الثقات (١٣٩٧)، ورواه أبو داود (٣٥٥)، والترمذي (٦٠٥)، والنسائي (١٨٨) مختصرًا.

10303 — Khalīfah ibn Ḥuṣayn narrated that his grandfather Qays accepted Islam, and the Prophet ﷺ instructed him:
“Perform a ritual bath using water mixed with lote-tree leaves (sidr).”
The Prophet ﷺ also said concerning Qays:
“This is the leader of the people of the desert (Ahl al-Wabar).”
Authentic: Narrated by al-ʿIjlī in al-Thiqāt (1397). It was also narrated by Abū Dāwūd (355), al-Tirmidhī (605), and al-Nasāʾī (188) in an abbreviated wording.

صحيح: رواه العجلي في الثقات (١٣٩٧)، ورواه أبو داود (٣٥٥)، والترمذي (٦٠٥)، والنسائي (١٨٨) مختصرًا.
10303 — Khalīfah ibn Ḥuṣayn narrated that his grandfather Qays accepted Islam, and the Prophet ﷺ instructed him:
“Perform a ritual bath using water mixed with lote-tree leaves (sidr).”
The Prophet ﷺ also said concerning Qays:
“This is the leader of the people of the desert (Ahl al-Wabar).”
Authentic: Narrated by al-ʿIjlī in al-Thiqāt (1397). It was also narrated by Abū Dāwūd (355), al-Tirmidhī (605), and al-Nasāʾī (188) in an abbreviated wording.

١٠٣٠٤ — عن كعب بن مالك قال: – في قصة تخلفه عن غزوة تبوك وتوبة الله عليه – قال رسول الله ﷺ وهو يبرق وجهه من السرور: ((أبشر بخير يوم مر عليك منذ ولدتك أمك)).
قال: قلت: أمن عندك يا رسول الله أم من عند الله؟ قال: ((لا، بل من عند الله)).
قال: وأنزل الله على رسوله ﷺ: ﴿لَقَد تَّابَ اللَّهُ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ وَالْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنصَارِ﴾ إلى قوله: ﴿وَكُونُوا مَعَ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾ [التوبة: ١١٧–١١٩].
قال: فوالله ما أنعم الله علي من نعمة قط بعد أن هداني للإسلام أعظم في نفسي من صدقي لرسول الله ﷺ، وأن لا أكون كذبته فأهلك كما هلك الذين كذبوا.
الحديث.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٤١٨)، ومسلم (٢٧٦٩/٥٣).

10304 — Kaʿb ibn Mālik said—in the account of his remaining behind from the expedition of Tabūk and Allah’s acceptance of his repentance:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me with his face shining with joy and said:
“Rejoice with the best day that has come to you since the day your mother gave birth to you.”
I asked:
“Is this glad tiding from you, O Messenger of Allah, or from Allah?”
He replied:
“No, rather it is from Allah.”
Then Allah revealed to His Messenger ﷺ:
“Allah has certainly turned in mercy to the Prophet, the Muhājirīn, and the Anṣār…”
until His statement:
“…and be with the truthful.”
 (Sūrat al-Tawbah 9:117–119).
Kaʿb said:
“By Allah, after Allah guided me to Islam, He never bestowed upon me a blessing greater in my sight than my being truthful with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and not lying to him, lest I perish as those who lied perished.”
The remainder of the narration follows.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (4418) and Muslim (2769/53).

١٠٣٠٥ — عن كعب بن عجرة، أن النبيَّ ﷺ فقد كعبًا فسأل عنه، فقالوا: مريض، فخرج يمشي حتى أتاه، فلما دخل عليه قال: ((أبشر يا كعب)). فقالت أمه: هنيئًا لك الجنة يا كعب. فقال: ((من هذه المتألية على الله؟)). قال: هي أمي يا رسول الله. فقال: ((وما يدريك يا أم كعب؟ لعل كعبًا قال ما لا يعنيه، أو منع ما لا يغنيه)).
حسن: رواه ابن أبي الدنيا في الصمت (١١٠)، والطبراني في الأوسط (٧١٥٧).
